values.title: Accept or pass on a ranked record
values.job: Turn a person's accept or pass on one suggestion in a review list into the request that keeps it as their stand, in their own words
values.description: Give the same descriptor and the one record, the id of the action the person took (the descriptor says which stance each action keeps: accept is agree, pass is disagree) and what the person said. Returns the request for the keep-where-you-stand tool, with the stand on the row's own view and answered_by person. Writes nothing; run the returned tool with the returned input only (the other fields are for you): skip it if unchanged is true (the stands you gave already say this) or if you have already run this idempotency_ref, since running it twice makes two versions of the stance record. A record the descriptor leaves out, an unknown or disabled action, or a copy rule that sets anything but why, by or at is refused with the reason.

values.title: Act on one of my notices
values.job: Perform one action explicitly offered by one of this person’s kept notices
values.description: Pass a notice id (told:<seq>) and the exact action id it offers; include text and a stable submission_id UUID for a reply. An explicit local open action returns done=true and its local path. Actions whose effect belongs to another source owner are refused unless that owner is available to this run; this tool never claims a post or agent action ran without its owner’s result.

values.title: Adapt my next training session
values.job: Adapt the next training session from the adjustments my progress rules gave for the session I just did
values.description: Takes a session prescription (or the plan and the id of the session) and the adjustments already worked out by the progress evaluator (its list may be empty). Applies them in order and answers `from` (the prescription as given), `next` (the adapted prescription) and `applied` (how many adjustments). An adjustment's doseScale multiplies every number in dose and its intensityScale every number in intensity (whole numbers stay whole, others round to two places); its note is kept at intensity.note; any other key is ignored and words in dose or intensity pass through. The input is never changed. This tool does not decide which rule fires: run the pick-fired-rules tool of the progress evaluator first and give its adjustments here.

values.title: Add a customer
values.job: Add a customer or contact to my customer list, with their name, how to reach them and where they came from
values.description: Keeps the customer in your own customer records and returns their record with its id, which record-a-customer-step and see-where-each-customer-is use. Give contact_id to change a customer you already added.

values.title: Add a private result to the pool
values.job: Keep one person's noisy yes or no about a shared situation in the pool everyone learns from, under their random contributor id
values.description: Runs in the account that holds the pool. Keeps one row of the pooled results list: { contributor, situation, worked, embedding, day }. The embedding is read from the shared situation's own row (list pooled-situations), never taken from the sender, so a result lands only on a situation that is shared and is linked to no shared text. contributor is the person's random id (64 lowercase hex), kept only in their own store; worked is the randomized bit tool:randomize-a-result gave. The row holds no account.

values.title: Add a shared situation to the pool
values.job: Keep one situation a person made safe to show strangers, with its meaning, so others can learn how similar decisions turned out
values.description: Runs in the account that holds the pool. Keeps one row of the pooled situations list: { entry, embedding, day }, under a new random id it answers. The entry is the rewrite the person's side already checked (tool:share-a-decision); the plain privacy pass runs on it again here with no private terms, and words that still carry an address, a handle, a long number, an amount of money, a key, the removed mark or a name inside a sentence are refused. embedding is the meaning of the entry's situation, at most 4096 numbers. The row holds no account and no contributor.

values.title: Add captions to a video from its transcript
values.job: Burn captions into a video from its transcript, in a caption style: plain subtitles, large captions, or words that light up as they are said
values.description: Takes timed words (the speech-to-text tool's output, or a list of {text, start, end}) and burns captions into the whole video in the style you name (see style), words gathered into short lines the way that style reads best. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Add to my workout log
values.job: Add new evidence to my workout log, or confirm, discard, correct, split or merge an entry already in it
values.description: Takes the workout log record, an operation and when it happened (observed_at; the tool holds no clock). `add` needs descriptor_id (how the evidence was captured, part of the atom id unless id is given), a subject with a kind, dimensions (each a number or text, or { value, unit, role, label }), and optionally source, links, confidence, evidence_refs and a raw_artifact. `confirm` and `discard` need target_atom_id and may carry a note. `correct`, `split` and `merge` need target_atom_id, dimensions holding the new values, optionally additional_target_atom_ids (for merge), subject and note. The entry is never edited: a new atom linking to it is added. Answers `log` (the next record to store: every other key of the record is kept as given), the `atom` added, the ids now in the review queue and the count of canonical entries. Adding the same atom id twice keeps one. The record is stored by the person's AI through the records door.

values.title: Add up revenue
values.job: Add up revenue, refunds, net revenue and active recurring revenue from a list of payments, by plan or any other group
values.description: Reads any payment provider's events: you say which field holds the amount, which holds the recurring amount, which event kinds add revenue and which subtract it (refunds), and optionally which field groups payments (a plan, an offer, a month). Returns gross, refunds, net and active recurring revenue in cents, totals by group and by role, and the payments that need a look (missing or negative amounts, duplicates, the same payment twice with different amounts).

values.title: Add a requested item to a work tree
values.job: Add a requested item to a work tree, keeping who asked for it and in which message, without adding it twice
values.description: Adds one item someone asked for to a work tree, under a branch or at the top, with the checks that will show it is done. Each item keeps where it was asked (a conversation and the message's number), so sending the same request again changes nothing, a later message can refine an existing item (attach_to) or correct it (correction: true), and the same message can never become two items. Returns the whole tree with the item in it, whether it changed, and the item as recorded.

values.title: Adopt a reviewed window of evidence into my library (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take a saved, reviewed set of intervals or evidence and adopt it into my library of records, refusing anything that does not match
values.description: Reads a saved adoption input the person gives (its schema member picks intervals or evidence-only) and adopts it into the library under the profile the library's schema declares, checking membership against the declared table first. Which tables, fields and rules apply comes from the schema.

values.title: Run a community's matchmaker clock: start or close a round, introduce, follow up
values.job: Pair a community's members on its cadence without anyone asking: start a round when it is due, close it at its deadline, make introductions everyone said yes to, and follow up the ones nobody acted on
values.description: The wake target of a community's matchmaker; a person declares it as their own wake (a wake-declaration record with tool tool:advance-a-community-matchmaker, a time repeat, and input { community_id }). Reads the community's settings (a match-community record, checked by tool:check-community-matching-settings), its members, rounds, matches and answers. When no round is open and the cadence (every_days after the last round) has come, it starts one: each opted-in member whose answers are incomplete gets a profile job for their own AI, and each complete member gets a bounded shortlist (an inverted index over categories and words, at most shortlist_size candidates, never every pair) and a score job asking their AI to score each candidate on the contract's factors with cited claims. Nothing here runs a model. At the deadline it forms groups from the grounded scores only (exact product of the factors, every factor cited), proposes each and hands each person's AI a consent job. It makes the one-to-one group of any match whose yeses all hold and hands topic jobs; it hands follow-up jobs at the community's follow_up_hours until the members talk. Jobs are ai-job records on the engine's job road, once per request key. Returns round (what started or closed, or null), next_at (when the clock next has something to do) and written; a community without usable settings returns ok false and its error.

values.title: Answer a decision's question
values.job: Answer the question my method is asking about a decision, with each of its checks
values.description: Answers the decision's current question (step_id) with answer as its answer_schema says: every field, every check handled (how) or, where allowed, not applying (because), each citing the decision's evidence refs or the person's current pursuit ids. verdicts are your judge's, beside the answer: a refusal that rests on the answer or an evidence ref and names words of its check refuses the answer. Out of turn is refused; the same answer again replays. Keeps the answer as its own step record and returns the next question.

values.title: Answer a community's matchmaker: profile, scores, yes or no, topics, wrote
values.job: Give a community's matchmaker what it asked for: a member's answers and on/off switch, an AI's cited scores for its shortlist, a person's yes or no to an introduction, first topics, or that they wrote in the one-to-one
values.description: One answer from one person (person), then the community's clock. kind profile: { on?, answers: { question_id: answer }, categories? }, refused when a question is not one the community asks or an answer holds the community's contact pattern. kind scores: { round_id, scores: [{ candidate_ref, factors: { factor: { score in (0, 1], reason, you: [claim_ref], them: [claim_ref] } } }] }; answers which candidates were grounded and why not, and the round closes once every asked AI answered. kind answer: { match_id, yes, consent }: a yes counts only when the run's task carries the community's person stamp (consent.yes_needs, a task fact the engine sets on a run the person started on their own page, which no input can set) and the consent the person was shown (read-my-community-matches gives it); an AI's yes is refused with the screen to open; a no, from the person or their AI, passes the match for everyone. Once every member's yes holds, the one-to-one group (group:introduction) is made and each AI is asked for first topics. kind topics: { match_id, topics: [line] }. kind wrote: { match_id }: once every member wrote, the match has talked. kind run-round: the community's owner closes the open round and starts the next. Returns outcome ({ ok: true, ... } or { ok: false, error, status, next_call?, changed?, consent? }), round, next_at and written.

values.title: Answer several typed questions about one thing in one request (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a model several questions about one piece of state at once and get one answer for each, in the type I asked for, or a refusal if any is missing or the wrong type
values.description: Give state (any JSON), questions ({<id>: {type: choice | score | noul, instructions, criteria?}}: choice answers with one of the names in criteria, or any text without criteria; score answers with a number; noul is yes or no answered as the likelihood of yes, 0 to 1), endpoint (a model server on your computer), model and timeout_seconds (no default). The state and the questions are written into the prompt and the answer schema names every question id, so the reply cannot use keys of its own. Returns answers keyed by question id. A server that answers with an error status, is unreachable or too slow, or sends a body that is not JSON, and a model reply that is not JSON, leaves a question out, or answers one in the wrong type, are each refused with a sentence saying which, rather than repaired. A noul answer is the likelihood of yes, a number from 0 to 1, checked as such (the old package accepted any text for it). This is an uncalibrated read of the state; for a decision, use tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict.

values.title: Put new titles into my video plans and the cards that name them (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the titles of my video plans to the ones in my titles list, and fix every card that points to an old title
values.description: Reads the person's titles list (one row per plan id, with its new title and any fields to copy) and applies it to every plan in a folder: the new title, the fields the request names, and every card segment whose text is an old title or a prefix the request names plus an old title. A title that is one of the request's placeholder words keeps the withdrawn title under its own field and leaves its cards as they are. A row may name the old title of a plan that is gone, so cards pointing at it are renamed too.

values.title: Approve a post
values.job: Approve a drafted post exactly as it was reviewed, so it may be set to go
values.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values of the post as it was reviewed); expected_values is required, and approval is refused when its words, file, destinations or time changed since. A post going nowhere yet is refused. approved_by names who approved it. Returns post and said.

values.title: Arrange videos side by side
values.job: Put two or more videos side by side, stacked, or in a grid in one frame, such as a swing next to a pro's
values.description: Plays the videos together in one frame: side by side (h), stacked (v) or a grid, with their sound mixed. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Ask a small model a question about some text, and trust it only if it got my known cases right (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a small model one question about some text (yes or no, which of a list, or how much on a scale) and get its answer with how sure it is, but only after that model got my already-answered cases right
values.description: Give rubric (your question, answer_shape {kind: true-or-false | one-of with options | score with levels, and for a score score_tolerance: how many levels away still counts as right}, calibration cases [{content, expect}] with at least two different answers, optional confidence_bands [{at_least, then}], accept_when_answer_in) or rubrics_file plus rubric_id, the content, and providers (the models you can ask: {via: locally-served, endpoint} for a model server on your computer, or {via: hosted-classifier, endpoint, model, key_file} for a hosted classifier whose key is in a file you name). A rubric with no cases, or whose cases all expect the same answer, is refused, and so is a model that gets a case wrong, so a yes-man never becomes your judge. Returns the answer, accepted (does your rubric accept it), confidence, the whole spread, the band your rubric drew for that confidence, who answered and the scoreboard of who was tried. Content longer than a provider row's accepts_characters is refused, never cut; a row that declares no limit is sent the whole content, so declare one for any model with a smaller reading window. remember_file keeps the calibration so later questions are one call; log_file (with excerpt_characters, how much text to keep) keeps each verdict with an excerpt so a wrong one can be turned into a known case with tool:tell-it-when-it-was-wrong.

values.title: Ask a web address, or give me the last answer it gave
values.job: Ask a web address for its answer and keep that answer; when the address cannot answer, give back the last answer it gave, so a feed or service that is down does not leave the person with nothing
values.description: Give address (a web address that starts with http:// or https://) and key (a short name for this answer: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, so the last answer can be found again); wait_seconds (1 to 120, default 20) is how long to wait for the address. The answer is JSON when the address says it is JSON and text otherwise, up to 256 KiB. When the address answers, the answer is kept in the person's own records under the key and returned with origin from-the-source. When it fails (an error status, no answer in time, an unreadable or too large body) or answers with nothing, the last answer kept under the key is returned with origin from-what-was-kept and when it was kept; an empty answer never replaces a good one. With nothing kept the origin is nothing-to-give and the answer is null. Failures are returned in words (source_failure, keep_failure, kept_failure), never raised: a failure to keep never costs the answer already in hand. The engine keeps this to public web addresses.

values.title: Cut my recordings into a video from a plan (runs on your computer)
values.job: Cut my recordings into a video following my plan: which stretch of which recording goes where, lines a voice reads over a held frame, my look on every shot, my graphics laid over it, and only show me the cut once every check I name passes
values.description: Reads a plan (segments in order, each a stretch of a recording from-to, a voiced line or a slide) and a piece table that says, per format, what each segment kind becomes. Cuts each recording frame-exact at the plan's own aspect, with edges that never catch the word before or after and a crossfade where two recordings meet; holds an open-eyed frame under each voiced line; plays a sound-only recording over a borrowed still with its words as captions; colours every shot with the person's look and shot-matches them to one another; places every sound at the exact start of its picture, with one loudness pass. The whole cut is one edit of the Workshop tool media-composition, rendered by its render-an-edit. Graphics are the person's own device templates, laid out clear of the face and drawn once over the whole cut by the overlay renderer the person names. The cut is made in a work folder and moved to the folder the person sees only when it is whole and every check row in the request passes; otherwise it stays in the work folder and the answer names what failed. A plan of slides becomes one picture per slide and a PDF. Steps: timeline (lengths only, nothing made), lay-out (the timeline, the overlay spec and the edit, nothing rendered for the person), build (one plan), run (every plan of a folder, each first through the person's plan checks). It runs on the person's own computer.

values.title: Assess Commons file reuse and prepare credit
values.job: Check one Commons file's exact original license fields, exclude unsupported rights and prepare required source attribution for any objective
values.description: Offline, file-specific check over the page object returned by Commons metadata lookup. Only an explicit Public Domain declaration with Copyrighted=false, Public Domain Mark 1.0, CC0 1.0, or matching canonical CC BY 1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0/4.0 metadata with title, author and source page can pass as eligible_for_selection. BY-SA, NC, ND, missing, conflicting or ambiguous metadata is refused. Output preserves original license/author/title/source and rights-warning values, identifies license class and version, and prepares a text credit with declared changes. It does not render metadata HTML. eligible_for_selection means the explicit license policy is met from source metadata; it is not exhaustive legal-rights verification or automatic permission. Inspect source warnings and intended-use rights independently.

values.title: Assign helpers to the people who need them, within each helper's capacity
values.job: Assign mentors, volunteers or helpers to the people who asked for help when each helper can only take so many, best pairs first, and say who was left without one and why
values.description: operation solve_capacity_constraints takes help_seekers [{ id, match_case_id?, demand? }], helper_candidates [{ id, capacity_ref?, session_ref?, mode? }], capacities (by helper id, or a list in helper id order), and your answers about pairs: eligibility [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, eligible, reason? }] and ranking [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, score, explanation? }]. The best-ranked eligible pairs are taken first; a helper is never booked past capacity and nobody is assigned to themself. operation solve_expected_value_capacity_constraints takes scored candidates (as for tool:form-matches) with expected_value, group_size, capacities and exclusive_participation, and needs a clear cut after each seeker's demand. propose_assignment turns a solved answer into proposals; record_outcome records outcome_fact_refs for one assignment_proposal. Returns assignments (state proposed), unmatched (with reason: capacity_exhausted, no_eligible_helper, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), capacity_usage and how much work was done. Rounds that swap who helps and who is helped are two requests.

values.title: Blur and silence everyone who has not agreed to be filmed
values.job: Make a copy of a video with every face blurred and every word silenced except those of the people who agreed to be filmed, before it is posted or shared
values.description: Give video, a video in the person's files, and agreed, pictures of each person who agreed to be filmed (a clear picture of their face; the person themself included). Every face in every frame is found; a face that matches someone who agreed stays as it is, and every other face, including one it cannot be sure of, is blurred past recognition. Give agreed_voices too, a recording of each of them speaking, and every word said by anyone else is silenced, judged half a second at a time; without it the sound is copied unchanged. The original video is never changed. The copy is kept in the person's files under Made by tools, named by name when given. Returns how many faces were seen, blurred and kept, how much speech was silenced, and any agreed picture in which no face was found. Faces are found with YuNet and recognized with SFace (OpenCV Zoo) and voices told apart with CAM++, on the tool's own computer; nothing leaves it.

values.title: Break down visits and sales by source
values.job: Break down visitors, leads and sales by where they came from (source, campaign or any tracked field), with conversion rates and revenue
values.description: Counts each visitor once by their first visit, then gives one row per source (or campaign, or any field the visits carry): visitors, each outcome you track (leads, purchases, sign-ups) with its rate, and revenue and revenue per visitor when conversions carry a value. can_break_down_by lists every field the visits allow; a conversion with no outcome counts toward the project's first one.

values.title: Brief a profile of how someone does their thing
values.job: Work out how a person or creator does their thing, such as their style or voice, from what they have made or said
values.description: Give the profile's name, the subject's name and the subject's own records (what they made or said). Returns what you need to derive the profile: the records, the rules for the answer and the shape of the answer. It asks no model; you derive the items, then give them to tool:keep-a-profile. An empty list of records is refused.

values.title: Brief a triage of one incoming item
values.job: Decide what to do with one incoming item, such as a message, note or finding, by weighing it against what the person cares most about
values.description: Give the item (a ref, an optional version, and what it says), the person's priorities, the dispositions an item can be settled as (each a ref and a label; exactly one is the fallback; blocked_default and needs_objective are optional), the least confidence an answer may have (0 to 1) and, if the person wants limits, the most words the rationale and the objective may have (max_words). Returns what you need to judge it: the item, the priorities, the dispositions, the rules for the answer (including fail closed to the fallback; where a disposition needs an objective, that it is the smallest safe, reversible assignment that produces evidence and may not authorize messages, spending, publishing, promises, credential changes, live changes, anything illegal, deceiving or harassing anyone, or taking what belongs to another party) and the shape of the answer. It asks no model; you judge, then give your answer to tool:settle-a-triage.

values.title: Bring back my similar decisions
values.job: When I am about to decide something, show what I decided in similar decisions before, what came next and how each turned out
values.description: Reads the person's own decision records. The newest ones are weighed by the words their goals share with the named decision's goal, plus a point for the same method (read-data/decide-with-a-method.json `similar`). The closest are kept, closest first, limit of them (10 when not given, never more than 50). Each comes back with its goal, its method, the option it chose, its next action, its status (from its own current evidence) and its observed and reported results. Only those few are read whole, and nothing leaves the person's account.

values.title: Build a markdown section from entries, word for word
values.job: Write one markdown section out of a list of entries (what people said or wrote), keeping every entry's words exactly as they came in
values.description: Give a heading and one or more sources, each a JSON document holding a list of entries. Every line of an entry's text is written behind a quote marker and nothing else about it is changed (blank lines, trailing spaces, headings and code fences inside an entry stay as they were), so the section is a record and not a paraphrase. Entries keep their order and are grouped by source. The names of the fields to read (the list, the text, a label, a time stamp, a group name) are inputs. A source with no list, an entry without its text field, and sources holding nothing are refused, because an empty section looks the same as one that found nothing. The result is ready for tool:place-a-section-in-a-markdown-document.

values.title: Prepare records for my lists with their sources and basis (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take records I keep in files and prepare everything to put them into my lists as records, each value with where it came from and how sure we are, in batches I can send
values.description: Reads the mapping and source files from the one folder the person granted this tool. A declared records source reads only its type and id prefix through this run's scoped records capability; its sender config and Keychain credential are not used. Maps each source by the person's rules, then returns counts, pending or diverted items and the records:write commands as result data. It writes no local file and sends no records. A row with no address, two rows with one id, a link to a row that does not exist, a value over the limit or a basis naming too many sources is refused by name. It knows no record kinds or lists: all of it comes from the mapping.

values.title: Call a treg endpoint
values.job: Call any endpoint in treg's catalog by its id, with its inputs, paid from the person's treg balance, never above a cost ceiling the caller names
values.description: Sends one call to treg for the endpoint id given, with the person's treg token from their treg connection (the token is placed as the request leaves and never shown), and answers the provider's reply as treg relays it (a routed treg.* endpoint answers {output, raw, _treg}). Send the method the catalog names (endpoint.method), its query fields in query and its body fields in body, exactly as tool:read-a-treg-endpoint-and-its-price lists them; a path field goes in query. max_cost_usd is sent as treg's X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: treg documents that a call it would bill above it is refused with HTTP 402 route_max_cost before anything is charged. This SPENDS the person's treg balance: read the endpoint's price first, say it to the person, and keep max_cost_usd at what they agreed to. A reply outside 2xx is an error that quotes treg: 402 is an empty balance or the ceiling, 503 provider_capacity_unavailable names other providers of the job; failed calls are not billed. The answer's headers (beside the reply, lower case) say what the call cost and how to follow it: x-treg-cost-micro is the charge in millionths of a US dollar (on an asynchronous submission, the amount held until the task finishes, not a charge; on a replay 0, with x-treg-original-cost-micro), x-treg-call-id is the call's id (keep it), x-treg-served-by the provider a routed call used, x-treg-cache a cached answer, and x-treg-async the descriptor of an asynchronous task. Tell the person the cost with each answer. An answer of 202 with _treg.outcome pending is a task still running: follow it with tool:read-a-treg-call and its call id, never by calling again. A team's own registered tool is called the same way, as <tool-name>/<path>.

values.title: Cancel a booking on my calendar
values.job: Remove a booking's event from my own calendar
values.description: Deletes one event from the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. An event already gone counts as cancelled. Answers changed, or error and why.

values.title: Cancel a Stripe subscription
values.job: Cancel a buyer Stripe subscription now, or at the end of what they have paid for
values.description: Give subscription_id, and at_period_end: true to keep the paid period running and stop the next renewal. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Cancel prepared resource usage report
values.job: Release only an unsent usage report; retain possible provider charges for reconciliation
values.description: Release only an unsent usage report; retain possible provider charges for reconciliation

values.title: Change a booking's status
values.job: Confirm, cancel, complete or mark a booking as a no-show, only in the ways a booking may move
values.description: Moves one booking record to a new status: waiting bookings can be confirmed or cancelled, a confirmed one can be completed, marked no-show or cancelled, and a finished one never moves. A cancel keeps its time and reason. Asking for the status it already has changes nothing. A move that is not allowed is refused with the moves that are.

values.title: Change fields of documents in my folder list
values.job: Change or remove fields of documents' frontmatter in a folder I granted, each only if the document is still the one I read
values.description: For each row { id, values: { note.<key>: value or null }, if_identity } rewrites only the frontmatter lines of the keys named: a value sets the key, null removes it, and other keys, comments and the body stay byte for byte. A value must fit the kind the folder's property-types.json gives the property; file facts cannot be written. When if_identity is given and the document changed since it was read, the change is refused and nothing is merged. The new bytes replace the document in one rename, and the answer is each changed document's new values and identity.

values.title: Change cells or words in a spreadsheet or document, keeping everything else (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the cells of a spreadsheet or the words of a Word document by rules, and write a new file that keeps every other part, style and chart as it was
values.description: Takes the file and a rules file (a JSON list). A rule is one of: kind cell (match by formula_contains, value_equals or text_contains, optionally on one sheet; set a formula, a formula_replace, a value or a text_replace), kind shared-string (match equals or contains; set text or replace), or kind document-text (match equals or contains; set text or replace). Cached values are written beside formulas so the next reader sees the intended value without a recalculation. Every part it does not change is copied byte for byte. The report gives how many places each rule changed; a rule that matched nothing is reported with a warning, never silently accepted. The input file is never changed; the new file is written to the output path.

values.title: Change my groups: add, move, order, nest and remove
values.job: Add things to my groups, lists or collections, move and reorder them, put some into a new group inside, take a group apart, or bring a whole folder tree in as groups
values.description: A group is any list of addresses (records, pages, people, other groups) in an order; a member whose address is a group nests that group. changes is a list applied in order as one change: ensure-group, add-member (nodeRef, memberId, role?, presentation?, placement?), remove-member (memberId), reorder-member (memberId, placement), move-member (memberId, toGroupRef, placement?), set-member-fields (memberId, role and presentation, null clears), patch-member-presentation (memberId, presentation merged into what is there), group-members (memberIds, toGroupRef: the new group, wrapperMemberId), ungroup-members (wrapperMemberId), delete-group. Every change names groupRef { family, parts }; a placement is { index }, { before: memberId }, { after: memberId } or { at: start | end }. Member ids are yours: nothing is invented. tree (optional) is { family, records: [{ node_id, parent_id, ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }] }: nodes with role group become groups and every node is placed in its parent by ordinal, its title and attributes kept as presentation. The groups touched are read first; a group can never end up inside itself, and a repeated member id is refused, so the whole change is refused and nothing is written. Only groups that changed are written; a group that is gone is removed. Returns groups (every group the change read or made, as it is now), written, removed (record ids) and unplaced (tree nodes not placed, with why).

values.title: Change speed over part of a video
values.job: Play part of a video in slow motion or sped up, such as the moment of contact at half speed, and optionally keep only a window around it
values.description: Plays the stretch from `from` to `to` (seconds) at `speed` (0.5 is half speed) with the sound, the rest at normal speed, keeping only `keep_from` to `keep_to` when given. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Check my app's bundle only uses what each package made public
values.job: Stop a build that takes a file from a package that did not declare it public: read the bundler's own list of what went into the finished bundle and report every import that reaches into a package's private files
values.description: Give metafile_file (the bundler's metafile, esbuild's shape, a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), packages_root (the folder whose sub-folders are packages), declaration (how a package declares its public files: file, the name of the declaration file in each package folder; entries_at, the dotted path to the list in it; kind_at and kind, where each entry says what it is and the value that means public source; path_at, where it names the file or folder) and optionally bundle_root (what the metafile's relative paths are relative to; the granted folder when absent). The tool has no default declaration. Each import from outside a package to a file the package did not declare, and each use of a package whose declaration file cannot be read, is a finding in words. Imports inside one package, to files no package owns, to external modules and to virtual modules are not judged. Returns ok, edges_checked, packages_reached and findings.

values.title: Check a buyer may open something
values.job: Decide whether a buyer may open one gated thing (a page, a lesson, a publication) from the access it requires
values.description: Takes the scope the thing is gated by ({ schema: "addressed-expiring-value-scope/v1", value_ref, instance_ref, required_access_refs }) and the buyer. A thing that requires no access is open to any named buyer; otherwise the buyer must hold any one of the required access refs now (tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works that out). Answers only authorized true or false: a scope that is not exactly that schema, no buyer, or access that cannot be worked out is false.

values.title: Check a destination is honest before it is published
values.job: Check a progress or results screen description before publishing it: it must not ship made-up numbers, ranks, bars or percents before the owner has worked them out
values.description: Give a destination descriptor and, if you want, refuse_keys: keys that may not appear anywhere in it. Returns honest (true when nothing is wrong) and every problem in words: a missing ref, subject_ref or statement, bars, stats, percents, ring labels, ranks, actors or fractions that are filled in instead of starting empty, and any refused key found.

values.title: Check a draft carries its profile
values.job: Check that a draft made for a person carries the references to the profile that shaped it and the profile it is checked by
values.description: Give the draft (a list of blocks, each an object), the names of the fields that must carry a profile reference, and optionally the profile's name. A field passes when some block of the draft holds a non-empty value in it, and, when you gave the profile's name, when one of those values is that name. Returns whether the draft fits and, for each field, whether it passed and why not. It judges references only, not the words.

values.title: Check a folder's files against rules I wrote
values.job: Check the source files of a project folder against rules the person wrote down, and say which files break which rule, where, and why the rule exists
values.description: Give rules: one row each, { kind: "source-file-rule", id, why, scope: { path_matches, path_excludes }, applies_when: { all | any | content_matches | content_absent }, subject: { named: "path" | "text" | "every_path" }, violation: { unit: { split }, forbidden, required, exempt }, message }. A pattern is a regular expression, or { pattern, flags }, or { collected: { pattern, capture } } to match any value found in the text being judged. forbidden and required mean AND across a list; exempt means OR. The rule is data: the checker knows no rule. Optional under (a sub-folder to judge) and recorded ({ known_findings: { <rule id>: ["path" or "path:line"] } }) to compare against a written baseline in both directions. Runs over the folder the person granted for reading, using git's listing when the folder is a repository and every file otherwise; it reads the files as they are on disk and refuses links and special files instead of following them. Returns passed, said, violations ({ rule_id, path, line, evidence }), report (findings grouped under each rule's why), rule_coverage, refused_paths, dangling_paths, files, ratchet. A run where no file met a rule is not a pass.

values.title: Check a page for search and answer engines
values.job: Read one public page the way a search or answer engine does, from the HTML it is served with and no script run, and say which checks it passes, which it misses and how to fix each
values.description: Fetches one public HTTP or HTTPS page, its host's robots.txt and, up to a set number, the pages it links to, and checks the served HTML against check rows: readable text without a script, one clear definition in the first words, a question as the first subheading, headings in order, named controls and labelled fields, structured data, a canonical address, published and updated dates, robots rules that let the answer-engine crawlers in, working links and more. A page that asks not to be indexed (a noindex robots tag) is not scored. It answers score (the share of scored checks that pass, among those that could be run), passed, failed, missing (each failed scored check with what it says, how to fix it and up to three examples), suggestions (failed checks that never change the score), and not_checked (checks that needed something that could not be read). The check rows ship with the tool and a caller may pass its own rows as checks, or name check ids to skip. It follows a small number of redirects, keeps at most 2 MB of a page and does not sign in.

values.title: Check a pipeline's stages for mistakes
values.job: Check a sales pipeline or any set of stages for mistakes: stages nothing can reach, a way out of a finished stage, or a move to a stage that does not exist
values.description: Give the stages, the moves allowed between them and the start stage. Returns sound (true when there is nothing wrong), each problem in words, and which stages are and are not reachable from the start.

values.title: Check a post
values.job: Say whether a post is ready for each place it is going, and what each place will refuse, before it is approved or set to go
values.description: Give post_id. Returns, for each destination, ready, problems (what that place will refuse, in plain words: words too long, a video or picture it needs, a kind or size of file it does not take, a setting it needs such as a video title) and not_checked (what could not be compared here, such as a video's length nobody gave, or whether the file is still in the person's files); and for the post, ready and said. Fix a problem with tool:draft-a-post. It changes nothing.

values.title: Check that a library of records is valid (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that my library of record files is consistent: every id a record names exists, ids are unique, counts match, tables use only their allowed values, and files derived from a source are not stale
values.description: Reads a library of JSON record files on the person's own computer through a schema file the person gives (it names the files, the relations that must hold between them, the tab-separated tables and their allowed values, the builders of files derived from other files, and the commands that say a derived file is stale). Runs every check the schema declares and prints one report: how many passed, which ones broke and exactly which ids or values break them, the table cells outside their allowed values and which derived files are stale. It changes nothing. It knows no record kinds: every file, id field and check comes from the schema.

values.title: Check my port or replica keeps its promises to its reference
values.job: Check a contract for work taken from a reference (a source ported, a behaviour ported, a visual replica, an inspiration, an anti-reference): the source and its identity, what must be preserved, and the proof (retained source lines, required mechanisms, measured pictures and pixel difference)
values.description: Give contract (the contract itself) or contract_file (a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), stage (pre-edit before the work starts, completion, the default, when it is done) and optionally target (a path the contract must own). A contract names schema (reference-adaptation-contract/reference-grounded-adaptation), id (REF-...), status, mode (SOURCE_FIRST_PORT, BEHAVIORAL_PORT, VISUAL_REPLICA, INSPIRATION_ONLY or ANTI_REFERENCE), directive, sources, targets, preserve, allowed_deltas, banned_substitutions, baseline and proof; every identity is the BLAKE3 identity 1f:<64 hex> of the exact bytes. Paths are read relative to the granted folder. Source drift, a copy directive relabelled inspiration, a missing target, retained-line and mechanism proof, and for a visual replica the measured geometry, the picture identities and an independently measured pixel difference at or under three percent are all checked. Returns valid, errors (each in words), id, mode, status and measurements.

values.title: Check a rendered video's frames, joins and audio (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check my finished video for mistakes a viewer would notice: a stray frame at a cut, a cut inside a word, graphics off the frame or over a face, text too small, sound effects too quiet or harsh
values.description: Reads a rendered video (and, for the checks that need it, a JSON spec of its cuts, held frames and the graphics laid over it, plus the overlay render with alpha) and runs checks on its frames, joins and audio: in-frame, joins, word-clip, jitter, text, face, exits, dwell, type-sync, backing, movement, sound-balance, sound-harsh, sound-loops, sound-sync, settle, tempo, zoom, camera, motion-blur, internal-text, text-size, info-added, math-shown, cue, broll, placement and filler-words-cut. Which checks run and every number and word list they use are the person's own limits, a JSON file the person gives (their AI reads the rows from the person's own records); the tool has no defaults, and a check with no limits row says so instead of passing. Each check prints PASS, WARN or FAIL with the seconds it happens at; a check that cannot run says why. It runs on the person's own computer, never on a server, and changes nothing it reads.

values.title: Check a move to another stage
values.job: See which stage a deal, order or applicant is in, which stages it can move to next, and whether it may move to the stage you want
values.description: Give the stages (a pipeline, deal stages, order states), the moves allowed between them, the start stage and the record's moves so far. Returns where the record is now, every next stage with why it is or is not open, and, when you name a stage in to, whether it may move there and the move to keep with the record. A finished stage never has a way out, and a move naming a stage that is not declared is refused.

values.title: Check a Stripe event
values.job: Check a Stripe webhook before believing it (its age and its signature), and read it as a payment event to keep
values.description: Give the raw payload exactly as received and the Stripe-Signature header as signature_header. The signature is checked with your webhook signing secret from your held values. Returns the payment event, or why it was not believed. Nothing unchecked is kept.

values.title: Check that my video moves as much as the one I copied (runs on your computer)
values.job: Tell me whether the video I made is as lively as the video I am copying, or holds still too long
values.description: Measures how much a reference video moves (the share of frames where the picture changes, and its longest still hold), sets the person's bar from the whole reference, then measures the piece from its start to the second its end card begins, at the same still threshold, and says whether it passed each row of the bar. The bar is not built in: the person passes a record of kind motion-bar, whose rows each name a measure, a relation (at_least or at_most) and either a multiple of the reference's own value or a fixed value. The bar always comes from the whole reference, so trimming a piece never moves it. Moving-pixel share is a measure of conformance to the reference, not of readability or quality. The measuring is done by this tool with ffmpeg and ffprobe, which it calls as declared programs; it reaches into no other app.

values.title: Check words or anything made against a person's own rules and verdicts
values.job: Check words, a title, a script line or a plan against a person's own rules and the verdicts they already gave, and say pass, fail or uncertain for each, with why
values.description: Give the units to check (each { text, kind } or { view, kind } for JSON such as a plan, with optional facts, field, context and findings you already have), rules (rule rows judge-words runs, and ask rows a model answers), and the person's own rule document (verdict_rules) and stands (stances, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives them), read at run time from their records or files. Their exact stand on a thing decides first: disagree fails, partly holds at review and fails at final, agree passes and clears the generic rules they named. Then their stated rows fail and their inferred rows (at_most uncertain) only hold. Nothing passes on silence: a thing nothing of theirs judges is novel, and an ask row never passes without a calibrated answer. The answer lists the questions a model may answer, by id; send the answers back in answers to use them. Nothing about any person is built in.

values.title: Check my challenge definitions
values.job: Check my time-boxed challenge definitions are complete before I enroll anyone in them
values.description: Takes a list of challenge definitions and checks each one: its kind, id and label, the window it runs (a unit and a positive length, any unit), the reference to the rule that scores who fits, the reference to the content it walks through, the lowest score that joins, and an optional objective reference. Answers one result per definition: its id, whether it is valid and every problem found. It does not follow the references; the records they name are checked by their own owners. A window is an overlay on engagement, never a reason to take content away.

values.title: Check claims cite sources that were read
values.job: Check that each claim in an answer cites a source that was really read, and none cites one that was not
values.description: Takes the claims of an answer (each with citations naming a source id) and the ids of the sources that were really retrieved. A claim is grounded when at least one of its citations names a retrieved source. A claim with no citation is not grounded, and a citation to a source that was not retrieved is a fabricated reference that fails the whole answer. The answer is grounded when the share of grounded claims reaches min_grounded_ratio (1 when left out) and nothing was fabricated. An empty answer is never grounded.

values.title: Check a community's matchmaker settings before keeping them
values.job: Check that a community's matching settings can run: cadence, sizes, the evidence contract and the questions that cover every factor's citations, consent, follow-up hours, words for every job, refusal and state, contact pattern, limits and experiments
values.description: community is the value of a match-community record: { title, owner, created_at, matching }. Returns usable and problems, each a plain sentence naming the field to fix. matching holds every_days, round_hours, shortlist_size, posting_cap, group_size, cadence_label, default_on, contract (the match-evidence contract: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions, citation_requirements, authority, forbidden_interventions), questions (the contract questions this community asks, which must cover every claim kind a factor cites), expected_value? (minimum_expected_value, minimum_distinguishable_delta), initiative { required_level, pre_authorized_levels }, grouping?, consent { answer_hours, selection { approved_values, veto_values }, yes_needs { field, equals }, screen }, follow_up_hours, jobs (profile, score, consent, topics, follow_up: { said, job } with {name} fields), words, state_words, contact_pattern, limits, discover { offers, seeks } and experiments? ([{ id, arms: [{ id, weight, jobs }] }]). Nothing is written.

values.title: Check copy before a person reads it
values.job: Check text, Markdown, pages, JSON, decks and picture readings against the rules you send, and the whole set against your required lines, audience, offers and counts, and say pass, fail, held or uncertain for each unit
values.description: Give words as text, texts, Markdown, value (any JSON; fields names which keys hold words, or "strings" for every string), units, sources (JSON with its place), html (pages), decks (a rendered deck's HTML) or pictures with their readings. Markdown reads headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells and fenced display text; unresolved quotes, preamble before a declared document title and unsupported blocks stay coverage problems. It retains each block's role and field; for findings whose context is not established, name the matching rule ids or grammar check names for review, which keeps those findings uncertain and leaves other findings in force. Give rules (one row each: words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check) or leave them out to use mechanical grammar rows. Optionally give required (locked lines, features, baseline ids, approvals with the person's own words and the text they sit in), audience, offers and counts, and the person's verdict_rules and stands. Nothing about any person is kept here; their rules are input. A source with no words, a required line gone, a row for the wrong audience, a count that is not a published list view, an offer listing fewer lines than the others and a picture with no reading are problems, never passes. Model questions come back as questions; send answers on a second run.

values.title: Check a value has enough support
values.job: Check that a value has enough independent support before my AI acts on it
values.description: Takes named checks (each passed or not, some required) and how many of the optional ones must agree. Permitted only when every required check passed and enough optional checks passed. No checks at all is not permitted. Answers permitted, which required checks failed, which optional checks agreed and the reason in words.

values.title: Check the places I let my AI write in keep a history
values.job: Check that every place declared writable (on the promise that something keeps what is written there, such as a version history) really keeps it, and say which keep nothing
values.description: Give the declaration (the JSON that lists the places, or declaration_file, a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), places_key (the key that holds the list, found at any depth), id_key (the key naming each place), bases (folders inside the granted folder a place may live under; "" is the folder itself) and retention_kinds ([{ kind, marker }]: a kind keeps what is written when its marker, a file or folder name such as a history folder, is present at the place or any ancestor up to the granted folder). exemptions ([{ place, why }]) names places that keep nothing on purpose; they are still examined and shown with their reason. A declared place with no folder here is unresolved, never a finding. Reading zero places is refused, never a pass. Returns passed, places_declared, examined_count, keeps_nothing_count and each place with what keeps it.

values.title: Check my documents have not fallen behind their source
values.job: Check that documents which each claim to reflect one source (summaries, translations, copies for other readers) still carry the source's newest numbered item, and the markers each must hold, and say which have fallen behind
values.description: Give sets: one record per source, { set_id, source, unit_pattern, required_markers?, mirrors: [{ document, required_markers? }] }, every document a path inside the folder the person granted for reading. unit_pattern is a regular expression for the identifier the source and its mirrors share (its first capture, when it has one, is read as a number, so item 99 sorts below item 218). A mirror is behind when it lacks the source's newest unit; being shorter than its source is not a finding. required_markers are literal strings a document must carry (a set's apply to every mirror, a mirror's own replace them). A document that does not exist is reported as missing, not as stale. Returns agrees and, for each set, newest_unit, the mirrors behind with what each lacks, the markers missing and the documents missing. A run over no set is refused.

values.title: Check answers to a form
values.job: Check a person's answers to a form's questions and say which are missing or not valid, and why
values.description: Checks each answer against its question: a required question left empty, a number outside its range, text too short, too long or not in the right format (an email, a phone number), or a rating off its scale. Question types (text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) are rows with their own rules, and each question can lay its own rules over them. Returns every question's verdict and message, whether all answers are valid, and the first one to fix.

values.title: Check whether a tour step may move on by itself
values.job: Decide whether a guided-tour step has met its advance condition: tapped next, touched the highlighted thing, answered, watched enough of a video, waited long enough, finished an embedded form, or a fact someone looked up has the right value
values.description: Give the step's advance condition ({ op, args }) and what is known now (signals: next_tapped, target_interacted, answer, media_ratio from 0 to 1, elapsed_ms, surface_completion_refs, owner_readbacks keyed by the fact's ref). Ops: tap-next, target-interacted, answer-given, media-watched (args.min_ratio, default 1), timeout (args.ms), surface-completed (args.completion_ref), owner-readback (args.readback_ref, answer_fact_ref or objective_answer_ref, with required_values_present, required_nonempty, required_answer_values, accepted_states or required_states), and all-of / any-of over a list in args.of, nested as deep as written (an empty all-of is false). Every threshold is in the condition. An op that is not defined answers false, so a typo never pushes a person on; they can still move on by hand.

values.title: Check live orders with the broker
values.job: Check my live orders with my broker: which are filled, at what price, and which never got there
values.description: Give routes (the same routes the orders were placed with, each with status_request and open_statuses). Every live order still open (sending, unknown, or a status in the route's open_statuses) is asked about at the broker, and its record takes the broker's real status and fill; order_ids checks those orders whatever their status. An order the broker never named and does not know is marked not-placed and its day's spend is given back. Each answer is kept as a trade-order-event. The held live-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Check that a match rests on what people actually said
values.job: Turn people's intake answers into scoped profiles and check that a proposed match's scores cite what both people actually said before anyone is matched
values.description: Everything about the intake is the contract you give: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions [{ question_id, claim_kinds, primitive_ids, scope_field? }], citation_requirements per factor [{ side: subject | candidate, any_of: [claim kinds] }], authority [{ name, claim_kind, list? }] and forbidden_interventions (the authority entry whose values block a proposal). operation build-profile takes participant_ref, answer_facts [{ question_id, answer_fact_ref, value, evidence_refs? }] and connected_source_facts (each must carry its consent, access lease, field scope, observation and expiry times and whether it can be revoked, or it is not evidence) and returns the profile: claims, the scope, coverage per primitive, authority, status grounded or partial, and problems. operation check-assessment takes subject_profile, candidate_profile, assessments (per factor: score in (0, 1], rationale, inference_ref, the claim refs it cites on each side and evidence_refs) and proposed_interventions, and returns per-factor evidence with status grounded or no_justified_match and the reasons; a proposal either person forbids blocks every factor. Nothing here scores: scores come from whoever assessed, and only cited ones pass.

values.title: Check paper orders with the broker
values.job: Check my paper orders with my broker: which are filled, at what price, and which never got there
values.description: Give routes (the same routes the orders were placed with, each with status_request and open_statuses). Every paper order still open (sending, unknown, or a status in the route's open_statuses) is asked about at the broker, and its record takes the broker's real status and fill; order_ids checks those orders whatever their status. An order the broker never named and does not know is marked not-placed and its day's spend is given back. Each answer is kept as a trade-order-event. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Check a pick prompt or result for wording the person does not want
values.job: Check the words of a free pick prompt, its choices or a result summary against the wording the person does not want used (for example talk of money) before they are written
values.description: Give the texts to check, each as { field, text }, and banned_terms: the person's own list of words and phrases. Nothing is shipped as a default list. A term is found anywhere in a text in any letter case (so a short term also matches inside a longer word); a phrase written with spaces matches any run of white space. Returns passed and, for each hit, the field, the term and a message. An empty list passes everything. Refuses texts or terms written wrongly.

values.title: Check the proof behind finished work
values.job: Check whether the proof given for a finished task is something someone else could go and check, or just a claim
values.description: Reads the proof recorded for one finished item and answers CHECKABLE when it names something a second person could look at (a command and its result, a count, a file, a measurement, a screen to open, a wall that was hit) or VAGUE when it asserts, restates the task, or describes a feeling or an intention, followed by one sentence saying why. It judges only whether the record can be trusted, not whether the work is good.

values.title: Check the Facebook Page connection
values.job: Check that the person's Facebook connection still reaches its account, before a post is set to go there
values.description: Asks Facebook which account the person's facebook-messenger connection signs in as, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown). Returns the Page's id and name. A refusal (an expired or revoked sign-in) means the person connects Facebook again. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

values.title: Check the Instagram connection
values.job: Check that the person's Instagram connection still reaches its account, before a post is set to go there
values.description: Asks Instagram which account the person's instagram connection signs in as, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown). Returns the account's user_id and username. A refusal (an expired or revoked sign-in) means the person connects Instagram again. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

values.title: Check what a buyer paid
values.job: Check that the money a buyer actually paid is a price my offer declares, before giving them what they bought
values.description: Give offer_id and paid ({ amountCents, currency }), and optionally quoted (the amount, currency, cadence and priceOptionId that were quoted). A per-unit price is accepted only for an amount some whole unit count produces.

values.title: Check when I am busy
values.job: Read when my own calendar shows me busy between two times
values.description: Asks the person's own Google calendar when it is busy between two instants, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account). Answers the busy intervals, or unknown with the reason when the calendar cannot be read: unknown is never an empty free answer, so offer no times it guessed. Changes nothing.

values.title: Check that a rewrite kept the template's words (runs on your computer)
values.job: Tell me which words of the original a rewrite deleted, replaced or added, and whether the slots were filled from real sources
values.description: Judges any script (markdown with fenced dim blocks, a table column, or plain text) or any piece JSON (a fill, a measured render, another template) against a template, dimension by dimension: words by difflib on normalised words, categories by sequence alignment, numbers within a limit, timed events within a tolerance, boxes, colours and vectors by distance. Reports every fixed word deleted, replaced or inserted, every slot run as sourced, empty, unsourced, removed or still holding the original's value, the share of fixed words preserved, the worst lines and an annotated line view. A change listed with a reason in an exceptions file counts as preserved and stays visible. With --check it exits 1 unless every judged dimension meets its threshold, nothing unexcused was inserted and every slot fill has a source.

values.title: Check writing against its recipe
values.job: Check something written from a recipe before it goes anywhere: it cites only the sources given, it keeps the recipe's rules and reviews, and it is shaped for the next tool
values.description: Give recipe_id or recipe (as tool:compose-a-writing-instruction took), writing (the JSON object you wrote in the recipe output shape), grounding, work_item, context and review. For ordinary recipes, review is { accepted, verdicts: [{ id, accepted }] }. For an opt-in gate_policy.evidence_contract of source-backed-claims/v1, also give evidence_packet with exact source editions, claims, scopes and UTF-8 quote spans; writing must include exact draft_text and matching claim refs/version/text/scope/source_refs. Semantic review then binds each required verdict to the exact draft, claim version and scope, and source edition set. Reviewer attribution is caller-supplied and is reported unverified; it is not authenticated. Rights metadata is preserved but does not authorize publication. Checks stop at first refusal, then build one delivery request for the named owner tool. A refusal has no delivery.

values.title: Check writing from a file
values.job: Check a source backed writing request from a file the person granted to be read, without sending the source bytes in the tool call
values.description: Give file (a relative path in the folder you granted the tool to read), and optionally recipe_id or recipe to override the request's recipe. The file is bounded to 8 MiB and must be a regular JSON file inside the granted folder. It uses the same writing gate as tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe and returns only that gate result; the file contents are not returned.

values.title: Choose which options go ahead together
values.job: Choose which of several options (a person, a workflow, a tool, a place) go ahead now: every worthwhile one that does not compete for the same thing, the best where they do
values.description: configurations [{ id, configuration_kind (any word), expected_value, scope: { <field>: text }, required_resource_refs?, collision_refs? }] and scope_fields (the scope every configuration must name). Every configuration with a positive value and a complete scope goes ahead at the same time; two compete only when they share a collision ref, and then the higher value wins. Two that share a collision ref and are within minimum_distinguishable_delta of each other are both held back rather than picked between. Returns selected, rejected (with reason: non_positive_expected_value, scope_missing, resource_collision, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), configuration_requests (state proposed) and counts.

values.title: Choose how I am notified
values.job: Keep one of a notification setting's options as this person's choice
values.description: setting is the setting's name and choice one option id from tool:my-notification-choice. A choice that is not one of the options is refused with the options named. A setting that is not described, or describes no options, has nothing to choose from: it returns changed false and says so in said, and keeps nothing. Returns { setting, choice, previous, changed, said }; choosing what is already chosen changes nothing.

values.title: Choose what one visitor sees
values.job: Pick which version of a page, offer, headline or feature one visitor gets, from rules you write as data, keeping the same visitor on the same version
values.description: Scores every candidate version with a decider (a rule written as structured data: a split by visitor, a switch on what is known about the visitor, a preference for the version with the best recorded result) and returns the winner, the full ranking and any findings. The same visitor key always lands on the same version. One candidate is a feature flag, two or more is an A/B test, a decider that reads recorded results is a bandit. A candidate set or decider that does not validate is refused with every problem listed.

values.title: Keep principles from captioned videos, each backed by a quote checked word for word (runs on your computer)
values.job: Collect the principles that creators and teachers state or show in their videos, with the exact words and the second they say them, prove every quote is really in the captions, and rank each principle by how many independent channels back it and how well their videos did
values.description: Works on a folder of YouTube caption files (<id>.en.json3) with their <id>.info.json. corpus: one line per captioned video with its channel, title, views, kind (short or video), the captions as timed lines, and how many times its channel's usual views the video got (the usual is the median from a views table the person gives, or from the folder itself). candidates: the best 40-second windows of each video for what the person wants principles about, scored by their topic words, advice-giving phrases, a matching title and how well the video did, per channel, plus the first 45 seconds of each channel's best videos. find and verify: the second a quote is said at, and a check that every quote in the person's rows is an exact substring of its video's captions (ignoring case, white space and curly apostrophes), telling a wrong quote from a missing caption file and a quote at the wrong second. registry: merges the person's working rows (their own groups, lane names and stage names, passed in as files) into one registry of principles ranked by evidence strength (for each independent channel the best of log2(1 + the video's times-the-usual, capped at 64), halved when the quote only demonstrates the principle), with sources linked to the second, demonstrations, and contradictions linked both ways. extract: reads every part of every video with a chat model the person names (Ollama, MLX, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server, given as {url, model}), asking for the rows their own asks file describes, from any domain; each row's quote is put back onto the exact caption words and the seconds they start and end, rows whose quote is not in the captions are set aside with the reason, and a stopped run continues from the next unfinished video. coverage: videos, shorts and words per platform and channel, and how many videos the person's rows already cite. Word-timed transcripts from other sites are read too. What the principles are about, how advice sounds, what rows a model is asked for, and how rows group and are named for stages come only from the person's files; the tool holds none. Only extract sends words anywhere, to the model the person names; with a local model nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

values.title: Give a record the label of the first rule it meets
values.job: Give a record the label of the first of my rules that holds: each rule has clauses over facts read from the record (is present, is absent, at least, at most, equals), and I get the rule's key, label, tone and severity, or none
values.description: Takes a record, the facts to read from it (a key, a path, and how to read it: present, as a number, as an age in seconds up to now_ms, or as it is) and rules in order (a key, a label, an optional tone and severity, and clauses over facts). Answers the first rule whose clauses all hold, with its key, label, tone and severity exactly as given (null where none was given), or no result when none holds. A request that is unfinished (a rule with no key, label or clause, a clause naming a fact that was not declared, an operator that is not listed, an age fact with no now_ms) is refused with a sentence. The tool names no label, tone or threshold; the clock is now_ms, never read.

values.title: Re-voice the spans that are still bad, in the speaker's own voice (runs on your computer)
values.job: Where the speech in a recording is still unusable after cleaning, say the same words again in the speaker's own voice, with the same timing
values.description: Takes the output folder of tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio and the same spans file, and for each span still graded clone: checks that the span's speaker is the voice of the reference recording (wespeaker embeddings; similarity at or above the threshold in the person's settings) and refuses it otherwise, so nobody else's voice is cloned. A span that passes is split into phrases at the pauses of the original; each phrase is spoken by the settings' clone model in the reference voice, read back by whisper (zero word errors against its words), stretched to the time the original phrase took (never more than the settings allow) and laid at its original offset, so the span keeps its length and every phrase starts where it started. The span is kept only when the whole read has zero word errors against its text, and is then marked cloned in grades.json. The reference must be a clean recording of the person who agreed to be cloned. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Commit the chosen changes
values.job: Commit what is chosen for the next commit in a project on the person's computer, with a message
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and message (what this commit says). Commits what is staged, as the person's own git settings say who made it, and returns the project's changes after it. It does not stage anything itself and does not send the commit anywhere. With nothing staged, git's own words say so.

values.title: Build the instruction to write from
values.job: Build the exact instruction to write something from a writing recipe and the person's material, before writing it
values.description: Give recipe_id (from tool:list-writing-recipes) or your own recipe (instruction_plan.prompt_template: literal text, { block_ref }, { slot: work_item, path }, { slot: schema }, { slot: grounding, label } and conditional segments; optional output_contract, gate_policy, delivery_target, context_retrieval, work_item fields), work_item (the person's text and the answers the recipe asks for; missing answers take the recipe's defaults), grounding (source excerpts, each with its id) and blocks (your own instruction blocks, replacing kept ones of the same id). Returns instruction_text to write from, input_refs, output_kind, output_schema, and the recipe's gate_policy and delivery_target. Write from instruction_text yourself, then hand what you wrote to tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe. Nothing here writes or sends anything.

values.title: Copy a website
values.job: Copy an existing live website, its pages as visitors see them plus its pictures, styles and fonts, into the files a public app is published from
values.description: Opens each page of the site in a headless browser, waits for it to finish drawing, and keeps it as a visitor sees it with its scripts taken out; follows the site's own links up to the page limit and fetches same-site pictures, styles and fonts. Copied addresses point at the copy; omitted pages and files keep their original addresses. Returns site.json in your files: { files: { path: contents } }, which publish_public_app_definition takes as its files, and a list of what could not be copied and why. Works on public web sites: the engine lets it reach nothing else.

values.title: Correct a resource usage settlement
values.job: Append a corrected supplier-cost settlement under the original purchased terms, retaining the old version and the exact customer refund, credit or additional-authority obligations
values.description: Append a corrected supplier-cost settlement under the original purchased terms, retaining the old version and the exact customer refund, credit or additional-authority obligations

values.title: Keep and review cost measurements
values.job: Append cost observations once, keep forecasts by version, and aggregate only comparable measured units
values.description: Writes provider and operation level measurements through the existing records door, preserves corrections and unknown coverage, and reads grouped history with scenario, currency, source revision and time windows kept distinct.

values.title: Count a paid installment in Stripe
values.job: When a pay-in-N plan invoice is paid, count it, and stop the plan after the last one so no extra invoice is ever made
values.description: Give subscription_id and the paid invoice_id. A replayed invoice is counted once; the last installment keeps the buyer access and cancels the subscription. Plans that are not pay-in-N are left alone. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Credit what visitors did to the version they saw
values.job: Join who saw which version with who bought, signed up or clicked, so each version's results can be read
values.description: Takes two lists of records (which visitor was assigned which candidate, and which outcomes each visitor produced) and a join that names the fields of each, and returns one observation per visitor, outcome and candidate with how many times it happened and the value it carried. The same records always give the same observations. A join that does not validate is refused with every problem listed.

values.title: Critique a public page
values.job: Judge public web pages (one page, or every page a sitemap lists) against the saved craft rules at phone and desktop width, with a marked picture of each
values.description: Opens the page (url), or every page a sitemap lists (pages_from, less the paths skip names), at 390 and 1280 pixels (the widths are DATA in parts/page-critic/read-data/page-craft-rules.json) and checks it against the craft rules: headings wider than their measure, body text wider than about half the page, small label lines above headings, text too close to the browser's edge, links to anchors that are not on the page, links that do not open, cards that look openable but are not, a page whose newest date is older than fresh_within_days (one number, or { "/path": days } for some pages), a page many screens long, and controls that look the same with a pointer on them. Each finding says what to change, in plain words, and where; each width is kept as a whole-page picture in your files with every finding boxed and numbered. The page is only read.

values.title: Find the techniques from anywhere that would work for what you are making (runs on your computer)
