values.job: Take what I am making (a sales page, a lesson, an app's first screens, a pitch) and find every technique I have kept, from any medium, whose reason for working serves it, which ones work better together, and exactly how to use each one here
values.description: A writer model turns the goal into wants (what must happen in the mind of the person it is for, or in the system it runs on), each naming the properties of the shared vocabulary that must change. Every technique whose operates_on holds one of those properties is joined exactly, its mechanisms ranked by how many media they span, and the writer picks the mechanisms that serve each want. The answer is the techniques holding them, whatever medium each came from, spread over media. Pairs come from the rows' own fields: 'prepares' when one technique changes a property another needs, 'covers' when two serve different wants. The writer adds one concrete line per technique and pair for the goal's own medium, and drops any a constraint rules out (listed in ruled_out with the constraint). Terms the writer names that are not in the vocabulary are listed in unknown. Rows need the crossing fields that tool:say-why-a-technique-works gives them, and the vocabulary their terms come from. Uses a chat model the person names (any OpenAI-compatible server, such as Ollama on their computer).

values.title: Cut a clip and caption it
values.job: Cut one stretch out of a video and burn in its spoken words as captions
values.description: Keeps `from` to `to` (seconds) of the video and burns the words spoken in it as captions in the style you name (see style), for example words that light up as they are said. Without a transcript it only cuts. Saves the clip in your files.

values.title: Decide whether to nudge a person
values.job: Decide whether a person should get a nudge now, honouring their opt-out and a rate limit
values.description: Takes a person's context (a risk number, whether the rate limit still allows a nudge, whether they opted out) and the person's threshold, tone and framing. Checks in this order: opted out, rate limit, then risk. Nudges only when the risk is a number at or over the threshold. A missing context, an unknown risk or a threshold that is not a number means no nudge. The tone and framing come back exactly as the caller gave them. When allowed_tones is given, the nudge is only sent in a listed tone; any other tone means no nudge.

values.title: List what a presentation runtime exposes on a slide, a shape and the notes (runs on your computer)
values.job: Print the property names a presentation runtime exposes on one slide, one shape's text and the speaker notes, so an edit request is written against the real names
values.description: Opens a presentation with the runtime module, takes its first slide and the first shape that has text, and prints the property names found on the slide, the shape's text object, the notes object and its text frame, plus the first shape's text and the notes text. Read-only.

values.title: Draft a funnel
values.job: Start a new funnel with a title and its steps, or add steps to a funnel I already have
values.description: Gives back a funnel-definition record for the person to save in their own records: a new one from a title (with an id that cannot clash with another funnel of the same title) and the step titles, or the person's existing one with steps appended after its last, every other field of it kept as it is. Steps start as titles only; pointing a step at a workflow step, an offer or a measure is adding a ref to its row. A new funnel has only the steps asked for: nothing is made up.

values.title: Draft a post
values.job: Keep a post as a draft for the person to look at: its words, its video or picture, where it goes and when
values.description: Give caption (the words), media (the file as the person's files list it: { identity, name?, media_type?, byte_length? }) with media_facts ({ duration_seconds, width, height } the file does not say), destinations (account_id values from tool:list-post-destinations), caption_by_platform ({ platform: words }), settings_by_platform ({ platform: { ... } }, like a video title), link (an https page; it is added after the words, tagged with the post and the place), scheduled_for (a date and time with its zone), time_zone, source ({ kind, id } of the record it came from, kept as given), format_id, reaches (the people it contacts first, each with where they were found) and drafted_by (the AI writing it). Give post_id to change a draft; changing an approved post, or a scheduled one nothing was sent for, makes it a draft again. Returns post, ready (as tool:check-a-post gives it) and said. Nothing is posted.

values.title: Edit a presentation's text and slide order from a request, then read it back (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the words on slides, rebuild a slide, change speaker notes, delete slides and reorder them in a presentation file, and read the new file back as proof
values.description: Takes a request file naming a presentation runtime module (any module exporting FileBlob and PresentationFile with importPptx and exportPptx), the source and output paths, and per-slide edits by ORIGINAL slide number: replace_text (keeps every other shape), notes, or a whole rebuild (bg, text items, rectangles), plus delete and slide_order. slide_order is applied last and must list every surviving slide exactly once, or the whole request is refused. The report gives each slide's actions and how many shapes each replace_text rule matched (0 when none), then the new file's slide titles in final order and its notes: the readback, not the request, is the proof. The source is never changed. Fonts come from the request (fonts.regular, fonts.bold, or typeface on a text item); none are assumed.

values.title: Enrol someone's voice or face so they can be named
values.job: Let the person's AI name this person later by their voice or face, after they agreed to be known that way
values.description: Measures a recording of one person speaking, or a picture or video of one person's face, or takes a voice heard in a listening, and keeps it as that person's print so later recordings and pictures can name them. It refuses before it measures anything unless `consent` says who agreed to be known by their voice or face and how. Enrolling the same name again adds samples and the new consent words to the same print and keeps the earlier ones. The voice-print, face-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: the numbers of a print are kept only on the device they were made on and are never shared, exported, synced or sent to a model off it. The answer says how many samples the person has, never the numbers.

values.title: Enroll someone in the challenges that fit them
values.job: Decide which time-boxed challenges one person joins from their scores, and build their enrollment records
values.description: Takes the challenge definitions, the observer's score for each challenge (scored beforehand, for example with the tool that scores candidates for an observer), who the observer is, when they start and the status word a new member starts in. A challenge joins the observer when its definition is valid and the score reaches that challenge's own min_score; a person may join many. Answers `enrollments`, each with its record address and the record to store (the window is copied from the definition now), and `skipped`, each with the reason: an invalid definition, no score given, or a score below min_score. Re-running for the same pair gives the same address, so storing it twice keeps one record. The tool holds no clock and no status words: started_at and status_key are required.

values.title: Evaluate a formula over rows
values.job: Evaluate a formula over each row of a list: read a value from the row, then run a pipeline of steps (and, or, not, equals, more than, less than, is in a list, position in a list, lower-case, contains, starts with, join, is empty, is unknown) over it
values.description: Takes a binding (select from the row at a path, or a stated literal, then a transform list of { op, args }; an argument may itself be a binding evaluated over the value the step receives) and rows. Answers one value per row, in order, and the rows that could not be evaluated with the reason (a step given a value of the wrong kind, or a step that is not supported). Three-state logic: and, or and not answer true, false or unknown, and a comparison with an unknown side is unknown. Nothing outside the row is read.

values.title: Expand a canned reply template
values.job: Fill a canned reply template with the details of a request, such as a name or a button label, and give back the finished reply
values.description: Give a template (any JSON in which a value to fill is written as {"$kind":"binding","select":{"from":"dataSource","key":"caller_request","path":"label"},"default":...}) and the details to fill it from: caller_request, provider_record and data (each top-level entry of data can also be named as a key). If you give no template, the provider_record's template is used. Returns the template with every binding replaced; everything else is kept as it was, whatever its shape. A binding that finds nothing gives its default, else null (select.required changes nothing). An object key named itemTemplate is kept as written. A template that is present and null gives null. A binding that reads from another source or has a transform is refused by name. It sends nothing and keeps nothing; the caller delivers the reply.

values.title: Expire old holds
values.job: Free the places whose hold time has run out, and offer each to the waitlist
values.description: Ends every confirmed hold whose expiry has passed by this run's clock and, by default, promotes one waiting entry into each freed place. A hold with no expiry is never ended. Run it on a schedule so a place is never held for ever by someone who went quiet.

values.title: Save a document as a Word file, a PDF, Markdown or plain text (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a document written as a tree of text blocks into a Word (docx) file, a PDF, a Markdown file or a plain text file, with headings, paragraphs and tables kept in order
values.description: Takes a job file and a rules file. The job holds the title, the tree (each node has props with its text, a heading level if it is one, and children; a node with children that all hold two or more short texts is read as a table row, two or more such rows as a table) and a descriptor: format_id, destination_dir (a full path) and file_stem (a plain name, no folder). The rules file is a JSON list of rows of kind structured-file-projection-rules; each names which props carry text, where a heading level is, and per format how the body is built (Markdown and text by templates, Word by heading, body and table styles, PDF by a TrueType font file name and heading sizes). A starter rules file is in read-data/starter-projection-rules.json. Word is written with the standard library only. PDF needs the reportlab library and the named font; an unreadable font or a character the font cannot draw stops the export with a message, never a substituted character. The file is read back and compared to what was meant before the result is printed. Add --project-only to see the sections the tree would give without writing a file.

values.title: Export an editor timeline
values.job: Export an edit as a timeline file (Final Cut Pro XML) that Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut can open
values.description: Writes the edit (the same format render-an-edit takes, with encode width, height and fps) as an xmeml timeline naming each source by the path it has on the editor's computer, saves it in your files, and says what the file could not carry.

values.title: Export the ink marks on a space as an SVG picture
values.job: Draw the ink marks showing on a page or picture as an SVG fragment, with the bounds of all the ink, so the ink can be laid over an export of that page
values.description: Give the mark operations, their styles and the space. Every showing mark becomes one stroke path in the space's own coordinates (M x y, L x y, Z when closed, round caps, the style's stroke, width and opacity, width 3 and opacity 1 when the style says nothing), so the fragment needs no transform to sit over the page it was drawn on. The bounds are the box around all the ink, or null when there is none. A style that names only a colour token has no colour a standalone picture can resolve, so give default_stroke; a mark with neither is refused rather than drawn in a colour nobody chose. Fills are not drawn.

values.title: Turn my records into rows for my Trillion lists (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take records I keep in files (JSON, spreadsheets saved as tab-separated text, markdown tables) and prepare them as rows for my lists, using a mapping I write once
values.description: Reads a mapping file the person gives: the lists to make and, for each source of records, where the records are, which to drop, what to work out from each and how a row is made from it (fields copied, filled into templates, read as numbers or dates, mapped to a list's choices, joined, counted in a file). Writes make_lists.json, the rows in batches and a manifest into a folder the person names. It sends nothing: the batches are put into the lists afterwards. Row ids are stable, so loading the same rows twice updates them. Rows whose ids are in a skip file are left out, so existing rows are never overwritten. When two records make the same row id the mapping must say which one to keep, because choosing silently would drop a record. A re-run replaces only the files an earlier run wrote. It knows no record kinds: every file, column and list comes from the mapping.

values.title: Extract the sound from a video
values.job: Take the sound out of a video as a small audio file, for example to transcribe it
values.description: Saves the video's sound as a mono 16 kHz MP3 in your files (about 0.5 MB a minute), small enough for the speech-to-text tool.

values.title: Sort what I said in my recordings into topics and rate how usable each moment is (runs on your computer)
values.job: Go through my transcribed recordings, cut them into moments, file each moment under topics, and tell me which moments stand alone as a usable idea, story or lesson
values.description: Cuts each transcript (a <name>.words.json with segments) into moments (a new one starts after a silence of 4 seconds or past 120 words), then asks a model that runs on the person's own computer (Ollama) which topic buckets each moment belongs to (0 to 3) and how much it stands alone as a usable spoken idea, claim, story or lesson (0 to 1: camera setup, filler and half sentences score near 0, a complete quotable idea 0.6 to 1). The model judges each moment only from its own words. The buckets come from a vocabulary file that starts from a short seed and grows as the model proposes new buckets, so the person can edit it. A moment the model leaves out of its answer is asked about again alone. The tool writes the moments, their buckets and relevance back into each transcript (or to a separate file with --dry-out), can tag a long file of moments one batch at a time and continue after a stop, and reports how many moments each bucket holds and how many are usable. Nothing leaves the computer, nothing is paid for and no key is needed.

values.title: Fill a template's slots with sourced values and nothing else (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put my own numbers, names and product into a template without changing any of its other words, and show where each value came from
values.description: Takes a template and a fills file giving each slot a value and its sources (a URL, git:<repo>@<commit>, a file line, a timestamp or a time range). A value counts only when every source is checkable and the value's words and numbers appear in a cited source; otherwise the slot stays visibly empty as [TYPE: no source yet] and is listed with the reason and what would fill it. A source can be one of the person's recorded moments (a time range of a word-timed transcript), and the fill then keeps where the value plays. It refuses any id that is not a slot, so the fixed words cannot be changed. Writes the filled script as markdown with the sources table, and with --piece the filled piece for checking and re-timing.

values.title: Keep the rows that match my rules
values.job: Keep the rows of a list that match my rules: a tree of comparisons (is any of, has all of, contains, is more than, is between, is empty, is known and more) joined by all-of and any-of groups, each group optionally negated
values.description: Takes records, the fields the rules may read (an id, a kind and a path into each record) and a rule tree. Answers the positions and the records that match, the field ids the rules read and the rules left out because they are not finished (an unknown field or comparison, a comparison the field's kind does not offer, missing values), never guessing at them. A tree with no finished rule keeps every row. A value that is unknown never matches a comparison that cannot tell (contains, starts with, more than, less than, between and the like) nor its negation (does not contain, has none of), but an unknown value is simply not in a list and not equal to a word, so is none of and is not keep it. A group whose combinator is not one of the listed ones is refused with a sentence. A row whose value is of the wrong kind for a comparison is counted in error_rows and left out. The comparisons are rows of data: send operators to add or change them, or leave it out to use the ones list-comparisons shows.

values.title: Find a completed Stripe checkout
values.job: Find the completed Stripe checkout for one buyer and offer when the buyer browser never came back
values.description: Give offer_id and the buyer customer_email, or a created_after_unix time to look from (then exactly one match is needed). Returns the session id if found, or why not. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Find a published destination
values.job: Find the destination screen an owner has published (a progress page, a results page) among saved records, for one person or subject, and read it safely
values.description: Give rows (records shaped {record, payload}, the payload being the decoded destination-descriptor), the destination's ref and, when the descriptor is for one subject, that subject_ref. Returns found, the descriptor read within safe bounds (at most 64 sections, 200 items each; malformed parts dropped) and finished_refs, the items the owner marked to celebrate whose own percent is 100 or more. A descriptor for one subject is never returned when no subject, or another subject, is given. Nothing is added up or ranked here.

values.title: Find action moments in a video
values.job: Find where the action happens in a video, such as the moment a ball is hit, and give each moment's time in seconds
values.description: Ranks the moments where a sharp sound meets movement in the picture (a racket meeting a ball, a clap, a landing) and returns their times in the video's own seconds, strongest first. Search the whole video or only a stretch of it.

values.title: Find the beats in music
values.job: Find the beat times in a song or in a video's soundtrack, to cut on the beat
values.description: Returns the time of each beat (seconds) and the tempo in beats per minute.

values.title: Find the faces in a picture or video and say who they are
values.job: Find every face in a picture or video and name the ones that belong to people who agreed to be known
values.description: Finds the faces in a picture, or in a picture taken from a video every few seconds, and answers each face's place (the second, the box in pixels) and who it is: the person's name when one enrolled face is clearly the closest, every person it could be when two are too close to tell, nobody otherwise. Changes no file. Thresholds are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented pictures. The face-print record kind is stays_on_this_device: true: prints are read here and never leave the device they were made on.

values.title: Find my files in my index
values.job: Find a person's files by words, name, place, kind or spoken words, in a file index that already exists on their computer
values.description: Give index_dir (the full path of the folder that holds the index, one the person has let this tool read) and query (the words to look for). The index is a JSON-lines file with one row per file (index_file, default assets.jsonl) and an optional types file (types_file, default content-types.json) whose type_keywords turn a word such as a kind of file into a type and whose stop_words are ignored. A search matches file names, folder paths, tags and the words spoken in or written in the file, ranks name above tag above folder above text, boosts adjacent words and files that hold every word, and never returns another type than the one asked for (type, or a type word in the query). Returns each hit's path, display_path, root, type, identity and size with its score, and how many candidates each root held, so an absence can be told from a thin index. fields names the row field for each of path, display_path, name, root, type, tags, text, identity and size when the index uses other names; weights changes the ranking weights; other_lanes holds hits a caller already has from a meaning or picture search (rows with scores) to be merged with the word hits. values.description: Move every message of one Gmail conversation to Trash, where it can still be restored. Runs as the Google account the input's connection names, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown).

values.title: Edit email draft
values.job: Replace the contents of an existing Gmail draft. raw is a base64url-encoded RFC 2822 message.
values.description: Replace the contents of an existing Gmail draft. raw is a base64url-encoded RFC 2822 message. Runs as the Google account the input's connection names, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown).

values.title: Update email signature
values.job: Set a Gmail SendAs signature using the exact sendAsEmail from the row where isPrimary is true in list_send_as. Gmail sanitizes the HTML and returns its saved value; read list_send_as again to verify provider state. This operation does not manage aliases.
values.description: Set a Gmail SendAs signature using the exact sendAsEmail from the row where isPrimary is true in list_send_as. Gmail sanitizes the HTML and returns its saved value; read list_send_as again to verify provider state. This operation does not manage aliases. Runs as the Google account the input's connection names, with the value the person's vault holds for it (placed only as the request leaves, never shown).

values.title: Change a video's colour
values.job: Put a colour look or grade on a video and adjust its brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, warmth or vibrance
values.description: Applies named looks (film grades, camera log to normal colour, VHS, golden hour, film grain and more) and colour adjustments to the whole video, optionally matching its colour to another video first, and saves the new video in your files at its own size and length.

values.title: Grade the speech in my recordings and clean up what sounds poor (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check whether the speech in each part of my recordings sounds good, keep the good ones as they are and clean up noise, hum, wind, room echo and clipping in the rest
values.description: Takes a list of spans (a stretch of one recording, the words said in it and, ideally, the word times) and measures each: loudness, noise floor read from the pauses between words, signal to noise, clipping, mains hum, wind rumble and room tail, against the person's own settings (a JSON file they give; the tool has no values of its own). A span with no fault is kept as it is. A span with a fault is remastered: high-pass, a notch at the hum and its harmonics, then up to three denoised candidates (DeepFilterNet3 full, DeepFilterNet3 limited to the soft limit in the person's settings, ffmpeg afftdn), each finished the same way (pauses ducked when the room was the fault, de-ess, gentle compression, loudness to the person's target) and read by whisper; the candidate whose read matches the original read or the text, with the best signal to noise, wins, and the remastered cut is graded again. Writes grades.json (per span: grade good, remaster or clone, why, the measures before and after, which candidate won) and one wav per span with the settings' handle either side; the source recordings are only read. A span that is still bad after the remaster is marked clone, for tool:clone-speech-that-repair-could-not-fix. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Hand a request to its owner
values.job: Ask an owner to run an action with what a form, a check or a person supplied, once
values.description: action names the owner and what is asked: owner, action_ref (or action_refs, one request each), optionally id, a fixed input, and copy rows { key, from } or { key, value } where from reads request.<field>, answers.<field> or fields.<field> of the context. context has operation_id (asking again with it is the same request), and optionally record_ref, shape_ref, field_values, answers, linked_receipt_refs, receipt_ref and requested_at. Returns { handed, already, said }: the owner-action-request ids kept now and those already kept, which stay as the owner left them.

values.title: Hold a place
values.job: Hold a place for someone, or put them on the waitlist when every place is taken
values.description: Holds one place on a capacity ledger for a subject, or adds them to the waitlist when their class has no place left. The same idempotency_key sent again answers the first outcome and holds nothing twice. A hold may expire after a number of seconds from now. Answers held or waitlisted and how full the ledger is.

values.title: Hold an output back when risk is too high
values.job: Hold an output back, and give the person's own support resources instead, when its risk is too high or unknown
values.description: Takes a risk assessment (was it run, the risk from 0 to 1 or null, categories) and the person's threshold. The output is released only when the assessment was run, the risk is a number and it is under the threshold. A missing, unfinished or unreadable assessment, or a threshold that is not a number, holds the output back. Held back, the answer carries the support resources the person gave. With an output sent, answers what goes out: the output, or the held-back notice.

values.title: Hold a group to what it agreed
values.job: Keep an agreement a group made, or a session one person planned (a daily meeting, a habit, a deadline), work out when to remind and check, mark who kept it and keep the scorecard
values.description: keep { group, what, agreed_by, cadence?, ... } keeps the agreement as a record and, when it says a time, answers its next meeting and the reminder and the check as something to arm (a repeat or one time); with no time it answers needs_time and arms nothing. retime { group, agreement_id, at, ... } gives or moves its time. agreements lists the group's. remind answers the sentence. check { group, agreement_id, arranged, evidence } works out who came to the last meeting from the evidence handed in (speakers heard, members who wrote), marks each person from the group's policy, keeps one mark per person, day and rule, and answers who missed and any run of misses. mark records one mark with its evidence (a newer mark for the same day replaces the older). scorecard answers each person's points. Nothing is sent or booked: whoever runs it arms the wake, books the calendar and tells the group. The marks and their points, the meeting length, the time zone and the reminder and check minutes are the group's policy, a record or handed in; there is no default. Reading who was heard in a call needs a listening owner; until one exists the caller hands in the names it has.

values.title: How results like this turned out for everyone
values.job: Say how often things worked for other people in situations like mine, without anyone's own result being readable
values.description: Runs in the account that holds the pool, and is the only read of it: the pooled results whose situation is at least rules.min_similarity close in meaning (cosine) to the asked embedding, then one vote per contributor, nothing under rules.min_people distinct people, the median across rules.shards contributor shards, the randomized response undone, Laplace noise fixed by the question and by the rows of the shards that answer it (asking again gives the same answer; any join or withdrawal there draws new noise), and counts rounded to rules.people_bucket and rules.share_step. Returns { enough, people_at_least, worked_share? }, never a row or a contributor. rules are the pool's own settings (pooled_outcomes with search.min_similarity).

values.title: Import Markdown as an editable document
values.job: Turn Markdown into the editable document scene tree, keeping its headings, lists, tables, code and source spans
values.description: Provide Markdown text for a bounded result, or use the file adapter with a folder grant for a large editable tree. The result is a Documents page made from the same Container, Text and Image scene nodes used by the editable document model, plus each visible block's exact source token and UTF-8 byte span. The importer uses its declared editing rules for list shortcuts and inline marks, and verifies that exporting and importing the resulting tree preserves its semantic revision. Markdown source byte spans point into the original UTF-8 input; they are evidence distinct from canonicalized output bytes.

values.title: Import a Markdown file as an editable document
values.job: Turn a Markdown file into the editable document scene tree, keeping its structure and source spans
values.description: Reads one Markdown file inside the folder you grant, imports it through the maintained editable Documents parser, and writes the full editable scene tree plus checked UTF-8 source spans to a new private JSON file inside the same folder. It returns only a small summary. Source and output paths are relative to your granted folder. It never overwrites an existing output. Inputs are limited to 500,000 bytes.

values.title: Join a waitlist
values.job: Put someone on the waitlist for a class or table without trying to hold a place first
values.description: Adds a subject to the end of a capacity ledger's waitlist with a reason, even when places are free. The same idempotency_key sent again answers the first entry and adds nothing.

values.title: Check words or anything made against your rules
values.job: Check words, a plan or anything else someone made against the rules a person set, and say what breaks which rule, why, and what to do instead
values.description: Give rules (one row each) and what to check: text, texts, value (any JSON whose words a person reads), artifact (any JSON a rule reads by path, like a plan or a take's measures) or items, each with an optional kind. A row picks words (words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check), named groups of markers (groups: a framework's parts, the feelings or cues a script should carry), values (path, with where or where_pattern to keep only some) or an evidence check over supplied evidence (evidence: exact source spans, complete review, a captured answer set), may apply only to some kinds, may judge every item together as one piece (across), and may say what must hold: required, count_at_least, count_at_most, value_at_least, value_at_most, equals, includes_all, in_order, repeated_at_least, percent_found_at_least or together_at_least. Its because and at_most travel with every finding. Each row may carry a weight; the answer's score is the weighted score of the rows that apply, and min_score fails a request scored under it. Returns status (passed, failed, held when only capped rows found something, no-applicable-rule, no-input), score, findings (with the offset of each word found) and lines in plain words. Nothing passes on silence: a value test that finds nothing is a finding.

values.title: Keep a profile of how someone does their thing
values.job: Keep the profile of how a person does their thing, so drafts made for them are shaped by it and checked against it
values.description: Give the profile's name, the subject's name, the items you derived (a non-empty list of objects) and, as refs, the feature schemas, evaluators, generators and validation policy that go with it. Returns and keeps one profile record under the profile's name; keeping it again replaces it. Empty items, or a ref that is not a non-empty string, are refused.

values.title: Keep the newest videos of channels and their captions
values.job: List the newest videos of each channel, tab or playlist I name and keep each new video's captions with the times they are said, its description and, if I ask, its top comments, without downloading any video
values.description: For each seed (a channel's @handle, id or link, a link to one of its tabs such as /shorts, or a playlist link) lists the newest `newest` videos with yt-dlp on this computer, then fetches the captions (in the first of caption_languages the video has; json3, else WebVTT), the site's description and, with also ["comments"], the top comments_per_video comments of every listed video not in skip_ids. It never downloads a video. It asks politely, one request at a time with a drawn wait between requests, at most a set number of requests and budget_seconds per run (the settings file harvest-settings.json in this folder holds every number), and it stops at the first refusal (a robot check or too many requests). It keeps three files in your files: listing (listing.json: every listed video of each seed, with kept_before), captions (captions.jsonl: one line per video settled now, { video_id, url, seed, status ready|empty|failed, language, format, lines [[second, words]], info }) and comments (comments.jsonl). With rows it also writes one row per seed or per settled video into your sources list (record:sources:<id>), each field from a fact ({ fact }), a text with {fact} holes ({ text }) or a value ({ value }); a row you already hold keeps the fields this does not write. Facts of a video: video_id, title, url, published, duration, view_count, seed, listing_url, source, caption_status, caption_language. Facts of a seed: seed, listing_url, source, listed, kept, finished. The answer says what was done and, when anything is left, `again`: the input to send next; after a refusal wait `wait_minutes` first. Repeat until again is null.

values.title: Collect current measurement coverage
values.job: Discover operation catalogs, source revisions and execution receipts, then return current neutral measurement observations and forecast coverage
values.description: Reads the configured measurement_source_config account record through the records door, resolves bounded source and receipt roots plus the configured meter book, and collects with a freshly returned provider-qualified price book. New operations under those roots are discovered automatically. Receipt content and source, meter and price revisions are pinned. Missing values, unknown meters, failed work, missing prices, unconfigured roots and incomplete discovery stay unknown. The scheduled workflow persists returned history through the measurement-ledger owner.

values.title: Keep public posts by link
values.job: Keep the text, numbers and media addresses of public posts I name by link, through a public mirror, without opening the posts' site
values.description: For each link to a public post (x.com or twitter.com status links; the link pattern is in harvest-settings.json) asks a third-party public mirror for the post as JSON and keeps its text, counts, author and the addresses of its media, never the media themselves. This depends on that mirror staying up: its address is `posts.mirror_base` in harvest-settings.json and can be changed there. It asks politely with the same limits file as the channel harvest: one request at a time with a drawn wait, a bounded number of requests and budget_seconds per run, a stop at the first refusal. Links already kept (skip_ids) are not asked again. It keeps one file in your files (posts.jsonl: one line per post settled now: user, post_id, link, status ready or failed, the post's kept fields or the reason). A run that stops early answers `again`, the input to send next, and after a refusal `wait_minutes`; repeat until `again` is null. With rows one per post, the posts go into your sources list over the rows already held.

values.title: Keep a resource usage observation
values.job: Keep an attributed measured source attempt once, or preserve its unknown outcome, with a correcting event instead of rewriting history
values.description: Keep an attributed measured source attempt once, or preserve its unknown outcome, with a correcting event instead of rewriting history

values.title: Keep where you stand on something
values.job: Write down whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with something made for them, such as a title, a take, a plan or a file, in their own words
values.description: Give kind (what the thing is: a title, a take, a plan, a file), the thing (artifact_ref, its identity: 1f: and 64 hex digits, or file: and that identity; or the thing itself: text, contains for a part of a text, or view for any JSON, with fold, how its owner says two texts are the same), stance (agree, disagree or partly, or null to take a stand back), why (the person's own words, kept exactly) and answered_by "person": only send what the person said. Returns the stance record, kept in the person's records as one record per kind and identity (stance:<kind>:<identity>), so a change of mind is a new version and every earlier stand stays in its history. Text is identified folded, so the same title typed again finds the same stand. A name instead of an identity, or a stand not answered by the person, is refused.

values.title: Keep the map of who is connected to whom
values.job: Keep a map of who is connected to whom, built from the connection records the person already has, as records of its own
values.description: Give how.record_selectors: how to read connections from the person's connection records, each with match (which records are connections) and connection {identity, endpoints [{role, value}], attributes [{name, value}]}, where a value reads the record: {"method": "json-path", "params": {"path": ["from"]}}, {"method": "literal", "params": {"value": ...}}, {"method": "record-address"}; a match is {"method": "json-field-equals", "params": {"path": ["type"], "value": "introduction"}}, "equals", "exists", "and" or "include-all". Reads every record of kind connection, keeps one graph-node record (id graph-node:<id>) for each person or company and one graph-connection record (id graph-connection:<id>) for each connection, and returns how many it kept and any record that could not be read.

values.title: Lay out a calendar view
values.job: Arrange time blocks for a day, week, month or agenda view, split overlapping blocks into columns, and name the blocks that clash
values.description: Takes time blocks and the views the person keeps (each a record naming a geometry: a time grid with a number of day columns, a month grid, or an agenda list, and the numbers it reads) and gives back the days to show with the blocks on each. In a time grid, blocks that overlap in time share the day column in equal parts, and every set of blocks that overlap is listed as a clash. Days are the person's own: give utc_offset_minutes and every time moves by it before it is cut into a day; an all-day block is a date and is not moved. There is no clock: the day comes from the anchor, the selected block, the first block or the range start. A view whose geometry is not known is answered with a notice.

values.title: Lay out a person's profile
values.job: Lay out one person's profile page from their record: name, fields with values, related lists such as their activity or deals, and the actions that apply
values.description: Give layout (what the profile shows: surfaceId; identity {titlePath, subtitlePath, fallbackTitle}; fields [{id, label, sourceId, valuePath, fallbackValue, editable, visibleWhen}]; relationships [{id, label, sourceId, itemPath, fields [{key, path}], emptyLabel}]; actions [{id, label, enabled, intent, visibleWhen}]) and sources (the records it reads by name; record is read when a field names none). Returns the profile's title, subtitle, each visible field with its value, each related list with its items, and each visible action.

values.title: Lay pictures over a video
values.job: Put a logo, a photo, or a picture-in-picture or b-roll video over a video at chosen times, with position, size and opacity
values.description: Draws each picture or video from `start` seconds for its length, `size` wide, its centre at `x`,`y` (0..1 across and down), at its opacity, later ones over earlier ones; a video plays its `from`..`to` stretch. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Line up two movements by their phase, whatever their speed (runs on your computer)
values.job: Match each moment of one movement to the same part of another movement, even when one is slower, starts later or has more frames
values.description: Takes two pose tracks (from tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video, or any file in the pose.keypoints.v1 shape) and writes the pairs of frames that show the same phase of the movement: dynamic time warping over each frame's posture, with the joints centred on the hips and scaled by the torso so camera framing and body size do not count. It uses the most confident person in each track. Gamma 0 is hard warping; above 0 is soft warping with a smoother path. The path is monotonic (time never runs backwards), starts at the first pair and ends at the last pair. An empty or torso-less track, or a joint that is not a number, is refused with the reason; nothing is written. The cost grows with the product of the two frame counts: a 10 second clip at 30 frames a second takes seconds, a 10 minute clip does not.

values.title: List a channel's latest videos (runs on your computer)
values.job: Get the latest videos of a creator's channel: their titles, dates, lengths and links
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer with yt-dlp, which lists a channel's videos without downloading them: the answer is the channel's name (source) and its latest videos (30 unless --limit says otherwise), each with item_id, title, duration, published (as the site writes it), url and the first 500 characters of the description. The channel is a link, a channel id (UC...) or a @handle. Nothing is sent to Trillion and no key is needed.

values.title: Look inside a folder on a drive
values.job: List the files and folders in one folder on a drive connected to this person's computer, a page at a time
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. hidden "1" includes hidden files; offset and limit page through a long folder. Returns path, name, parent, mount, entries (name, path, kind, file_kind, bytes, modified_at), total and has_more.

values.title: List the comparisons a rule can use
values.job: List the comparisons and the all-of and any-of groups a rule can use, for one kind of field or every kind
values.description: Answers each comparison's id, its label, what it takes (nothing, one value, a list of values, words, text, a day or a range) and the field kinds that offer it, the group combinators, and the field kinds known. Send operators to list a person's own comparison rows instead of the built-in ones.

values.title: List completed Stripe checkouts
values.job: List every completed Stripe checkout since a time, payment links included, so each buyer can be followed up once
values.description: Give created_after_unix, and offer_id to keep one offer. Returns each checkout oldest first (session id, time, buyer email, offer and price option, amount, currency, subscription id), complete, and next_created_after_unix for the next read. The same checkout can come back in two reads: keep each one once by provider_session_id. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Drives on my computers
values.job: List the drives connected to this person's computer: each drive's name, where it is mounted, its size and free space, its kind (USB, disk image, internal) and whether it can be ejected
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the drives they granted it to see. Returns devices: each with name, mount, size_bytes, free_bytes, kind, internal, ejectable and state.

values.title: List email sending domains
values.job: See which domains my email-sending account can send from and whether each is verified
values.description: Reads the domains of the person's connected email-sending account (Resend) with the key they connected, and answers each domain's name and status and how many there are. It never shows the key and sends no email.

values.title: List ended Stripe subscriptions
values.job: List every Stripe subscription that ended since a time, so each customer record can be marked ended once
values.description: Give ended_after_unix. Returns each ended subscription oldest first (subscription id, when it ended, its metadata) and complete. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Where a post can go
values.job: List the accounts this person can post to, each ready or not and why, and each place they have no account for yet
values.description: Reads the person's connection records. Returns destinations: each account_id (the connection id), platform, label, name and ready, with said when it is not ready (a field the place needs that the connection lacks); not_connected: each place with no account yet; and said. Use the account_id values as tool:draft-a-post destinations. It changes nothing.

values.title: List public prediction markets
values.job: See which prediction markets are open right now, what each asks, its outcomes, their prices and its trading volume
values.description: Reads the public prediction-market list (no account, no key) and gives each market's question, outcomes, outcome prices (the market's own odds), outcome token ids, volume, liquidity, whether it is open and when it ends. The busiest markets come first. Give limit (1 to 100, default 20). The answer's status says live or error with the HTTP status; an error returns no markets and never invented ones. Use a market's token id with tool:read-prediction-market-order-book.

values.title: Programs running on my computer
values.job: List the programs running on this person's computer and how much memory each one uses, the largest first, optionally only the programs whose name has some words
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the right they granted it to see the programs running there. Returns total, programs (each with pid, name, footprint_bytes and resident_bytes; null memory for a program the person may not read) and complete (false when the list was cut at `most`).

values.title: Saved examples
values.job: List every example this person saved of posts, videos and pages that worked, newest first, each with its link, words, pictures and why it worked
values.description: Returns examples (each { id, url, host, site, title, words, pictures, why_it_worked, collection, added_from, added_at, updated_at }, newest first) and count. Read it before writing something for this person in a shape that already worked for someone.

values.title: List tasks and what blocks them
values.job: Read the facts kept about tasks into one entry per task, and see for each task what it blocks
values.description: Takes the facts about tasks, one row per fact ({ subject_id, property_id, value }, the property named like prop:task:title). Returns one entry per task with its number, title, project, status (default pending), priority (default MEDIUM), objective, acceptance criteria, what blocks it, what it blocks (worked out from what blocks the others), attachments (opaque references, never followed) and dates.

values.title: List the items in a list saved on your computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a list the person saved in a file (bookmarks, a source list, an exported set of rows, a browser's saved tabs) into items to research
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer and reads one JSON file: an array of rows, or an object holding rows under sources, bookmarks, items, records, rows or data (shape list, the default), or the sidebar file of the Arc browser (--shape browser-sidebar: pinned and current tabs of its default profile with their folders; an address that looks like an account, admin or sign-in page, or carries a token, is kept as Private page with no address). Each row becomes an item with item_id, title, url, published, description, source_family, source_type, container_path, license_status (unknown when the row says nothing) and lifecycle_status; at most 5000 (--limit cuts it). Nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Kinds of conversation export I can read
values.job: List the kinds of conversation export that can be read (chat apps, email, the Messages database, AI assistant logs, captured web chats), what each one's files look like and what the run must say for it
values.description: Returns said (the count and the ids, in a line) and sources: each { id, label, format, reader, needs, app, files_look_like }. id is what source takes in tool:read-an-export-of-my-conversations; needs lists the choices the run must make for that kind (mailbox_address for mail, expected_provider for a captured web chat); app is the name its conversations are kept under; files_look_like is what a file of that kind holds, which is how a file is matched to its kind when none is named. A kind not listed is a new row in a file of the person's own.

values.title: List the latest items of a feed
values.job: Get the latest posts, videos or episodes of a creator or a topic from their Atom or RSS feed
values.description: Reads one public Atom or RSS feed (at most 2 MB, 15 seconds) and returns its title (source) and its items, each with an item_id (the id the feed gives it, else its link), title, published, url and description. Give limit (1 to 200, 50 when left out) to cut the list. It reaches public sites only and does not sign in. The address of the feed is the person's own: this tool knows no creator and no site.

values.title: List what is due for review
values.job: See which of the things a person is learning are due for review now, soonest first, from the grades they have given them
values.description: Give the items being learned (each with an id and optional text; anything else on an item is handed back), the grades given so far (the item id, the grade word and when) and the person's own spacing policy. Each item's due time is folded from its grades, oldest first, so the grades are the only record and the queue cannot drift from them. Returns every item with whether it is due now, when it is next due, its state to keep and how many grades went into it. Items never reviewed are due at once. Due items come first, soonest due first, then by text and id. Pass learner to count only that person's grades. The policy may be given as policy or found among rows by policy_kind. There is no default policy: a missing policy or field is refused with its name.

values.title: Writing recipes and instruction blocks
values.job: List the ready writing recipes (summarize, translate, rewrite, critique and more) and the instruction blocks a recipe can use
values.description: Give words (every word must be in a recipe's or block's id or label) and section to narrow the list, or nothing for all. Returns recipes, each with id, label, section, needs (the work item fields it must have) and fields (the answers it asks for, with choices and defaults), blocks (id, label, body) and sections. Use a recipe's id as recipe_id in tool:compose-a-writing-instruction.

values.title: Listen to the microphone until a time, and keep who said what
values.job: Listen in on a meeting or a room until a time I give, and keep each person's turn as it is said
values.description: Records the microphone on this computer until `until`, hears each short piece of it on this computer with the Whisper model the person names, names each turn from the voices people enrolled (tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face; unknown voices keep the same number for the whole listening), and writes one heard row per turn as soon as its piece has been heard: the listening, the device, when it began and ended, the words, who said it, whether it is the person, the voice and how sure the match was. The sound never leaves this computer: pieces are kept in the run's own folder and deleted once heard, and only the words and the names are written. It stops at `until` by itself; the person's AI cancels the run to turn listening off, and what was heard before then is kept. The run lasts as long as `until` is from now, up to the row's longest run. The voice-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true.

values.title: Look up a Stripe checkout
values.job: Read a Stripe checkout and the subscription it made: whether it was paid, who by, the metadata set when it began and the real recurring amount
values.description: Give provider_session_id. The amounts and status come from Stripe, not from the buyer browser, so a success redirect cannot forge them. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Look up instruments at my live broker
values.job: Find the instruments my broker lists for trading, such as option contracts, from my live account
values.description: Give route (one broker route with mode "live" and its lookups), lookup (a lookup's name) and query (by the names the lookup allows; the lookup's own defaults fill the rest). A lookup is any read the broker answers: its listed instruments, the account (a lookup with one_item reads the one object as one item, for example equity and buying power) or the positions held. Answers the listed items the lookup keeps (for example only tradable ones), numbers read as numbers, sorted as the lookup says, with the next page token. An error answer carries no items. The held live-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Look up instruments at my paper broker
values.job: Find the instruments my broker lists for trading, such as option contracts, from my paper account
values.description: Give route (one broker route with mode "paper" and its lookups), lookup (a lookup's name) and query (by the names the lookup allows; the lookup's own defaults fill the rest). A lookup is any read the broker answers: its listed instruments, the account (a lookup with one_item reads the one object as one item, for example equity and buying power) or the positions held. Answers the listed items the lookup keeps (for example only tradable ones), numbers read as numbers, sorted as the lookup says, with the next page token. An error answer carries no items. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Make a calendar invite
values.job: Make an invitation file that any mail client turns into a calendar event, or into a cancellation
values.description: Writes a standard calendar file (.ics): a request that creates or updates an event, or a cancel that removes it. The host is the organizer, so the host's own calendar shows it, and everyone else is an attendee. The same uid with a higher sequence updates the event. Times are instants, written in UTC. It sends nothing: attach the text to a message.

values.title: Make a colour lookup table that fixes flat log footage from any camera (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a LUT file so my flat, grey-looking log camera footage looks like normal colour
values.description: Writes a .cube 3D lookup table that maps a camera's log footage to display colour. The camera is not built in: the person passes a profile (a record of kind log-to-display-profile) holding the camera's log curve (a straight-line toe under a cut code, a log segment above it), its gamut matrix, luma weights, video range, the soft shoulder that rolls highlights off and the display gamma, with optional look settings (exposure, saturation, size, red and blue white-balance gains). The table expects the colours ffmpeg gives after it decodes limited-range video to full-range RGB, so it first undoes that expansion. Flags override the profile's settings. The same profile and settings always give the same file, byte for byte. Do not apply a table to footage from another camera or curve: it makes that footage washed out or blown out.

values.title: Make a referral code
values.job: Make a referral code that earns a share of the sales of one product or one seller, and give back the event to save
values.description: Makes a short readable code (letters and digits, no I, L, O or U, so it survives being read aloud) or checks the one you chose, and gives back the event that makes it live once the person saves it. You say what the code points at: the sale attribute and the value it must have, from the attributes you allow. A code someone else already made stays theirs when the events are read. Nothing is kept by the tool.

values.title: Make a sales contract's terms, file request and approval link
values.job: Make the terms of an accepted sales contract ready to give out: what the buyer must accept, the terms as rows, the request that turns them into a PDF, Word, spreadsheet, Markdown or text file, and a link the buyer opens to accept
values.description: Give a contract (its name, currency, total in cents, customer, offer and a list of rules such as Commitment and GrantAccess) and which file forms you want (pdf, csv, xlsx, md, txt; all by default). Returns acceptance_requirements (always the terms; the payment obligation when a rule is a Commitment; the installment authorization when it has a payment schedule), terms_rows (the contract's facts and one row per rule, money in the locale you name, en-US by default), file_request (a structured-file-output.request that tool:export-documents-to-files turns into the files) and output_forms. With a base_url it also returns approval_link: a link that carries the whole request, so the buyer can open it on any computer and see the same contract. The forms a contract can be made in are the rows of data/contract-output-targets.json. Nothing here knows what is being sold, who the parties are or what anything costs.

values.title: Turn something I made or copied into a word-for-word template (runs on your computer)
values.job: Keep the exact words of a script, post, slide set or page as a template where only the specifics (numbers, names, the product) can change
values.description: Reads a spec (sources, lines, slots with their rule, keeps with their reason) or one bare measurement it recognises (a word-timed transcript, a caption file, a post, a table of units, a folder of images) and writes a template: every word and every other measured value of the piece, each marked KEEP, with only the author's own specifics marked SLOT, each slot naming the rule that made it one. Works for any medium the registry lists (spoken scripts, posts, threads, slides, articles, newsletters, pages, audio). Writes TEMPLATE.json and a readable TEMPLATE.md beside it with the slot table, every region, and the dimensions it could not measure with the reason and how they would be measured.

values.title: Make labelled examples from where a person stands
values.job: Turn the verdicts a person already gave into good and bad examples, to tune a model that answers their reading rules
values.description: Give the person's rule document (verdict_rules) and their stands. Every thing of a reading row's kinds whose current stand is their exact agree is a good example; a stand a reading row names in pairs[].rejected is a bad example for that row. A pair naming no current exact stand is refused.

values.title: Make quiz questions from text
values.job: Make fill-in-the-blank quiz questions from a piece of text, such as notes, a lesson or an article
values.description: Splits the text into sentences and turns each into a question by blanking its most telling word, with the answer kept beside it; a sentence with no such word becomes a recall prompt. The same text always gives the same questions with the same ids, ready to ask with the form tools.

values.title: Make the decision
values.job: Record what my AI decided, why, what to do next and how we will know it worked
values.description: Once every question is answered: decision is { option_id (one of the options), reason, next_action, success_measure, evidence_refs, move?, and every decision field the decision asks for }. verdicts are your judge's on the decision fields. A decided decision changes only after a failed result: the earlier decision moves to decision_history. Returns what to do now and how to say it.

values.title: Make a tracked link
values.job: Make a tracked link with UTM fields for a post, ad, email or bio, so visits and sales can be traced to it
values.description: Adds the project, source and campaign (and optionally the medium and a content tag for one post) to a web address as UTM fields, replacing any already there. Refuses an address that is not a web page or carries a user name or password. Use the same project, source and campaign names when breaking visits down later.

values.title: Manage usage pricing
values.job: Read, list, set, supersede, retire or delete my resource pricing rules, with effective dates, resource, plan and client overrides, without changing purchased terms
values.description: Read, list, set, supersede, retire or delete my resource pricing rules, with effective dates, resource, plan and client overrides, without changing purchased terms

values.title: Map an app's screens and controls
values.job: Find the screens of my app and what a person can do on each, so journeys can be written to check it
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer and follows its links within the same origin, at most most_screens screens (20 at most). For each screen: its address, title, headings, the same-origin links, every visible control with its role and accessible name, the actions it offers as `do` objects ready to paste into a journey for tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users, a picture, and the console errors and failed requests seen while it loaded. not_opened lists links that were found but not opened.

values.title: Map who is connected to whom
values.job: Map who is connected to whom from records such as introductions, referrals or deals between people and companies
values.description: Give the records (bare or as {address, payload}), in records or as a JSON file from your files, and how to read connections from them: how.record_selectors, each with match (which records are connections) and connection {identity, endpoints [{role, value}], attributes [{name, value}]}, where a value reads the record: {"method": "json-path", "params": {"path": ["from"]}}, {"method": "literal", "params": {"value": ...}}, {"method": "record-address"}; a match is {"method": "json-field-equals", "params": {"path": ["type"], "value": "introduction"}}, "equals", "exists", "and" or "include-all". Returns each person or company once with the connections it is in, each connection with its ends and details, and any record that could not be read.

values.title: Mark my notices read
values.job: Record which notices this person has read and the first surface they saw them on
values.description: Pass ids such as told:12, or a notification key, and optionally read=false to undo. on.channel names the surface (in-app, browser, watch, apns or device-pull); device_id says which registered device saw it. The first read surface is retained, so repeated reads never move it. Returns ids, read, changed, on and said.

values.title: Match a video's colour to another
values.job: Make one video's colours match another video's, so clips from different cameras or light look like one shoot
values.description: Measures the colour of both videos (this one at its start, the other at match_at seconds) and shifts this video's colours to match, then saves the new video in your files at its own size and length.

values.title: May this spend go ahead
values.job: Just before my AI pays, check that the spend still holds its one current budget reservation
values.description: Reads the latest budget check and the reservation for one operation and answers available only when the check approved this operation, idempotency key and spend authority, has not expired, and exactly one current reservation matches it. Answers the reason, the reserved amount in whole cents and the reservation's fencing token. It changes nothing.

values.title: Measure how much of a checklist is done
values.job: See how much of a packing list or other checklist is done and group its items, for example by category
values.description: Give the items (id, status, and optionally group) and which statuses mean done and which statuses leave the count (an item no longer needed). Returns how many counted items are done, how many are counted, the share done (0 when nothing is counted), and the items grouped by their group with a count and a done count for each. An item with no group goes under ungrouped_label (default uncategorized). Both status lists must be given, and may be empty. An item with no id is refused.

values.title: Measure what ad spend brings back (CAC, LTV, payback)
values.job: Measure return on ad spend per source, campaign or keyword: cost per sign-up, CAC, customer lifetime value, LTV to CAC ratio and payback months, flagging what meets 5x
values.description: Joins ad spend with the visitors each source, campaign or keyword brought (first touch, the same counting as the visits breakdown), their sign-ups, paying customers and revenue. Spend is given as rows ({ amount, source or utm_campaign or utm_term: value }) or as the answers of the Meta Ads and Google Ads spend tools (spend_answers with shape meta-ads-campaign-spend, google-ads-campaign-spend or google-ads-keyword-spend), whose campaign names fill utm_campaign and campaign ids utm_id. Each row and the paid and all-visitor totals give spend, visitors, sign-ups, customers, revenue, cost per sign-up, CAC, revenue per customer per month, LTV (needs gross_margin and monthly_churn or customer_lifetime_months), LTV:CAC, payback months and whether LTV:CAC meets the target (5x unless target_ltv_to_cac says). Payment values are the revenue of revenue_months months (1 when left out). A figure the numbers cannot give is null and unknown says what would give it. Spend in another currency than the project is refused.

values.title: Measure funnel stages
values.job: Count how many visitors reached each stage of a funnel, how many converted and the revenue each stage brought
values.description: Reads the facts a person recorded (one per visit or per sale) and counts, for each stage you list, the visits, the conversions, the conversion rate to one decimal and the revenue in cents. You say which field of a fact holds the stage and which holds the amount; a fact is a conversion when it is marked converted or carries an amount. Facts that name none of your stages are counted separately, not hidden. It reads and counts only.

values.title: Measure a video's loudness
values.job: Measure how loud a video or recording is and whether it is ready to publish
values.description: Measures integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness range and true peak, and says whether it meets the target (-14 LUFS by default) without clipping.

values.title: Measure exact page citations across planned questions and answer engines
values.job: Compare every planned page × question × answer engine cell against recorded answer observations, keeping exact page citations, unavailable answers and unasked cells distinct
values.description: Builds the complete page × question × engine matrix from a plan and supplied observations. A citation counts only when its parsed HTTP(S) URL exactly matches the page URL, its supplied checked canonical URL, or an explicitly supplied verified redirect URL; a path prefix is never enough. Query strings remain significant and fragments are ignored. Original answers and citation links are preserved. Missing/not-run and unavailable cells stay unknown; only an observed answer with an explicit citations array can be cited or not cited. This tool measures supplied observations and does not query engines, establish who observed them, or prove why an engine cited a page.

values.title: Cost measurements
values.job: Review provider and operation usage, forecasts, unknown coverage, and billed history in my account
values.description: Shows the account's saved measurement Lists with a live overview, run history, provider and operation filters, versioned forecasts, billed records, source revisions, retries and errors. It keeps units, currencies, scenarios and measured, assumed and unknown values distinct. It includes no private measurements in the screen code.

values.title: Find the moments in my videos, pictures and talks that match a phrase (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find which of my recordings show or mention something, and at what second
values.description: Builds a local index of what a person's videos and pictures look like (frames sampled every few seconds, embedded with a CLIP model) and what their talks say (transcript chunks embedded with a sentence model), then answers a phrase with the best moment in each recording, picture lane and speech lane apart. The script reads one JSON request per line on standard input and prints one reply per line: embed_picture and embed_speech return a value the AI keeps (vectors by the identity it gave), add brings kept values back in so nothing is embedded twice, search takes a phrase. Model names, sampling interval, frame cap and the near-duplicate cut are fields of the request or the config file; the script holds none of a person's recordings, words or settings. Models are read from the local cache and never downloaded by the script, and nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Mix sounds under a video
values.job: Lay music, voice-overs and sound effects under a video at chosen times, each trimmed, with its own volume and fades, music lowering itself under speech
values.description: Plays each sound from `start` seconds into the video, trimmed to `from`..`to` of its file, at its volume with fades; a sound with duck drops while the video's speech or a voice-over is heard. Optionally evens out the whole video's loudness (loudness_lufs, -14 suits most sites). Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Move a booking on my calendar
values.job: Move a booking's event on my own calendar to a new time
values.description: Moves one event on the person's own Google calendar to a new start and end, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. Answers changed, or error and why.

values.title: My browser push application key
values.job: Get the public key browsers need to register for notices
values.description: Returns only the base64url P-256 public applicationServerKey derived from the web_push field of the held notification-signing-keys bundle. The private signing scalar and contact stay on the credential pipe.

values.title: Notices for this device
values.job: Read the newest notices kept for one registered device, oldest first after its cursor
values.description: Pass the device_id returned by notification-device registration. channel must match its route: device-pull for live, web-push or apns; omitted channel uses the registered route. after is the last cursor seen. Returns only notices queued or positively delivered to that device, oldest first, including body and offered actions. It changes nothing.

values.title: What I was told, where it reached me and where I saw it
values.job: List what Trillion told this person, newest first: each notice with every way it went (sent, waiting its turn, turned off or unavailable) and the surface the person saw it on
values.description: Optional limit (up to 100, default 20) and kind (only notices of that kind, such as take-me-there). Returns notices, each { id, kind, title, at, open, read, read_on: { channel, device_id, at } when the person saw it, told: { channel: sent | a stage | not-sent }, why: { channel: what its sender said } for each way that did not carry it }, and said, the count and how many were seen, in words. It reads every notice Trillion keeps, whichever ways it went, and kind is applied before the newest are taken, so one kind is found however many of another came after it; an AI reads where the person saw something instead of guessing. It changes nothing.

values.title: How I chose to be notified
values.job: Show the options a notification setting offers this person and which one they chose
values.description: setting is the name of a setting the person described in their own records. Returns { setting, heading, explanation, options: [{ id, label, description, current }], current, status, said }. status is ready, empty (the setting describes no options), missing (the person has described no such setting; said tells how) or invalid (the saved choice is not one of the options; it is reported, not corrected). It changes nothing.

values.title: My notification devices
values.job: List the devices registered to show or read my notices
values.description: Returns each registered device by opaque device_id, route, label and status. Push tokens and addresses are never returned.

values.title: Notices recorded for me
values.job: List the notification events recorded for one audience, newest first
values.description: audience is the reference the events name in audience_refs; limit is optional (up to 100, default 20). Returns { audience, events, said }, each event exactly as it was recorded. It changes nothing.

values.title: Requests taken and who owes an answer
values.job: List the requests taken, newest first, with their receipts and the ones still waiting on an owner
values.description: Optional owner (only that owner's requests), waiting true (only requests handed to an owner that has given no receipt) and limit (up to 100, default 20). Returns { requests: [{ request_id, text, at, status, disposition, reason, owner_ref, owner_request, receipts, waiting_on_owner }], said }. It changes nothing.

values.title: Name a voice
values.job: Attach a person's name to one voice cluster after identifying that voice
values.description: Keeps your explicit person name for an existing voice cluster. Later analysis shows that name on matching voice segments; the model itself never guesses a name.

values.title: What is using a drive
values.job: Name the programs on this person's computer that are using one drive right now, which would stop it from ejecting
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Returns mount and processes (each pid and name): the programs with files open on that drive.

values.title: Read a decision's next question
values.job: See the next question my method asks about a decision, or, when all are answered, the options and my similar past decisions
values.description: Reads one of the person's decisions and returns its current question (step_id, question, fields, the checks to answer and their verdict words, the answer_schema), the person's current pursuits when the question weighs them, and the method coverage. With every question answered it returns the options, the decision fields, how to say it, and the person's similar earlier decisions with how each turned out.

values.title: Observe something I watched or read
values.job: Turn one thing a person watched, read, used or saved (a page they visited, words they selected, an app they spent a while in, a feed item) into one observation with a stable identity, so seeing the same thing again is recognised and a changed page is a new revision
values.description: Give source_ref (what to call the source) and content (an object saying what was seen: url, text, title, app, window, whatever applies). Optional: native_ref (the item's own id; else its url, else the identity of its content), observed_at (ISO-8601 UTC; else now), metadata. Returns observation { id, source_ref, native_ref, observed_at, content_revision, payload } and said. A url adds its host and, where none was given, a title. content_revision is the BLAKE3 identity of the payload without the time, so the same words seen at another time are the same revision and the same id. Reads nothing and keeps nothing: hand the observation to whatever keeps the person's records.

values.title: Open a capacity ledger
values.job: Set up how many places there are for a class, table, room or any limited thing, so my AI can hold them one by one
values.description: Opens one capacity ledger as a record in the person's own records: the total number of places, and optionally how many are kept back for a named class (members, guests, VIP). A class that is not named shares what is left. Opening an id that already exists changes nothing and answers how full it is.

values.title: Open a paid file for a buyer
values.job: Check, each time a buyer opens a paid file link, that they still hold access, and say which sealed bytes to stream
values.description: For a link's token and the account presenting it: refuses a malformed or expired token, then checks the file's paid-file record against what the presenter holds now, so a refund or an ended subscription stops the very next open and a link passed to someone else does not open. On authorized it answers the sealed copy's identity, the cipher, the nonce and the NAME of the key the door decrypts with; never the key.

values.title: Sort my saved browser tabs into folders by my rules
values.job: Sort the tabs a person pinned in their browser into folders by rules they wrote, keep every tab and a backup of the file, and undo it
values.description: Works on the browser's sidebar file (the Arc layout) inside the folder the person granted for change; close the browser first, because it rewrites the file while it runs. Give file (the sidebar file's plain name) and rules: space (title of the space), root_folder (title of the pinned folder that holds the sorted tree), folders ({ top: [sub, ...] }, the tree to make; the root folder must already hold exactly one folder for each name, because the browser makes folders and this reuses them), fallback ([top, sub?] for a covered tab no rule places), and optionally skip_hosts, relevant_hosts, relevant_words (what covers a tab outside the root folder) and rules ([{ put_in: [top, sub?], hosts, words }], first match wins; words are matched anywhere in the tab's title, address and folder path, ignoring case). Tabs already in the root folder are always covered; a split view moves whole. Without apply: true it only reports every tab's decision and the counts, and writes nothing. With apply: true it first copies the file to a backup beside it, checks that every tab is still reachable and no item appeared or went, then replaces the file in one step.
