To undo, give file and restore_from (the backup's name): the file is put back and what it replaced is kept. Reads no history, cookies, passwords or page content. Returns the counts, each tab's decision and folder, whether it was applied, and the backup's name.

values.title: Pay someone a share through Stripe
values.job: Pay a share of what I took on to a person I pay, out of my own Stripe balance
values.description: This pays real money out. Give amount_cents, currency, destination (their Stripe account id), optionally source_transaction, and confirm_moves_money: true in the same request, or nothing is sent. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Pick a cover frame for a video
values.job: Choose the best frame of a video for its cover or thumbnail and save it as a picture
values.description: Scores frames across the video for sharpness and exposure, saves the best one (or the frame at `at` seconds) as a JPEG in your files, and returns its time.

values.title: Pick the progress rules that fire
values.job: Pick which of my progress rules fire for my current numbers and give the adjustment each carries
values.description: Takes one value per metric (signals) and the person's rules. A rule fires when its metric has a number and the number lies in the rule's half-open band [min, max) (an omitted min is minus infinity, an omitted max is plus infinity). Answers the fired rules with the value that fired them, their adjustments in rule order, and whether any fired. Rules may overlap, so several can fire. Metrics, bands and adjustments are the person's; the tool knows none.

values.title: Find the cleanest stretch of someone's speech to use as the voice to clone from (runs on your computer)
values.job: From a person's own recordings, pick the cleanest ten seconds of continuous speech to clone their voice from
values.description: Takes a list of recordings of the person who agreed to be cloned, each with its word times. In each recording it takes the first run of words with no pause over 0.4 s that lasts the window length (ten seconds by default), cuts it to a wav (the recording is only read), measures it, drops windows that are too quiet, too loud or clipped, and ranks the rest by signal to noise. Writes reference-candidates.json with each window's wav, text and measures, and prints the best few. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Check or update the pins of a folder of DATA files
values.job: Check that a pin file records each DATA file's exact byte count and BLAKE3, or bring the pins up to the files, so a program that reads them can refuse a file that changed after it was pinned
values.description: Reads every file under a folder (skipping folders whose names start with a dot, and the files named as never pinned), hashes each with BLAKE3 and compares it with its entry in the pin file. check answers which pins are added, changed or gone; write rewrites only the entries, keeping every other key of the pin file and the order of the entries it keeps. The pin file's shape is DATA (read-data/pin-shape.json or the caller's own).

values.title: Pin a video's frames into labelled contact-sheet pages (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a manifest of extracted video frames into labelled page images, with timestamps, that an AI can look at and cite
values.description: Projects a frame manifest into the form the pages need, then tiles the frames into labelled page images (optionally pairing adjacent candidate frames with their frame number and time). Each page is bound to the identity of the frames on it. Sizes, quality and font are options.

values.title: Put a section into a markdown document
values.job: Put one named section into a markdown document without repeating it: replace the section with the same heading, or add it at the end
values.description: Give the whole markdown document as text and the section as text. The section names itself by its own first heading line. When the document already has that heading, the section from there to the next heading of the same or a higher level is replaced (its deeper subsections go with it, its sibling sections stay); otherwise the section is added at the end. A heading-looking line inside a fenced block never ends a section, so a document that quotes markdown is safe. Placing the same section twice gives the same text. A section with no heading is refused, because it could never be replaced later. Returns the new document text, whether the section was appended or replaced, and its heading.

values.title: Place live orders from a trading policy
values.job: Place the orders of my trading policy at my broker's live (real money) account
values.description: Give policy (its version, its orders, and its own limits: risk.max_order_notional, risk.max_daily_notional and risk.day_time_zone), routes (how your broker takes an order, each route with mode "live") and prices for market orders. Every order is checked first and skipped with its reason when it is malformed, says live: false, has no live route, was already sent for this policy version, or would pass a limit; nothing is resized. Each sent order is kept as a trade-order record before it leaves, with the broker's real answer after; a 4xx answer is a refusal, and no answer is "unknown" and is never sent again. With no policy nothing is sent and the answer says what to give. The held live-broker-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never kept or shown.

values.title: Place paper orders from a trading policy
values.job: Place the orders of my trading policy at my broker's paper account
values.description: Give policy (its version, its orders, and its own limits: risk.max_order_notional, risk.max_daily_notional and risk.day_time_zone), routes (how your broker takes an order, each route with mode "paper") and prices for market orders. Every order is checked first and skipped with its reason when it is malformed, says live: true, has no paper route, was already sent for this policy version, or would pass a limit; nothing is resized. Each sent order is kept as a trade-order record before it leaves, with the broker's real answer after; a 4xx answer is a refusal, and no answer is "unknown" and is never sent again. With no policy nothing is sent and the answer says what to give. The held paper-broker-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never kept or shown.

values.title: Plan a side-by-side video of two movements, each framed on its person (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make the edit for a video that shows two movements next to each other, each cropped to the person doing it, with labels and an optional slow-motion pass
values.description: Takes two clips with their pose tracks (from tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video), the second of each clip to centre on, and the look as data: labels and corners, side by side or stacked, a mirror for a clip filmed from the other side, the passes (a full pass and a slow-motion pass, each with its own window), the picture size and an optional narration to replace the sound. It writes an edit for the media-composition tool: for each pass one split segment whose cells are crops of each clip around the joints it found in that window, padded and cut to the cell's shape and kept inside the clip's frame; with no confident joint a centred crop. The window is cut to the shorter clip so both cells stay in step. It renders nothing: hand the edit to the media-composition tool.

values.title: Plan moving kept stands into stance records
values.job: Turn stands a person took that were kept somewhere else into their stance records, with every earlier stand as an earlier version, and show what would change before anything is written
values.description: Give stances (rows: kind, text, contains or view, stance, why, by, at, earlier as [{stance, why, at}], and the old ref if there was one) and fold, how the owner of the rules says two texts are the same. Returns writes, the record versions to send one at a time in order (each record's earlier stands first, oldest first), and summary: rows, records and versions by kind, refs_changed (rows whose identity differs from their old ref) and collisions (records two or more rows became under the fold, with each row's text and time). summary_only true leaves the writes out. It writes nothing.

values.title: Plan the write that accepts an evaluation of a learner's step
values.job: Accept the result of judging a learner's work on a step: the receipt to keep and the learner's next progress state, without applying one twice
values.description: Give the evaluation receipt, the learner's current progress state (leave out if none) and the revision you expect it to be at, and the receipt already stored under that evaluation id if there is one. Returns the writes to make through the records door, each with what it expects to find (the receipt not yet stored; the state at the revision you gave), then you read both back. The step is finished only if the receipt's decision says so. The same receipt again returns idempotent with no writes; a different receipt under the same id, a stale revision, a state that belongs to another learner or track, or an unsound receipt is refused with the reason.

values.title: Plan an event
values.job: Turn my draft of a gathering into its session, its catalog entry, the places to open and the link people will use
values.description: Checks an organizer's draft (a retained 128-bit hex id, the owning group, labels in any language, a primary time and an optional alternate in the zone given, a place, a mode and a visibility word the organizer chooses, a capacity of 1 to 1,000,000, the host's web address and the workflow to run) and answers the session, the catalog entry that offers it, the capacity ledger to open for its places (the input of tool:open-a-capacity-ledger), and the preview and share addresses. The same draft always gives the same plan. It plans only: nothing is kept, published or sent. Refuses a half-given alternate, an end before a start, an unsafe route or a web address that is not https (except this computer's own).

values.title: Point editor projects at clips' new places
values.job: On the person's own computer, point their Premiere Pro projects and DaVinci Resolve's open project at clips that moved to a new place, such as their Trillion files connected as a drive
values.description: Runs on the computer where the editors are. Rewrites each Premiere Pro project that names a moved clip so it opens the clip from its new place, keeping the original project beside it, and relinks the clips in the project DaVinci Resolve has open through Resolve's own scripting. A project that is open is left alone and reported. On a computer every Premiere project is found by Spotlight; elsewhere name the project files.

values.title: Keep cards to practise and bring them back on schedule
values.job: Keep something a person wants to get right every time (a word, a habit, a fact) as a card, ask for what is due now, grade each recall and see how well it is known
values.description: Operation add keeps a card { prompt, answer, why?, deck?, source_ref? } (adding the same prompt in a deck again keeps its progress and refreshes the answer and why). due { deck?, limit? } lists the cards due now. grade { card_id, grade } records one recall and answers when the card is due next, whether it lapsed and its mastery (0 to 1000, when the policy names how many days count as fully learned). cards { deck? } lists every card with where it stands. remove { card_id } stops a card coming back. remind answers how many are due and a sentence, so a wake or a workflow can tell the person; it sends nothing. Cards and grades are the person's own records; a due time is folded from the grades each time and never stored. The spacing policy (starting ease, the first two gaps, the lapse quality, the grade words and their quality) is the person's record of type record:practice-policy, or comes with the request as policy; there is no default. Ask the person the prompt, let them answer in their own words, then grade it.

values.title: Predict how a viewer's brain responds to a video, second by second (runs on your computer)
values.job: See, second by second, where a video should hold a viewer's attention and where it goes flat, by predicting the brain's response to it
values.description: Runs a published brain-response model (TRIBE v2 by Meta FAIR) on one video on the person's own computer and writes curve.json and curve.png: the mean predicted cortical response for each second of the video, scored against the video's own average (z), the seconds where it spikes and the stretches where it stays flat. It is a prediction for an average viewer, not a measured view count or retention: use it to compare two cuts of the same video, never two different videos. Every model name, which of picture, sound and words to use, the device, and the spike and flat thresholds are fields of the request. The model's weights are licensed for non-commercial use only (CC-BY-NC-4.0); the person must be using it that way. The video is only read: the script works on a copy. Nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Prepare the notes a match plan is made from, and record the plan
values.job: Plan a match against an opponent: gather what the trusted notes say about both sides into the brief a plan is written from, then check and record the plan that was written
values.description: Calls no model: the AI that reads the brief writes the plan. context takes the person's records, who is self and who is the opponent, who asked, and plan_shape { strategies, tactics_per_strategy } (how many of each the person wants; both required). It returns a plan-request record whose promptText asks for exactly that shape and then lists what only the usable evidence says of each side, one line per fact: names, facts, style, strongest, weakest, strategies that worked and did not work (earlier tactic outcomes included), ratings out of 100 and any other fact in the profile. Missing facts are left out, never written as unknown. It also lists the ids of the public, private and to-be-reviewed reports, the profiles and the tactic results behind the brief. A report is usable only if the confidence policy allows it (confidence_policy, or an evidence-confidence-policy record in the rows); with no policy none is, and every report is listed for review. record-plan takes the written strategies (each { strategyId, name, tactics: [{ tacticId, label, reason? }] }) and returns the match-plan result record only if it has exactly the strategies and tactics asked for. Records come back for the caller to write; nothing is kept here.

values.title: Prepare sign-ups and payments to send back to Meta Ads and Google Ads
values.job: Send sign-up and payment conversions back to Meta Ads (Conversions API) and Google Ads so their bidding learns which clicks became customers
values.description: Off until a destination is turned on (on: true) with its account (Meta: pixel_id; Google Ads: operating_account_id, the customer id without dashes) and which outcome is which event (Meta: an event name like CompleteRegistration or Purchase; Google Ads: a conversion action id). Each conversion (visitor, outcome, at, value, event_id, email, phone) becomes one event carrying the click ids of the visitor's first touch (gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbc, fbp; fbc is made from fbclid when absent) and the email and phone hashed with SHA-256 after each platform's own plain-form rule; the plain values never appear in the answer. The answer lists the sends, each a connection tool (tool:meta-ads-send-conversion-events or tool:google-ads-send-conversions) with its exact input, batched to the platform's limit, and the conversions skipped with why. Event ids are the conversion's event_id or project:visitor:outcome, so sending again is counted once; give each repeat payment its own event_id.

values.title: Prepare public content for people and discovery tools
values.job: Prepare one explicitly authorized public source page as consistent HTML, Markdown, structured data and discovery-feed data, with exact source versions and continuation state.
values.description: Takes a site identity, one bounded page from the existing current-public-view owner, its real source version and observation time, public document citations and one origin-relative route per document. A customer’s existing public List/share read enforces current visibility; this pure projector does not authenticate caller strings or create rights. Imported or model-written text is parsed as safe blocks and rendered through the existing structured page renderer. The complete flag, requestedCursor and nextCursor must match the owner’s actual paged result. Preparation never publishes or caches content.

values.title: Price a sale
values.job: Work out what a buyer would pay for one of my offers and one of its prices: what is due today, what repeats and when, with a trial, a per-unit count, a code or an amount they choose
values.description: Give offerId, priceOptionId, checkoutAttemptId and checkoutStartedAt, and optionally checkoutCode, unitCount, customerSelectedAmountCents or chargeDimensions. Your offers and code adjustments are read from your own records (or pass offers and adjustments). Nothing is charged; this only works out the quote.

values.title: Price resource usage
values.job: Price measured resource costs from my versioned resource, plan and client rules or purchased snapshots, and keep one total with expandable detail without charging rollups twice
values.description: Price measured resource costs from my versioned resource, plan and client rules or purchased snapshots, and keep one total with expandable detail without charging rollups twice

values.title: Print a file
values.job: Print a file from the person's Trillion files on a printer their computer already has (paper size, fit to page, two-sided, colour, copies), so the person never opens a print dialog
values.description: Give file (its name in the person's files, such as /Projects/sample-card.pdf, or its identity); printer (from tool:printers; the computer's default when left out), copies, paper (the print system's size name, such as Letter, A4, Tabloid), fit (true to fit the page), sides (one-sided, two-sided-long-edge), color (color or monochrome), orientation and title when wanted. Returns printed, the printer, the job id and said. Large-format or many copies belong to a print shop (workflow:print-and-deliver).

values.title: Printers I can use
values.job: List the printers the person's computer can print to, and which one is the default

values.title: Promote from the waitlist
values.job: Move the next waiting person (or one I name) into a place that is free
values.description: Promotes the first waiting entry whose class has a free place, or the waiting entry named, into a hold. Nothing happens when no place is free or nobody waits. The same idempotency_key sent again changes nothing.

values.title: Publish what a saved view of my list shows into a file my site shows (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put the rows one saved view of my list shows (a changelog, the articles I marked public) into a file my website renders when it is next deployed, without opening my account to the internet
values.description: Takes what tool:read-a-list-view read for one saved view (one page holding the whole view: the rows its rules keep, in its order, with the list's fields) and a config naming the view's record id, and writes { schema, source: { view, list, blake3 }, fields, rows: [{ id, values }] }. With media in the config, the pictures and recordings the rows name are copied into the site's own static files under the BLAKE3 of their bytes (never twice) and the rows name the site's address. The BLAKE3 of the fields and rows is the file's key, so publishing the same rows again writes nothing. A read that holds only part of the view publishes nothing. It names no list, view or field.

values.title: Publish a post now
values.job: Queue an approved post for immediate sending through each destination's existing send row
values.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values snapshot reviewed for this action). It is refused if the post changed, is not approved, or is not ready for every destination. When ready, it sets the post's time to now and queues the existing at-its-time wake; this action itself sends nothing and does not say the post was published. The wake and each destination's send row record the actual outcome. Repeating the same request while it is queued returns the existing state without arming another send. A destination whose outcome is not known is never sent again automatically. Returns post_id, status, post, ready and said.

values.title: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read into my own records
values.job: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read into my own records
values.description: Reads the text and announcement channels of every server the bot is in (only those the bot may view and read the history of), newest messages first, and keeps them in your records beside the ones already there: a message pulled twice is kept once, an edited message replaces the older copy, and a renamed channel takes its new title. The bot cannot read anyone's personal direct messages, and a message's text is empty unless the bot has the Message Content setting. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Discord bot token (name discord-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Discord did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the direct messages of my Instagram professional account into my own records
values.job: Pull the direct messages of my Instagram professional account into my own records
values.description: Reads the conversations of the Instagram professional account the token belongs to (through the Instagram messaging API, not by logging in as a person) and the newest messages of each, and keeps them in your records. Each conversation keeps the service's own description of it (its participants) in source. A message pulled twice is kept once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Instagram messaging access token (name instagram-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Instagram did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the Messenger conversations of my Facebook Page into my own records
values.job: Pull the Messenger conversations of my Facebook Page into my own records
values.description: Reads the Messenger conversations of the Facebook Page the page access token belongs to and the newest messages of each, and keeps them in your records. Each conversation keeps the service's own description of it (its participants) in source. A message pulled twice is kept once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Facebook Page access token (name messenger-page-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Facebook Messenger did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull my Pinterest pins and boards into my own records
values.job: Pull my Pinterest pins and boards into my own records
values.description: Reads the pins and boards of the account the token belongs to (needs a token with pins:read and boards:read) and keeps each in your records. It stops at the first page it already holds, so a pull after the first reads only what is new; a pin or board pulled again has its fields refreshed. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages. The held Pinterest access token (name pinterest-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Pinterest did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed into my own records
values.job: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed into my own records
values.description: Keeps the conversations a Signal client on your computer printed (signal-cli output, handed in as conversations) as conversations in your records, with who the account is (self_id). It asks no one and holds no token: the Signal client holds its own login and the transport that runs it is a different row. A message pulled twice is kept once, an edit replaces the older copy, messages stay exactly as printed in time order, and the cursor is the greatest message time seen, which the transport asks the client from next time. Give self_id and conversations, and optionally account (a name for this account, default "default") and most_threads. Answers status (pulled), how many new messages arrived, the cursor, and anything that failed in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the messages from the Slack channels my bot is in into my own records
values.job: Pull the messages from the Slack channels my bot is in into my own records
values.description: Reads the public channels the bot is a member of, only the messages newer than the last pull (the cursor is the newest message time seen, and moves only when no request failed), and keeps them in your records: a message pulled twice is kept once and an edited message replaces the older copy. Channels the bot has not joined cannot be read. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Slack bot token (name slack-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Slack did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the messages my Telegram bot was sent into my own records
values.job: Pull the messages my Telegram bot was sent into my own records
values.description: Reads the updates waiting for the bot (messages and edited messages in chats, groups and channels it is in), keeps each chat as a conversation in your records and moves the offset past what it read so Telegram does not send it again. A message pulled twice is kept once and an edit replaces the older copy. A bot cannot read your own private chats. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Telegram bot token (name telegram-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Telegram did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X into my own records
values.job: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X into my own records
values.description: Reads your bookmarks (newest first; needs a token with the bookmark.read, tweet.read and users.read scopes) and keeps each in your records. It stops at the first page it already holds, so a pull after the first reads only what is new, and a bookmark pulled twice is kept once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages. The held X OAuth 2.0 user access token (name x-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when X did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

values.title: Put a booking on my calendar
values.job: Make the event for a booking on my own calendar and invite the people booked
values.description: Makes one event on the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account), and has Google invite the attendees. A video call is made only when video_call_request_id is given, and is an error when Google made none. With booking_id, the event's id (and call link) is kept on that booking record. Answers created and the event's id and link, or error and why.

values.title: Put prepared records into my account through my door, writing only what it lacks (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put the records I prepared into my account so a re-run writes nothing: read what my account holds, send only what differs (or, when I keep edited rows, only what it lacks), in small commands, and stop at the first refusal
values.description: Takes the result of tool:build-records-to-write directly. Through this run's separately scoped records door, it reads only the target record kinds declared on this row, skips records already held when keep_held is true, or merges source changes against an optional previous-import baseline while preserving live edits and deletions. It reports conflicts, writes bounded commands with fresh per-run request keys, reconciles unknown write outcomes and returns readback counts; a mismatching readback is never all_written. It reads no host payload file, config, keychain item or sender credential. The standalone send_record_write.py command remains available for a person who chooses the manual computer workflow.

values.title: Make the private bit for a result
values.job: Turn whether something worked into the one noisy yes or no that may leave my account to teach everyone, so nobody can tell my real result
values.description: Randomized response in the person's own store: returns worked as the truth with probability e^epsilon/(1+e^epsilon) and the opposite otherwise, drawn from the platform's cryptographic random source. rules.epsilon is the pool's privacy loss (the pool's own settings). Keep the bit you got with the result it is for, so the same result is never sent with a new draw.

values.title: Rank what is still open on a trip
values.job: Plan a trip: list everything still open across its schedule, packing list and bookings in the order to deal with it, with the one thing to do first and a count of open things per lane
values.description: Give the trip's lanes, each a list of rows (id, title, status, and optionally kind, group, day_order, day_date, starts_at, ends_at), and the person's policy: priority_order (the priority names, most urgent first, the last one meaning closed) and, for each lane, default_priority, priority_by_status (which status has which priority) and sort_by (the row fields that order things of the same priority, for example day_order then starts_at). A row with no status takes the lane's default_status. Returns every row with its priority, then the first open one as focus, the other open ones as later, and for each lane how many rows it holds and how many are open. Things of the same priority come lane by lane in the order the lanes were given. A row with no id is skipped and named under skipped. The tool knows no status and no urgency: a lane the policy does not cover, a priority name outside priority_order and a missing policy are refused.

values.title: Rank people by activity
values.job: Rank people by the points their activity earns, all time or over the last days, and give each person their level, like a leaderboard
values.description: Give each thing people did ({person, kind, at}), the points each kind is worth (weights), the counts to keep (metrics: {key, label, lookback_days}, null for all time), the levels ({level, name, min_points}) and which count ranks them (rank_by). Returns each person with their rank, points, every count and level, best first.

values.title: Rank people by the activity in your records
values.job: Rank the people in the person's own records by the points their recorded activity earns, all time or over the last days, and give each their level
values.description: Reads the person-activity records the person holds (each {person, kind, at}; fields maps another shape by dotted path) instead of being handed the activity. weights, metrics, levels, rank_by and now are as in tool:rank-people-by-activity. Returns each person with their rank, points, every count and level, best first.

values.title: Rank poker hands and name the winner
values.job: Rank poker hands against a board of community cards and say which hand wins
values.description: Give the community cards (none to five) and each player's own cards (up to two), every card as its rank then its suit: ranks 2 to 9, T, J, Q, K, A and suits S, H, D, C, for example AS or TD. Each hand is ranked on its best five cards out of its own and the board, from high card up to a straight flush (an ace plays low in the lowest straight, five high). Returns the hands best first with the category and the five cards that make it, a place (hands that tie share a place) and the winners: every hand in first place. A hand with fewer than five cards in all cannot be ranked yet and comes last with no place. Refuses a card written wrongly and a card given twice.

values.title: Rank records for review
values.job: Put a list of suggestions, matches or any records in the order a person should review them, showing the fields they asked for on each row and whether they already accepted or passed on it
values.description: Give a descriptor (which fields to show, which records to leave out, how rows relate to other records, which parts of a record name the suggestion a stand is on, and the actions on a row), the records, and optionally related records, the person's stands (their accept or pass records) and a list of upsert or delete events to apply over the records first. Returns the rows smallest rank first (then by record ref; a record with no rank has rank null and comes last), each with its shown values, relationship answers, status keys, actions and the person's newest stand on it (none if their newest version takes the stand back), plus counts. Every word about the domain is in the descriptor; a filter or relationship method the tool does not know is refused.

values.title: Move events to where their words now play (runs on your computer)
values.job: After I rewrite the script, move every transition, graphic, caption or section break that was tied to a phrase to where that phrase now plays
values.description: A token in a piece can carry bound_to: the word or phrase it responds to, an edge (start or end of the phrase), an offset in seconds, optionally a slot (so an event tied to a swapped specific follows the new specific) and which repeat of the phrase. Given the word-timed transcript of the rewritten script, every bound token moves to where its words now play and keeps its length when it has an end time. Words missing from the new transcript leave the time unchanged and are listed as unmatched, never guessed. The binding names no medium, so it works for any timed piece.

values.title: Read a capacity ledger
values.job: See who holds the places and who is waiting
values.description: Reads one capacity ledger: every hold and waitlist entry, how full it is, and the ledger as one reservation row (the scope, its state and who holds a place). It changes nothing.

values.title: Read a funnel definition
values.job: Read a funnel that is written as stages pointing at workflow steps, offers, price options and measures, and see each stage's title, versions, price and conversion
values.description: A funnel definition is a list of stages; each stage points at records kept elsewhere (a workflow step that gives its title, a selection surface holding the versions being tried, an offer with the price option the stage shows, and measures that count who entered and who converted). This joins them: each stage's title, its versions with the decided one marked live, its price, its measures with where they came from, and the conversion percent from entered to converted. A stage whose record is missing stays in the answer with what could be read. A stage with several price options and no named option gets no price rather than a guessed one.

values.title: Read a link
values.job: Read one public link into a card: its title, picture, description, site and the words on the page
values.description: Reads one public http or https page (at most 2 MB, 6 seconds) and returns its title, picture (image, and every picture in images), videos, description, site name and icon from the page's own tags and structured data (data, its schema.org JSON-LD), and its readable text. A link that is itself a picture or video is that picture or video. A page that does not answer or says nothing about itself returns the bare address with unread saying why. It does not sign in.

values.title: Read a page of one of my lists or saved views, or refresh its row sources
values.job: Read one page of what one of my lists or saved views shows, from my records, or refresh a list's row sources (a folder of documents, for one) into its records
values.description: Reads the list (or the saved view and its list) through the person's door, from records only: the list's rows are the records of its row type, and each row source's rows are among them, written there by the last refresh (row id <source>~<its id>), so a read runs no tool. A page holds `limit` rows (read_page_rows when left out, never more than rows_per_read) and answers `next` while more remain. A view with rules keeps the rows its rules keep, decided in the same process by the rule filter of tools/formulas, ordered by its sort. With `refresh` it runs the tool each row source names (read-data/list-view.json), reads the whole source, and writes its rows as the list's records: only the rows that changed, removing the rows the source no longer has, in bounded writes. A source with more than rows_per_read rows, a source no tool serves, or a source that answers no rows is refused and nothing of it is written.

values.title: Read a member's profile
values.job: Read the name, about text and email a member keeps in their profile
values.description: Give who (the member's id). Returns profile: display_name, about and email when set, or null when the member has no profile yet.

values.title: Read one treg call by its id
values.job: Read one of the person's treg calls by the id it answered: what it cost, and how an asynchronous task it started is going and where its result is
values.description: Give account and call_id, the x-treg-call-id header of a tool:call-a-treg-endpoint answer. Answers treg's own record of that call (GET /calls/<call id>): call (its endpoint, status and cost_charged_micro), async_task when it started an asynchronous task (status pending, settled, released or timed_out; reserved_micro, settled_micro, error, and once settled its result_url, which expires, or fetch_command), ledger (the money entries) and charged_micro. This is how a task is followed: treg itself polls the provider, so after a call answered 202 with _treg.outcome pending (its x-treg-async header says which statuses are final), read the call about 60 seconds later, then every 30 to 60 seconds, until async_task.status is no longer pending. Never send the call again or try another provider while it is pending: the task may still finish and charge. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read a treg endpoint and its price
values.job: Read one paid endpoint in full before calling it: its price, the inputs it takes, how it is called, and the other providers that do the same job
values.description: Reads one endpoint of treg's public catalog by its id: endpoint.method and endpoint.input (its query or body fields, which are required, their notes), endpoint.cost (usd per unit, per call or per success, and a note on per-row charges), endpoint.async (a task that is polled, when not null), endpoint.observed (how often it worked, over how many calls, when it last worked) and siblings (other providers of the same job with their prices). An id it does not know answers 404 with near misses in detail.did_you_mean. Free and needs no token. Quote the price to the person before the first call of an endpoint, and pass a max_cost_usd to tool:call-a-treg-endpoint that the quoted price fits.

values.title: Get the words spoken in a video from its captions (runs on your computer)
values.job: Get the words spoken in a video as text, from the captions the video site holds for it
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer with yt-dlp, which fetches a video's captions (the automatic ones when there are no others) without downloading the video. The answer is { video_id, url, has_captions, char_count, transcript, status }: status ready with the words, or empty (has_captions false, with the reason in stderr_tail) for a video with none. The original spoken language is read first, then plain English. The video is an id or a link; --watch-base sets the address an id is put after. Nothing is sent to Trillion and no key is needed.

values.title: Read an export of my conversations
values.job: Read an export of the person's conversations (a chat app's saved messages, a mailbox page or email file, the Messages database, an AI assistant's logs or a captured web chat) from a folder they chose, and give each conversation's messages in order, ready to be kept as the person's messages
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it. Give file (a path inside the folder). source names the kind of export (tool:list-the-kinds-of-conversation-export-i-can-read gives them); left out, the file is matched to a kind by what it looks like and a file two kinds could read is refused with their names. sources_file is a file in the folder holding the person's own kinds ({ sources: [row] }): a kind is a row of field names, so a new export is a new row, not new code. descriptor holds the run's own choices: mailbox_address (which address is the person's, for mail), expected_provider (for a captured web chat), source_ref (what to call this source), app (the name the conversations are kept under). mode all (the default) returns the whole export a page of atoms at a time (limit, cursor); threads returns the list of threads, newest first; page returns one thread's newest messages first from before_cursor, for a very large single log (session_id, limit). Returns threads and atoms (the canonical contract: each atom has a stable atom_ref that does not change when its words are edited), conversations ({ conversation_id, title, app, messages: [{ id, speaker, text, at }] }, speaker person, ai or the name the source showed, only what was said, a time only where the source gave one) in the shape the owner that keeps messages takes a chat read off its page, rejections (one structured entry for each thing the export could not give), next_cursor where there is more. Keeps nothing: hand conversations to the owner that keeps messages.

values.title: Read a spreadsheet, document or presentation as data (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a spreadsheet (xlsx), a Word document (docx) or a presentation (pptx) into plain data: the sheets with their rows and typed cells, the document's paragraphs and tables, or the slides' text in presentation order
values.description: Reads one Office file without opening Excel, Word or PowerPoint. A workbook gives its sheets in their declared order, each with rows of cells (what is shown, and with --formulas also what was typed); a document gives its paragraphs, each with a selector like paragraph:3 that counts empty paragraphs too, and its tables; a presentation gives each slide's paragraphs in the order the deck declares, never file-name order. Which kind of file it is comes from the parts inside it, not the file name. The file is never changed. Flags: --formulas, --sheet NAME (other sheets come back as skipped), --max-rows N.

values.title: Answers over time
values.job: Show one person's answers to a form across every time they answered, in order, and the trend of one numeric answer
values.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and field_map (the name you want for each answer, to its questionId), and optionally trend_field (which mapped answer to chart; default the first that is numeric). Returns one row per time answered, oldest first, with the mapped answers and when; the numeric series for the trend; the latest row; and the count. A person who has not answered gets no rows.

values.title: Check by listening that every cleaned-up or re-voiced span still says the right words (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read back every span in a graded folder with a speech transcriber and count the words that differ from what should be said
values.description: Reads the part of each audio file between its handles with whisper large-v3-turbo and counts word errors (edit distance after lower-casing, dropping punctuation and spoken contractions) two ways: against a read of the untouched cut (same decoder, so only the audio differs) and against the span's text. A kept or remastered span passes with zero on either count; a cloned span, which speaks the text, passes with zero against the text. Writes work/verify.json with what was heard and lists every span under the bar. Single-word filler flips between two reads of nearly the same audio are listed, not hidden. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Read my current screen look
values.job: Read this person's current worn screen look, look rules and day plan as the device token payload native screens draw
values.description: Reads this person's current worn screen look and returns the token payload native screens draw: every wearable look, the look now (including a scheduled blend), upcoming changes for twelve hours, and when to read again. `app_data` is the calling app owner's current look DATA: its starting look and themes, plan anchors/presets, and rule facts. Those values are supplied at runtime, never chosen by this generic reader. time_zone is required and must be an IANA zone. host, device, device_id and place are the facts this native screen says about itself; only saved rules matching those facts select another look. A missing personal choice uses `app_data.looks.start_with`. A workspace refusal or unverified answer is an error, never an empty record. Returns `{ worn, worn_record, now, ahead, looks, read_again_at }` in the DeviceLooks token format.

values.title: How long deleted files are kept
values.job: Read how many days this person's Recently Deleted and Archived keep things before they move on
values.description: Takes no input. states: each with its id, label, after_days (null: until put back), default_after_days and what happens when its time ends; choices: the usual numbers of days.

values.title: Show a folder of my documents as the rows of a list
values.job: Read the markdown documents in a folder I granted as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time
values.description: Reads every .md, .markdown and .txt document under the granted folder (or `folder` inside it), skipping folders whose names start with a dot and links that point outside it, in name order, and answers one page of rows: { id (its path under the folder), title, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its bytes), values } where values holds its frontmatter as note.<key> and its file facts as file.<key>. A page holds up to `limit` rows (200 by default, 2,000 at most) and answers `next` while more remain; pass it as `after` for the next page, so any number of documents is read. `match` keeps the documents whose path fits a glob such as */SKILL.md. `backlinks` adds file.backlinks, worked out over the whole folder. Nothing is copied: the documents are the rows. Optional content:true adds exact complete UTF-8 text including frontmatter in bounded linked pieces, keeping the original parent ID and metadata. Child pieces name their parent, part number and total; pass the opaque next cursor unchanged. No body is silently truncated.

values.title: Read how each version did
values.job: Sum what visitors did on each version of an experiment and work out the rate that decides the winner
values.description: Takes the recorded outcome facts for one experiment (views, clicks, conversions or any metric you track, per candidate version) and returns each version's totals. A rate you name (converted over views) is worked out per version, left out where either number is missing or the denominator is zero, and the version that leads on it is named.

values.title: Form results
values.job: Show who answered a form, the score each earned and the segment each was sorted into, with a count per segment
values.description: Give a form_id to see one form, or nothing to see every form. Returns rows (respondentId, formId, segmentId, score, decidedAt), newest decision first, and a summary with the total and a count per segment. A person with no decisions yet gets an empty list, never an invented one.

values.title: Read a glance feed
values.job: Read one feed or an ordered set of feeds for a glance surface
values.description: Give feed or surface and optionally limit (a positive whole number, default 50 per feed). Reads the record queries declared in Workshop DATA, applies each feed's row path, filters, order and displayed fields, and returns { surface?, feeds: [{ id, label, about, status, empty?, rows?, error? }] }. status is ready with empty and rows (an empty rows array is a successful empty read), or unavailable with error { code, message }; one failed feed does not discard available siblings. A row carries its displayed title, optional detail, note, open address, time and progress fraction, flagged and read booleans, actions when declared, and source, the unchanged row. Current data covers habits, waiting, pursuits, told and waiting AI jobs; other historical feeds are explicitly marked unavailable until their record contracts exist.

values.title: Read events from my Google calendar
values.job: Read the events in a time range from one of the person's own Google calendars and give them back as time blocks
values.description: Asks Google for the events of one calendar between two times (every occurrence of a repeating event, in start order) with the person's own Google OAuth client id, client secret and refresh token, and gives them back as time blocks that read-time-blocks and lay-out-a-calendar-view understand. A cancelled event is marked cancelled; an all-day event is a date. It reads only: it never creates, changes or removes an event. The three credentials arrive only on private pipes under the held-value names the row names; no answer or error carries them. Without all three it refuses.

values.title: Read how AIs are told to act
values.job: See the standing instructions every AI is given when it first connects, or read one of them whole
values.description: Answers the rows an AI is told on first connecting: with no id, each row's id, order, whether it is on, where it reaches and its size; with an id, that row whole. It changes nothing; a person switches a row off or adds a rule of their own with their own setting records.

values.title: Read Internet Archive item metadata
values.job: Inspect one Internet Archive item's original metadata, license, rights, collection and available file listing before deciding whether it fits an objective
values.description: Free, read-only lookup at Internet Archive's metadata endpoint. Accepts only an item identifier and returns the original metadata and available file listing, including creator, dates, collection, license/rights statements and access details when present. No media bytes are downloaded. Record the returned identifier and its canonical item page, https://archive.org/details/<identifier>, as provenance. Archive hosting or an available file does not establish permission to reuse. Missing or ambiguous rights stay unknown; independently check the item and collection against the intended use. The George Blood 78rpm collection states research, teaching and private study only and says copyright was not transferred; concert recordings need item-specific review too.

values.title: Latest answers as lines
values.job: Give the latest answers to a form as plain lines, each starting with the question it answers, ready to hand to a writer or a summary
values.description: Give form_id and optionally respondent_id. Returns lines: the most recent time the form was answered, one "Question: answer" line per non-empty answer (the bare answer when the question's label is not known).

values.title: Show live matches, their scores and a tournament board
values.job: Show the current score of live matches for the scorer and for spectators, and a board of matches with their schedule, bracket, standings and leaderboard
values.description: Give the records of the matches (match records, score events, context links and board rows) and get every match, newest first. Each match has the scorer's view (every event counts) and the spectator view (no actor ids, and no tap that is still pending-offline). Events with one sequence number, such as an offline tap and its confirmation, count once: reconciled beats confirmed beats pending-offline, and the same state keeps the later one. The board lists each match with its score line and its linked schedule, bracket, standing and leaderboard rows; a finished match without standing or leaderboard rows of its own gets one row per side (win 3 points, loss 0). With match_id the answer also holds that match's view and the sequence number the next event takes.

values.title: Read my matches in a community, my profile, and the score job I owe
values.job: See who a community's matchmaker proposed for me and where each introduction stands, what my profile still misses, the shortlist my AI still has to score, and fellow members who share my categories
values.description: Reads one member's view (person): on (their switch), cadence_label, next_at, matches (each match_id, status and the community's words for it, answered, answer_by, consent: what to answer a yes with, with, why: the scoring AI's cited reasons, topics, space_id once they are in the one-to-one), profile (answers, categories, complete, missing questions), waiting_for_your_scores (the open round's shortlist with citable claims), discover (members sharing a category, with what they offer and seek), waiting_jobs (this person's own waiting jobs, for their AI to pull: nothing is ever written into another person's account), wake_at (when the community's clock next acts, so the member side wakes then and pulls once), and for the community's owner experiments (each arm's introduced and talked counts and the shown and converted events an experiment owner reads). Writes nothing.

values.title: Read my groups and everything inside them
values.job: Show what is in my groups, lists or collections, with the groups inside them, in their order
values.description: Give roots: the addresses of the groups to start from, each { family, parts: { name: text } }. Each group is read from the person's records (type group) and every member that is itself a group is followed, so the answer holds those groups and everything inside them at any depth. Returns groups (each { groupRef, memberOrder, members: { memberId: { memberId, nodeRef, role?, presentation? } } }, members in memberOrder), count, and skipped: the ids of records that were not a well-formed group or claimed another group's address. A root that is not a group yet is simply not in the answer. It changes nothing.

values.title: Read what my plan needs to decide the next session
values.job: Read my stored progression rules and the last session's result from my training plan, ready for the progress evaluator
values.description: Takes the training plan feed (the plan, its stored progression rules and, when there is one, the last session's result with its measured signals). Answers `rules` (each stored rule turned into { id, metricRef, band, adjustment }, a rule with no metric dropped), `signals` (the last result's { metricRef, value } pairs), `session_id` and the `prescription` the result belongs to (the named session, else the last in the plan). With no usable result there are no signals and no prescription: nothing is made up. The rules are then evaluated against the signals by the progress evaluator (the pick-fired-rules tool), and its adjustments go to the adapt-the-next-session tool.

values.title: Read my saved bookmarks and pins
values.job: Read the bookmarks or pins a person saved on a social site (an export file of X bookmarks or Pinterest pins and boards) from a folder they chose, and give each saved item with its words, author and time, ready to be kept and found like anything else they read
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it. Give file (a path inside the folder). source is x-bookmarks or pinterest-saved; left out, the file is matched to a kind by what it looks like. sources_file is a file in the folder holding the person's own kinds of saved-items export ({ sources: [row] }): a kind is a row of field names, so a new site is a new row, not new code. descriptor holds the run's own choices (source_ref: what to call this source). mode all (the default) returns the whole export a page of atoms at a time (limit, cursor); threads returns the list of saved items, newest first. Each saved item is one thread with one atom: the atom has a stable atom_ref that does not change when its words are edited. Also returns rejections (one structured entry for each thing the export could not give) and next_cursor where there is more. Keeps nothing.

values.title: Read my saved X posts
values.job: Read the posts I bookmarked or liked on X, newest first, with their full words, links and quoted posts
values.description: Reads the posts the person bookmarked or liked on X through X's API with the access token of their connected X account, newest first: each post's full words, who wrote it, when, its pictures, every real link it carries (not the short t.co form) and the post it quotes. Give already_kept (post keys the person already has) to stop at the first posts they already have. It reads only: nothing is posted, liked, followed or changed on X, and the token is never shown. When X refuses (expired token, a plan or credits that do not allow the list, a limit), it says so and gives no empty list.

values.title: Read my training plan
values.job: Read my training plan: its goals, phases, weeks and the sessions prescribed in each week
values.description: Takes the training plan record (goals, phases in a goal, week blocks in a phase, session prescriptions in a week, each prescription with an open dose record and an open intensity record) and answers it decoded, with a count of each, and the sessions of one week when week_id is given. Rows with no id are dropped and a missing field reads as empty, never invented. A week's load intent may be a bare word or a record with any fields; it keeps its own identifier.

values.title: Read my treg balance and recent charges
values.job: Read how much is left on the person's treg balance and what recent calls were charged, to keep a run inside its budget
values.description: Reads the treg team's prepaid balance (balance_micro, in millionths of a US dollar), its credit blocks, amounts held for tasks still running, and its most recent charges. The balance is the hard limit on what any call can spend. Read it before a run's first paid call and after each step: what the run spent is the balance at the start less the balance now. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read which treg team my connection pays from
values.job: Read the treg team a connection's token belongs to, with the team's number that its balance is read by
values.description: Asks treg who the held token is (GET /auth/me, the request the treg command line makes when it needs the team's number). The answer's org_id is the team number tool:read-my-treg-balance takes. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read my workout log
values.job: Read my workout log: what still needs checking, my summary views, the rows to export and my progress over time
values.description: Takes the workout log record: a ledger of evidence atoms (each one thing observed, with when, source, subject, measured dimensions, links to other atoms and how sure it is), plus optional sessions, sets and the person's own projection lenses. Nothing is edited in place: an entry is confirmed, discarded, corrected, split or merged by a later atom that links to it. Answers `canonicalEvidenceAtoms` (entries not replaced), `reviewQueue` (not confirmed and not yet decided, newest first), `lensOutputs` (each of the person's lenses run: previous-value, review-queue, progress-summary, export-rows, or a list of matches), `exportRows` (confirmed entries as flat rows), `progressSeries` (the numeric measure with the most points over time, as plain numbers with its summary; null when none) and `diagnostics`. A lens that finds nothing says so. With done_status (the word the person uses for a finished session) it also answers completion_rate.

values.title: Show a folder of my account's documents as the rows of a list
values.job: Read the markdown documents in a folder of my account's files as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time
values.description: The same rows as tool:read-documents-as-list-rows, read from the person's Namespace files through the run's records door (list_files and read_file, every file read by its name) instead of a folder on their computer. A page holds up to `limit` rows and answers `next` while more remain; `match` keeps the documents whose path fits a glob; `most_bytes` ends a page at the last row whose answer fits. It writes nothing: the files door has no write that checks a file is still the one read. Optional content:true adds exact complete UTF-8 text including frontmatter in bounded linked pieces, keeping the original parent ID and metadata. Child pieces name their parent, part number and total; pass the opaque next cursor unchanged. No body is silently truncated.

values.title: Read where each person's joints are in a video, frame by frame (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the people in a video and where their joints are in every frame, so two movements can be compared
values.description: Runs a pose model on a video on the person's own computer and writes one file in the pose.keypoints.v1 shape: for each person (kept as the same id through the clip) and each frame, 17 joints (nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles) as x and y in pixels with a confidence from 0 to 1. A joint that is not found or is not a finite number is written as absent (0, 0, 0). A track already written for the same video bytes and the same pose model is reused. The model weights are the person's: a downloaded pose checkpoint passed by path; the script names and fetches none.

values.title: Posting calendar
values.job: Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another
values.description: Give from and to (dates and times with their zone). Returns posts: each post whose scheduled time falls in between (or, sent without a time, when it was sent), earliest first, with at, status, words and can_move; and unscheduled: the drafts and approved posts with no time yet. A post gets a new time through draft_post with post_id and scheduled_for, which makes an approved or scheduled post a draft again to approve. Its screen is the month and hour calendar, where a post is dragged to its time.

values.title: Read a prediction market's order book
values.job: See the buy and sell offers on one prediction market outcome: the best prices, the gap between them and how much is offered
values.description: Reads the public order book (no account, no key) of one outcome token and gives every bid and ask as price and size, the best bid and best ask, the spread, the midpoint and the total size on each side. Give token_id (one of a market's token_ids from tool:list-public-prediction-markets). The answer's status says live or error with the HTTP status; an unknown token or an empty book is an error with no levels, never invented ones.

values.title: Read price bars from my market-data account
values.job: Read recent price bars (open, high, low, close, volume) and the latest price for symbols from my own market-data account
values.description: Give feed (how your market-data account is read: url, its default query and the query names it allows, where each held field goes as credential_injections, where the bars are as bars_at, and what each bar field is called as fields with at least timestamp and close) and query (such as the symbols and the bar size, by the feed's own names). Answers bars (symbol, timestamp in milliseconds, open, high, low, close, volume), latest (each symbol's newest close, ready as the prices a trading policy's market orders need) and status (live or error with the HTTP status). An error answer carries no bars, never invented ones. The held market-data-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never shown.

values.title: Read a public web page
values.job: Open one public web page and return its title, readable text, links, the card it describes itself with, every picture and video it declares and its structured data; or walk an outlet's archive from a start address, following its older pages and reading a chosen, dated sample of its entries
values.description: Reads one public HTTP or HTTPS page and returns its title, readable text and links, and the card it describes itself with: its picture, description, site name and icon (each null when the page does not say), every picture (images) and video (videos) it declares in its tags and structured data, and that structured data (data, its schema.org JSON-LD objects). It reaches public sites only (the engine judges every address, every redirect and every address a name resolves to), follows a small number of redirects, limits the response to 2 MB and returns at most 30,000 text characters and 100 links. It does not sign in or reuse browser cookies. With walk it also walks the start address's archive: it reads the site's robots.txt first and obeys it and its crawl delay, follows the listing's next or older links (or a sitemap and its child sitemaps) for at most walk.max_listing_pages listing pages, collects the entries they list with the day each was published, chooses entries by walk.window (a first and last day) or by walk.eras (some of early, middle, recent: equal thirds of the time between the oldest and newest day the listings showed) with walk.count entries from each era or in all, and reads those pages one at a time with at least walk.delay_seconds (2 or more) between requests. Every request stays on the start address's own site. The answer is the start page's read with a walk object: the listing pages read, how many entries were seen and dated, whether the oldest listing page was reached, the eras, the pages read (title, text, day and where the day came from, era) and why the walk stopped. A count of 0 only measures the archive. With walk.source wayback the url is a page, not a listing: the walk asks the Wayback Machine's public index (web.archive.org, no login) for the snapshots of that page that were answered normally, one per walk.collapse period (year, month or day; default month) and inside walk.window when given, picks them by window or eras exactly as above, and reads each chosen snapshot as it was archived (the answer's pages carry snapshot_of, the address that was archived; their day is the snapshot's). Its robots.txt, delay and own-site rules apply to web.archive.org.

values.title: Read resource usage report
values.job: Read a usage report and distinguish provider acceptance from actual payment collection
values.description: Read a usage report and distinguish provider acceptance from actual payment collection

values.title: Read a resource usage settlement
values.job: Inspect a supplier-cost settlement and its original or corrected version, including exact customer amounts, company expense and unresolved funding, without moving money
values.description: Inspect a supplier-cost settlement and its original or corrected version, including exact customer amounts, company expense and unresolved funding, without moving money

values.title: Read spend rails
values.job: See which ways my AI may pay (card, bank, x402 and others) and which rail rows are refused
values.description: Reads the rails shipped with this tool and the person's own payment-rail records (a person's row replaces a shipped row of the same id). Answers each valid rail's id, label, whether it is turned on, the spend authority it spends from, the name of the credential it settles with and its settlement tool, and the rows refused because they do not go through the budget reservation and the spend record. It never shows a key.

values.title: Read records as time blocks
values.job: Turn any records that have a start and an end (bookings, scheduled work, reservations, events) into one ordered list of time blocks, and say which rows could not be shown
values.description: Reads each kind of record through a lens the person wrote: which field is the identity, the start, the end, the title, the colour, the state, and which fields point at other records. A new kind of record that happens in time is one more lens. Rows may be records or lists of cells (column N is the Nth cell). Gives back the blocks ordered by start, how many rows were read and skipped, and an issue for every lens that could not be used or has no rows. It can also read account records through account lenses, and show changes waiting to be written and changes that clashed as blocks of their own. It reads and shows only; it never writes a calendar.

values.title: Read what a running app really shows
values.job: Drive my running app through some steps and report what is actually on the screen after each: which controls exist, what a click would land on, errors, timing
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer, does each step's `do` (the same actions as a walk: goto, click, fill, press, upload, wait, on a control named by role and name), then reads what the page holds as the step's `observe` asks: `elements` (for each match of a selector: its box, cursor, stacking, opacity, whether it is disabled, what a pointer aimed at its own centre would land on, and `pointer_is_self`, which tells a control that is missing from one a layer covers), `count`, `attributes` (named attributes and the form value), `text`, `global_path` (whether a dotted name exists on the page and its kind) and `media_ready` (milliseconds until a video or audio can play). It asserts nothing and fails nothing: a step that cannot complete comes back with `completed: false` and `blocked_by`, its readings are still taken, and the run goes on. The page is never intercepted or stubbed; requests reach the real server. Page errors and failed requests are listed. Use tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users to check that people can do what they came for, with expectations and a verdict; use this to see why something is not working.

values.title: Read what I pulled from a connected account
values.job: Read the conversations, messages and saved items I pulled from a connected account such as Discord, Slack, Telegram, Signal, Instagram, Messenger, X bookmarks or Pinterest
values.description: Give source (discord, slack, telegram, signal, instagram-messages, messenger-messages, x-bookmarks or pinterest-pins) and optionally account (the name it was pulled under, default "default"). Without thread it answers the conversations (id, title, message count), the collections (name, count), who the account is, the cursor and when it was last pulled. With thread (a conversation id from that list) it answers that conversation's messages exactly as the service sent them, the last limit of them (default 100, at most 500). It reads your records and changes nothing; it never reaches the service.

values.title: Note new releases or commits from a repository (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a person's release mark or commit branch, stage each new entry once with its source identity, and let their mapping make list rows
values.description: Reads settings the person gives: a program in the repository that prints JSON naming a release, a git ref for the newest release, or a commit branch where each commit is one entry. In commit mode, each entry has the commit identity, date and its own subject; the first run may start after an explicit commit, and skip_subjects are filters in the settings. The staged file is what the person's mapping turns into rows. The sender with keep_held writes only rows the list lacks, so an existing row or a person's edits are preserved. The tool does not infer push boundaries or group commits by day, and knows no product, list or road.

values.title: Read where you stand on things
values.job: See whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with one thing made for them, in their own words, with every time they changed their mind
values.description: Two steps. First page records:history at @own-records for the thing's stance record (id stance:<kind>:<identity>, limit up to 100, before_version from next) until next is null; this tool cannot read the person's records itself. Then give the versions of every page together and next from the last page, exactly as records:history returns them. Returns stand: its stand now (the newest version), said, why in the person's own words, by, at, version, earlier (every version before it, oldest first, a tombstone as deleted) and complete (false while next is not null: earlier stands not yet read are unknown); and choices, the stands a person can take. No version, a tombstone or a stand taken back reads stance null with taken_back: silence is not agreement.

values.title: Read Wikimedia Commons file metadata
values.job: Read one Commons file's original license, author, title, source URL and rights metadata for any objective before selecting it for use
values.description: Free, read-only lookup of one Commons File page. Supply its exact File: title from search or another trusted source. The request places the title in an encoded query parameter, follows MediaWiki redirects, and asks for the canonical file page, original media URL, dimensions, MIME type and full extmetadata. No media bytes are downloaded. The extmetadata may contain untrusted HTML; retain it as data and do not render it. A Commons page or media URL does not grant permission to reuse. Run the file-level assessor; BY-SA, NC, ND, missing, ambiguous or conflicting rights are ineligible for selection.

values.title: Rebuild the files derived from my records, or list which are stale (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rebuild the files that are computed from my source record files, or tell me which of them are out of date, without changing anything
values.description: Runs the builders a person's schema declares for files derived from other files (counts, merged lists, tab-separated tables). With --check it writes nothing and lists the stale files, exiting 1 if any; otherwise it rewrites them, or writes them under a folder the person names. Which files, builders and formats come from the schema.

values.title: Receive files pushed by a camera, scanner or printer over FTP (runs on your computer)
values.job: Receive the files a device pushes over FTP, such as a scanner, camera, drone or printer, into a folder on my computer, with nobody there
values.description: Starts a receiver on the person's own computer that speaks FTP (passive mode, and explicit TLS when a certificate is given) for devices that can only push files that way. Each file is streamed into the folder; when it is whole, a note named like the file plus .finished.json is written next to it with content_identity (BLAKE3 of the bytes on disk), byte_length, media_type, finished_at_ms and handed_over_by, and only then is the device told the transfer is done, so a half file is never seen as finished and a device that did not hear the answer sends it again. Only the senders the person puts in the settings file can push (a login, a password and the opaque name written in the notes); there is no built-in sender, and the receiver listens on 127.0.0.1 unless the settings give an address. A path outside the folder, active mode and deleting or renaming a finished file are refused. It runs until it is stopped.

values.title: Count how often the same kind of thing has been flagged, even in different words (runs on your computer)
values.job: When something is flagged again, file it under the earlier flag it repeats, or as a new kind, and say how many times and in how many sessions it has come up
values.description: Give memory_file (where the flagged shapes are kept), rubric_id (which question it was flagged under), excerpt (the flagged text), keep_characters (how much of a new flagged text to store) and optionally session and providers. Once an earlier flag exists you also give plainly_the_same_at (the word overlap, above 0 and at most 1, at which two texts are the same without asking anyone); with providers you also give pass_when_share_correct (the share of the earlier flags a model must file back under themselves before it is trusted) and same_at_least (the confidence at which a model's pick counts as the same kind). None has a default. The same kind in different words is a closed choice over the earlier flags put to a small model, which cannot invent a kind that is not on the list; at most 40 earlier flags, each shown as its first 300 characters, are offered in one question, because that is what fits a small model's reading window.
