With no providers only text at or above your overlap is a repeat, so shapes are overcounted rather than a repeat count inflated. Returns the shape, times, sessions, first_seen and repeat. The count, not louder wording, is what to tell the person.

values.title: Reconcile resource usage report
values.job: Recover an unknown usage charge by reading the exact provider invoice item without sending it again
values.description: Recover an unknown usage charge by reading the exact provider invoice item without sending it again

values.title: Record a step with a customer
values.job: Write down a step with a customer, such as outreach, a reply, a booked call, a purchase, onboarding, a follow-up or feedback, as a record to keep
values.description: Keeps the step in your own customer records, with a new id, its time, a label (a plain default for the kind when none is given), the outcome and each piece of evidence once, and returns it; see-where-each-customer-is reads it back.

values.title: Record a notice for someone
values.job: Record one notification event for the audience the caller names, so it is kept and can be read back; nothing is delivered
values.description: Pass the event: notification_id, kind, conversation_ref, privacy_class, title, body, occurred_at (words) and audience_refs, source_refs, proof_refs (each at least one reference). Optional actions are preserved in the told notice as its offered action definitions, including post:{path,body}, open:{surface_id,...} and press. operationId, transitionId and idempotencyKey are optional. No audience is inferred and no field has a default. If the person saved a notification-event-rules record (kinds, privacy_classes), kind and privacy_class must be among those it lists; with none, any words are accepted. The same event again changes nothing; a different event under the same notification_id is refused. Returns { notification_id, recorded, said }.

values.title: Record a step on the work waiting to be published
values.job: Record a step on the finished work waiting to be published: change a field, link its proof, add a receipt that it was sent, correct it, or hand an action to whatever tool does it
values.description: Give graph (the queue as data; its actions are the person's own) and steps. Each step is { operationId, descriptorId (an action of the graph) or method (update-field, create-record, link-record, unlink-record, append-receipt, correct-record, archive-record or restore-record), recordId, fieldPatch, relationshipPatch, receipt, correction, expectedBasis, actor, observedAt, sources }. An action's patch, params and bindings apply; the record the step is about is offered to its bindings as the source named selected. A step on a local method becomes an operation and is folded into the queue: records get their fields and relationships added to, receipts and corrections are only ever added. A step whose action names a target or a definition is not done here: it comes back in handoffs with its inputs bound, for whichever tool does that job (for example the one that posts). A step that cannot be recorded (no operationId, an action the graph lacks, a method nobody declared) comes back in refused with a code and what was wrong; the other steps are still recorded. Returns operations, handoffs, refused and the queue as it now stands. The queue keeps no state of its own: read it with the tool that sees what is ready.

values.title: Record a spend
values.job: After my AI has paid, add what it spent to today's and the all-time totals
values.description: Adds one paid spend (whole cents) to the spend authority's total for today and for all time, and keeps a record of the payment. One payment is added once: sending the same payment_ref again (the operation_ref when left out) answers the record already kept and adds nothing. It records what was paid; it never authorizes a spend.

values.title: Record a demo of a web page
values.job: Record a web page as a demo video with a large clear pointer, click ripples and zoom, plus marked screenshots of each step for an article or post
values.description: Opens the address in a browser in the cloud and plays your steps on it the way a person would: the pointer travels to each target, clicks, types, scrolls. Returns an MP4 and a GIF with a large drawn pointer, a ripple at every click and the view easing in toward each step, a cover picture at the first click, and one picture per step with its target ringed, an arrow pointing at it and the step's caption. Pauses longer than a second are shortened. Works on any public page, and on a signed-in page when cookies are given; nothing needs installing.

values.title: Record a checklist answer or run its checked steps (runs on your computer)
values.job: Record a checklist answer or run a declared checker or gate, with the required folder change grant
values.description: Uses the same checklist consumer as the read-only gate, but only after the person grants this tool permission to change one folder. It records the person's answer, imports a checker report under the reviewed checker pins, runs the schema's sweeps or gates, holds files only when requested, writes the checklist generated from the person's text, or records and removes source assessments in the existing applications DATA through `library-assess` and `library-remove`. Assessments require current source and work-context pins and preserve other contexts. The existing consumer still checks criteria definitions, BLAKE3 file pins, checker pins, scopes and stale rows; this tool adds no alternate answer or bypass.

values.title: Record what the owner gave back
values.job: Link an owner's receipt to the request it answers
values.description: request_id is a request kept by tool:take-a-request; receipt has ref, owner_ref, title and optionally summary, process_ref, observed_at and raw. Returns { request_id, receipt_ref, linked, said }; the same receipt again changes nothing, a receipt that already answers another request is refused, and a request that is not kept is said in words with nothing linked (linked false).

values.title: Reframe a video to a new shape
values.job: Make a video vertical, square or any other shape, with the frame following the person or action
values.description: Crops the whole video to a new shape (9:16 for a reel by default) with the window following what moves in the picture, and saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Keep measurement history current
values.job: Collect configured operation evidence and save current history directly on a timed or record wake without an AI
values.description: Reads account source configuration, packaged qualified price DATA and prior forecast state, runs the canonical collector and ledger directly, and reads back append-once observations and forecast. It creates no AI job. Missing or stale measurements remain incomplete. Each physical refresh appends real OS CPU, wall and peak-memory observations. Final persistence overhead and monetary cost remain unknown. Replaying a native request does not run a second child.

values.title: Refresh provider price book
values.job: Read the current version of the declared provider price DATA and return provider-qualified unit prices with source revisions
values.description: Reads the dated provider-price-source DATA through its owner. It returns only scalar prices explicitly marked eligible for unconditional evaluation, preserves provider, meter, currency, source and revision, and lists conditional rates as excluded. It does not infer account plans, invoices, usage or billed amounts.

values.title: Register or end my Live Activity
values.job: Keep this iPhone Live Activity token so this account can update or end it
values.description: Pass board_key, the activity push token, app bundle id and environment. ended=true removes the token when the activity ends. Tokens stay private in your own records; the answer never returns them.

values.title: Register my notification device
values.job: Register this device to receive or read my notices
values.description: Pass route (web-push, apns, apns-activity or live) and the address its app received. For web-push, address is {endpoint,keys:{p256dh,auth}}; APNs routes use a hex token. Apple routes also need app (the bundle id); apns-activity also requires attributes_type, the receiving app’s exact Swift ActivityAttributes type and may set environment (sandbox or production). Optional label, can_show, turn_on and present describe this device. The stable device_id is returned; its private address is kept in your records and never returned. Repeating the same registration keeps its id. At most 40 devices are kept.

values.title: Regroup the segments of my plans (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rearrange the pieces of my video plans into groups: a new line to open each group, then the recordings I pick for it in the order I pick, each with an on-screen label if I want one
values.description: For each plan the person names, builds new segments from a shape: head segments kept as they are, then each group's lead segment (given whole, such as a voiced line) followed by existing segments in the order given, each taking the group's segment kind and its label, then tail segments. Indices are the plan's current segment positions (the outline step prints them). Every segment with a recording must be used exactly once, so no recording is dropped by accident. Writes the plans back and returns the seconds of recording in each group. Also: outline, each plan as a numbered list of its segments.

values.title: Regroup a folder tree the way I say, or turn it into groups
values.job: Move folders under other folders by their names, the way I describe it, or turn a tree of folders into groups
values.description: records is the tree as flat records { node_id, parent_id (null for a root), ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }; a node with role group holds others. operation nest-by-intent takes intent { nest: [{ parent_title, child_titles }], scope?: { root_node_id?, applies_to_role?, depth? }, materialize_missing_parents?: { kind } }: titles are matched without case or outer spaces, only the named nodes move, two nodes with one title are a refusal for that row and never a guess, a missing parent is made only when materialize_missing_parents is given (its id from new_parent_ids[title] when you give one), and a row that would put a group inside itself is refused; every other row still applies. Returns records (the tree after), moved, created, refusals ({ row, reason, detail }) and untouched. operation tree-to-groups takes family and returns groups, unplaced (with why), group_count and member_count. It writes nothing: tool:change-my-groups keeps a tree as groups.

values.title: Rehearse a payment schedule in Stripe test mode
values.job: Build a payment schedule in Stripe test mode and see what Stripe says it will charge and when, before a real buyer meets it
values.description: Give payment_schedule and product_name. Only a Stripe test key is accepted (it must start with a test prefix, checked before anything is built); it comes from your held values under a test-key name. Makes test objects only; no real money moves.

values.title: Release a place
values.job: Give a held place back, and offer it to the next person on the waitlist
values.description: Releases one confirmed hold, named by its hold id or by its subject, and by default promotes the first waiting entry that fits the freed place. The same idempotency_key sent again changes nothing. Answers the released hold and the promoted one, if any.

values.title: Remove a saved example
values.job: Remove one saved example this person no longer wants
values.description: id is the example's id from tool:list-saved-examples. Returns { id, removed: true }.

values.title: Remove my notification device
values.job: Stop sending or queueing notices for one of my devices
values.description: Pass the opaque device_id from my-notification-devices. The private address is removed from this person’s records. A device that later registers again receives its own id.

values.title: Render one frame of a square-grid pointillist film (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a film script of square-grid pictures, a grid and a time into one packed frame of coloured cells
values.description: Takes a request file: the grid (columns, rows, gap), the limits and style bounds, the script (target pictures, one style per cell, and timeline segments whose weights are small expressions over time) and a time in seconds. Writes one packed frame file: the cells at that time, each with its colour, opacity and scale, in a fixed little-endian layout that begins PFCF. The same request always gives the same bytes. A request that breaks a limit or names a missing target is refused with a message and nothing is written.

values.title: Pack a square-grid pointillist film as one target-animation file (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a film script into one compact file of its pictures and timeline at a frame rate, for a viewer that works out the frames itself
values.description: Takes an animation request: the grid, limits, style bounds, the script and a frame rate. Writes one target-animation file, whose first bytes are PFAT, holding the target pictures and the timeline (when each picture shows and by what weight) with the frame rate, in a fixed layout a viewer reads directly. The same request always gives the same bytes. A request that breaks a limit is refused with a message.

values.title: Render an edit
values.job: Render a video from an edit decision list: cuts, speed changes, reframing, captions, music and layouts of your files
values.description: Renders one edit in the media-composition edit format (spine.segments of clips with in, out, speed, speed_ramp, reframe, crop, fades; split layouts; subtitles.ass; audio_graph.music_bed; encode width and height). Every source is a file identity from your files. Saves the video in your files.

values.title: Render a run of frames of a square-grid pointillist film (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn one film script into a numbered file of packed frames, one for each time I list
values.description: Takes a sequence file: one frame request (grid, limits, style bounds, script) and the list of times in seconds. Writes frame-0000.pfcf, frame-0001.pfcf and so on into a folder, one for each time in the order given. Each is the packed frame the single-frame tool writes for that time, so the same file always gives the same frames. A request that breaks a limit is refused with a message.

values.title: Change one piece of text in a file
values.job: Change one exact piece of text in a text or code file without sending the whole file: give the words to find and the words to put there
values.description: Give file (a path inside the folder the person granted for change), find (the exact text, as it is in the file, newlines and quotes included) and replace (what to put there; empty removes the found text). The find text must occur exactly once: no match or more than one is refused and nothing is written, so a change that did not happen is never reported as done. Bytes are compared as they are: no pattern, no case folding, no whitespace tolerance. The file is replaced in one step after the full new text is written, keeps its permissions, and is left alone if it changed while the edit was prepared. A path that leaves the folder, goes through a link, is a folder or is not UTF-8 text is refused. Returns the file, its size before and after, and replaced: 1.

values.title: Report how a decision turned out
values.job: Tell Trillion how a decision actually turned out, in my words
values.description: Keeps the person's result of a decided decision: result (met, failed or unknown), summary, answered_by "person" (ask them). A failed result opens the decision for a new one. The same words again are kept once; source_ref and supersedes correct an earlier report. A claim is kept as the caller's claim; nothing here marks it verified.

values.title: Report resource usage
values.job: Report exact reconciled usage once to its purchased subscription, retaining fractional carry and unknown-outcome recovery
values.description: Report exact reconciled usage once to its purchased subscription, retaining fractional carry and unknown-outcome recovery

values.title: Request a booking
values.job: Book someone into one of my open times and keep the booking
values.description: Checks that the start asked for is an open time (same rules as tool:find-open-times, with the person's own booking records as taken), then keeps one booking record. It starts waiting for payment, waiting for the host to confirm, or booked, as the request says. The same idempotency_key answers the booking already kept and books nothing twice. A time that is not open is refused with the open times that day.

values.title: Ask for an action on a connection
values.job: Ask for an action on a connection (for example recording a status), kept as a request record for whatever owns the action to pick up
values.description: Give action (id, target, and optionally operation, definition_id, input_mapping: for each name a selector that reads the input, and status_mapping), input (what the action is given) and optionally correlation_id. Returns the target and payload of the request and the request_id it was kept under (connection-action-request:<correlation_id>). An action with no id or no target comes back as available false with the reason, and nothing is kept.

values.title: Reserve a spend within budget
values.job: Before my AI spends money, check the spend against my budget and reserve it, or refuse it
values.description: Checks one spend (whole cents) against the person's spend authority: it must be turned on and active, and stay inside the daily limit and the per-spend limit. Answers approved and the reason, and writes the check and a reservation the spend carries to the person's records; a refused spend is written too, with its reason. A zero-cost operation is checked and fenced without using the budget. The same idempotency key while its reservation is current answers the first reservation again and counts nothing twice. No authority record means every positive spend is refused.

values.title: Reset today's spend
values.job: When a new day starts (UTC), set my AI's spend today back to zero
values.description: Sets the spend authority's total for today back to zero the first time it runs on a new UTC day, and remembers that day; every later run the same day changes nothing. Answers whether it reset, the day and today's total. Meant to run on a schedule each day.

values.title: Resolve a brand
values.job: Pick the logo variant (wordmark or mark, SVG or PNG) a light or a dark page draws, from a brand kept as list rows
values.description: A brand is the rows of the person's brand list: one row per logo variant (name, brand, family, role wordmark or mark, format svg or png, background such as "black on transparent", url) and one selection row (role selection) naming the family in use. Give a request file: rows (as the list or the record store answers them), tone (light or dark) and, optionally, files_at (a folder with a copy of each asset under its address's file name). Answers the family in use and, for both tones, each role and format's variant (url, row id, and the local file when a copy is there). Making or changing a brand is writing those rows in the person's list; this tool only reads them.

values.title: Resolve a look
values.job: Turn a look's colour, size and font tokens into concrete values and the stylesheet a document carries, with the person's own font faces
values.description: Give a request file: look (the look record as its owner keeps it: tokens of {key, value, css_variable?}) and faces (the person's own font files: family, weight, style, file, relative to the request). Answers the look's concrete values by variable name (--accent-primary, --font-display and the rest), the font families the look names, which faces were written and which files were missing; with --css it writes one stylesheet: a @font-face for each named face, then the look's variables. Nothing about a colour or a font is in the tool: the look and the faces decide.

values.title: Make a raw control byte in my source files searchable again
values.job: Rewrite a raw control character hiding in source files (which makes search tools skip the file as binary) as the escape that means the same character, so the file stays exactly the program it was
values.description: Give files: the paths, inside the folder the person granted for change, of the files to rewrite (names, never a search: finding them is the caller's job, with grep -a). A file is rewritten only when putting every escape back reproduces the original byte for byte and, for a file Node can parse, Node still accepts the result; otherwise it is left alone and the answer says why. Tab, newline and carriage return are never touched. A path that is a link, special file or leaves the folder is refused. Returns rewritten, left_alone and each file's outcome.

values.title: Roll up how much work is finished
values.job: See how much of a body of work is really finished, which items were said done with no proof, and what is blocked
values.description: Counts a work tree from its items' states: an item marked done with nothing anyone can check is counted apart as said done, never as finished, and a percentage typed into the tree is refused rather than trusted. Returns finished out of all items, the share finished, what was said done without proof, what is blocked and by what, and the open items nobody has decided how to build; as "checklist" it also returns the tree as a checklist.

values.title: Route buttons for a trip
values.job: Give one-tap buttons that open the route to a place in each maps app, from a start and through stops on the way
values.description: Give destination, and optionally origin, stops (places on the way) and mode. Answers one button per maps app, each { id, label, url }. Pure: it reaches no network. A new maps app is a row in read-data/get-there.json.

values.title: Pick which of my places holds the answer to what I am looking for (runs on your computer)
values.job: Given something I am looking for and a list of places an answer could live, say which place most likely holds it, how sure that is, and which to try next
values.description: Give looking_for (the text), owners ([{id, holds (what that place keeps), ask (how to look there), for_example: [texts that belong there]}]) providers (the models you can ask) and your three settings: pass_when_share_correct (the share of the owners' own examples a model must file back under the right owner before it is used, above 0 and at most 1; below 1 lets that share of mis-filed examples through), confidence_bands ([{at_least, then}], what to do at which confidence) and band_when_confidence_unknown (what to do when a model gives an answer with no probability). None has a default. The examples are the calibration: a model that files fewer of them back under their own owner than your share is refused, and one that meets it is used even if it mis-files a few. Returns go_to, confidence, what_to_do (the then of the band that confidence falls in), how to look there and then_try, the close seconds, so a near tie is looked at in both places. The model only chooses among the owners you listed, so its worst mistake is the second-best place to look.

values.title: Run a game of Texas Hold'em at a table
values.job: Run a game of Texas Hold'em poker for a table of players: open a table, seat players, deal a hand, take each player's action, and deal the next hand
values.description: Keep the table's saved state (the room) and send it back with one operation each time. open-table makes a table in its lobby from a list of player names and optional settings (starting chips, blinds, blind mode and increase, most players). seat-player adds a player (only in the lobby) or reconnects one by id or name. configure-table changes the settings. start-game posts the blinds and deals every player two cards and the board. player-action is the turn of the seat to act: fold, checkCall, raise (with an amount) or allIn; a round that is over moves on by itself to the next street and then to the showdown, and the answer says in words what happened. next-hand moves the dealer on, raises the blinds by the table's mode and deals again. kick-player removes a player and deals again if a hand was in play. Every deal takes a seed (any whole number), so the same table and seed always deal the same cards. The room holds every player's cards: give a player only what view-a-poker-table-for-a-player returns. One pot is kept per hand: when a player who is all in has put in less than the others, the showdown still pays the whole pot to the best hand. Refuses an action out of turn, a request that does not fit the table's phase, and a room that is not a saved table.

values.title: Run a session step
values.job: Create, change, reschedule, fork, merge, cancel, supersede, confirm, close or ask feedback of a gathering I organize, keeping who came from where
values.description: Applies one named step to a coordination session and answers the next session (or, for supersede, the old one and its successor). The session carries its purpose, candidate times, places and modes, capacity plan, who may see and join it, and a lifecycle state, all as open descriptors the person names. Every step keeps lineage (which sessions it came from) and the provenance of who took part and what they preferred. Steps: create, update, reschedule, fork, merge (two or more sessions), cancel, supersede, confirm, record_no_show, close, request_feedback. A step that is not named is refused. Nothing is saved or sent: keep the answer as a record.

values.title: Save a form
values.job: Keep a form, a list of questions people answer, as one of the person's own records so it can be asked and its answers checked
values.description: Give a form_id, an optional title and presentation, and the questions. Each question needs a questionId and a questionTypeId (a row in the question-type list: text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) and may carry a label, required, options, its own validation rules laid over its type's, and an afterSaved hand-off naming an owner and an action. Saving the same form_id again replaces it. Returns the record id and how many questions were kept.

values.title: Save a member's profile fields
values.job: Save the name, about text or email of a member's profile, changing only the fields given and keeping the rest of the profile
values.description: Give who (the member's id) and fields: any of display_name, about and email, as text. Writes the profile once, reads it back, and answers saved: true with the profile only when the fields read back as written. Fields not given, and anything else the profile holds, stay as they were.

values.title: Save someone's interest in one email update
values.job: Keep the consent of a person who asked for one email if a course becomes available, without sending anything
values.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text) and course ({ id, public_origin as an https site root, consent_text, consent_version, capture_only: true }) and source (optional). Records the address with the words, version, time and source of the agreement as pending. Sends nothing, queues nothing; saving the same agreement again changes nothing. Answers { status: interest_saved, already_saved }.

values.title: Say what was done about a decision
values.job: Tell Trillion my AI did the next step of a decision, or the exact wall it reached
values.description: Keeps, with the decision generation it carried out, that its next action was done (state done) or the exact wall reached (state wall: the file, field, refused command or missing credential), in what_happened.

values.title: Say why each technique works, in words every other technique shares (runs on your computer)
values.job: Describe each technique I kept by why it works, what it changes, what it needs and what it produces, in shared words that let it combine with every other technique whatever medium it came from
values.description: For each technique row, a writer model proposes its mechanism (why it works, never naming a medium), the properties it changes (operates_on), its needs and what it produces, and the medium it came from, shown the nearest existing terms so it reuses them. Every proposed term then goes through the vocabulary's admission rule: the same words, or a term at least reuse_at close in meaning, is the same term (kept as an alias); a term below new_below is new; in between the writer judges. Each need is tagged with its closest property so one technique's change joins another's need. Returns the rows' fields with the writer's own proposal, the vocabulary to keep for the next call, what merged into what, and any row not read. Without a vocabulary it starts one from the measured lines.

values.title: Schedule the next review of something being learned
values.job: Work out when a flashcard, drill, passage or any other thing being learned should come back, from how well the person just recalled it
values.description: Give the grade the person just gave, the item's state from its last review (leave it out the first time) and the person's own spacing policy: the starting ease, the ease floor, the gap after the first and the second success, the recall quality below which an item lapses, and a map from each grade word to a recall quality between 0 and 1. Returns the item's next state to keep and hand back at the next review, when it is due (a time and a date), whether it lapsed and the quality the grade mapped to. The grade is an open word the policy defines. A grade the policy does not list counts as a total lapse and is marked grade_in_policy false. With prompt_id and schedule_id it also returns the next schedule record to keep (the state, the day it is due and state due). The policy may be given as policy or found among rows by policy_kind. There is no default policy: a missing policy or field is refused with its name.

values.title: Schedule the later payments in Stripe
values.job: After a buyer has paid at the door, set up the payments that come later (a week on, a month on, then every month) in Stripe
values.description: Give payment_schedule (charges with amount_cents as text and days_after_signup, and an optional repeat), customer_ref, product_name and signed_up_at_unix_seconds. The first payment is taken by the checkout, not here. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Keep score of a match point by point
values.job: Keep the score of a match (tennis, pickleball, padel or any game whose scoring a person writes as a rule): start a match, give a point to a side, undo the last point, type in a score, and link a match to a tournament, schedule, bracket, standings or leaderboard
values.description: Every answer is records for the caller to write; nothing is kept here. A game's scoring is a rule row (scoring-rule: ruleId, label, scoringModel with scoreUnit game or point, setsToWin, gamesToWinSet, tiebreakAt, pointsToWinTiebreak, winBy and, for a labelled ladder, pointLabels and advantageLabel). Rules for tennis, pickleball and padel come with the tool; pass scoring_rules to use the person's own. start-match takes a rule id, singles or doubles and the players of each side, and gives the match record and its first score event. score-point takes the match's records (rows) and the side that won the point, replays the log, and gives the next score event with the right sequence number: a game is won on the rule's points with its lead, a tiebreak counts to the rule's target, games make a set, sets make the match, and a point after the match is won is refused. undo-point writes the score before the latest event as a new event, because the log only grows. record-score writes a score the scorer typed in (whole numbers at or above 0). link-context writes a context link for a tournament, schedule row, bracket match, standing or leaderboard. A tap made offline is written with local_state pending-offline; spectators do not see it until it is confirmed or reconciled.

values.title: Score answers and pick a segment
values.job: Score a lead's or respondent's answers with your rules and pick their segment and follow-up, such as hot, warm or not ready
values.description: Adds up points for each answer by your rules (a value worth points, at least or at most a number, equal to a value, long enough, answered at all, one of a list), keeps subtotals under labels you name, picks the segment whose starting score the total reaches, and returns that segment's title, meaning, next step and follow-up steps. Every weight, threshold and follow-up is yours to set; nothing about a good lead is built in.

values.title: Score a questionnaire's answers
values.job: Score the answers to a questionnaire, flipping reverse-keyed items and filing each item under its subscale
values.description: Takes a questionnaire (its id, the response scale, the subscales and their item ids, which items are reverse-keyed) and a person's responses. Answers one scored fact per response: the response, the scored value (a reverse-keyed item is reflected on the scale: min + max - response), its subscale and whether it was reversed. A questionnaire not marked validated, or marked banned, is refused: it will not be scored.

values.title: Scout an opponent from the notes on file
values.job: Look up an opponent: list the people scouted, and pull together everything on file about one (what they are good and weak at, what worked and failed against them, their style and ratings) and which notes are trusted enough to plan from
values.description: Give the person's records and an operation. search lists every subject that is not the person themself, with how many reports and profiles are on file and how many tactics worked and failed against them. profile (with subject_id) joins the subject's reports (player-report evidence), profiles (profile-projection) and tactic outcomes into one view: strengths, weaknesses, strategies that worked and failed, style labels, ratings (any name, numbers 0 to 100; a value outside that is left out, not guessed), public and private reports apart, and the outcomes of tactics from earlier plans. It also says which reports a plan may use: the confidence policy is { minimumConfidence, missingConfidenceIsUsable }, given as confidence_policy or as an evidence-confidence-policy record in the rows, and with none no report is usable (every one waits for review). A report's confidence is its source's, else its own. Nothing here names a sport: the words for ratings, styles and facts are the ones in the records.

values.title: Seal a paid file

The key is handed to this run on a private pipe and is never in the record or the answer. A buyer then gets the file only through tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link and tool:open-a-paid-file-for-a-buyer.

values.title: Search Internet Archive
values.job: Search Internet Archive for books, articles, audio, concerts, films, images and other primary sources, with license and collection filters and source provenance for any objective
values.description: Free, read-only Internet Archive Advanced Search. Supply Archive's query syntax; the request always adds NOT access-restricted-item:true and returns a bounded page with identifier, title, creator, date, year, media type, collection, licenseurl, rights, description and access-restriction metadata when indexed. Query examples: (title:tennis AND mediatype:movies); (creator:Example AND collection:georgeblood); (mediatype:audio AND licenseurl:*creativecommons.org*). A license URL or unrestricted access is evidence to inspect, not proof of permission for your intended use. Preserve the item identifier and source metadata; missing or ambiguous rights remain unknown. The Archive's George Blood 78rpm description limits use to research, teaching and private study and says copyright was not transferred; concert recordings also need item-specific rights review. Search results only; this does not download or save media.

values.title: Search the public web
values.job: Search the public web for a creator, a topic or a question, and get back at most ten results with the address each one cites
values.description: Sends one query (1 to 500 characters) to a public web search and reads the one results page. Returns at most ten results, each with title, url (the page the result points to, never the search engine's own address), a snippet in description, and a citation { url, retrieved_via }. It follows no result and signs in nowhere; to read a result, read its page with the tool that reads a public page.

values.title: Search treg's catalog of paid endpoints
values.job: Find the external endpoints that can do a job (backlinks for a domain, a company's job openings, a brand's ads, a channel's posts) and what each costs, before spending anything
values.description: Searches treg's public catalog by the job in plain words and answers its matches, each with its id, what it does, its method, its inputs and its price (cost.usd per cost.unit, and whether it is billed per call or per success). Free and needs no account or token: nothing is spent. Read one match in full with tool:read-a-treg-endpoint-and-its-price, then call it with tool:call-a-treg-endpoint. A job usually has several providers at very different prices; choose by the inputs you actually hold first, then by how often each works, then by price.

values.title: Search Wikimedia Commons files
values.job: Find real images and other source files on Wikimedia Commons for any objective by searching for the exact place, object, event or subject
values.description: Free, read-only Commons File-page discovery for real media needed by any objective. Returns a bounded page of file titles and canonical file-page URLs, without downloading media or requesting expensive license metadata for every search result. Search Commons first when the task needs a real place, object or event. Read exact file metadata for a candidate, then run the file-level reuse/credit assessor before reuse selection. Only explicit public-domain/CC0/CC-BY metadata under the requested policy is eligible; BY-SA/NC/ND/unknown or conflicting rights are excluded. Source metadata remains a qualified assertion, not blanket permission.

values.title: See how one file changed

values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and file_path (the file, relative to the folder). Returns diff, git's text of the difference from the last commit. A project with no commit yet has no last commit to compare with, and git's own words say so. Changes nothing.

values.title: See what changed in a project

values.description: Give folder, the full path of a project folder the person has let this tool use. values.title: How each post did

values.description: Give observations (each place's own counts for a post, read with that place's tools: { post_id, account_id, metrics: { name: number }, observed_at } or { platform_post_id, account_id?, metrics }), visits and conversions (as tool:break-down-visits-and-sales takes them: { visitor, project?, signals: { utm_content, ... } } and { visitor, project?, value? }) and optionally post_ids. Reads the person's post records and returns posts: one row per place a post was published to that has a count, a visit or a conversion, with post_id, account_id, title, platform_post_id, url, metrics, observed_at, brought ({ visits, conversions, value }, only what was counted) and evidence. A visit counts for a place only when its utm_content is exactly that post's post_id (the post went to one place), the place's own post id, or post_id::account_id; a token that could name several places counts for none. Nothing missing is shown as zero.

values.title: See the ink marks drawn on a page or picture
values.job: Work out which ink marks are showing on one page, picture or other space, after later marks hid, restyled, reordered, copied or merged earlier ones
values.description: Give the mark operations (every drawing step ever recorded, in any space), the mark styles they name and the space to look at. Marks are only ever added; a later operation changes what shows by naming an earlier mark in its effects (hide_refs, style_ref_by_ref, order_by_ref, copy_ref_by_ref, merge_refs). The answer lists, in drawing order, each visible mark with its points, whether its shape is closed and its style (the style it names, with any fields the mark carries itself laid over it), plus the refs that are hidden and the operations that drew nothing. Operations for other spaces are left out. Rows may be bare, wrapped as { payload } or stored as { value_json } text. Nothing is written.

values.title: What is on a drive

values.title: See what runs on its own

values.description: Give now_ms, wakes (the causes tool rows declare: [{tool, id, on, budget}]), book (the engine's wake book record, or null) and, optionally, stamps (each watched resource's newest change stamp) and late_after_ms. values.title: See what finished work is ready to publish

Records come in graph.records or in recordAtoms ({ id, title, group_id, fields, relationships, action_ids, receipt_ids, issue }), receipts in graph.receipts or receiptAtoms. Optional selectedRecordId, status and issues. values.title: See where each customer is

values.description: Give rubrics_file ({providers: [...], rubrics: [...]} on your computer) and optionally passes (default 2). Every model on offer is asked every calibration case of every rubric. Returns held_access_refs (the one list every gate here asks), the episodes behind it, any allowance limits, and problems (events that gave no effect, and why).
