values.title: Send each post at its time
values.job: When the person's posts change, set each post that is set to go at its time to be sent then, to each of its destinations, by that place's send row
values.description: Runs on its own once the person switches on its wake (at-its-time): each time their posts change, it reads the changed posts, and for each one set to go at its time (tool:set-a-post-to-go-at-its-time) it sets one run of the place's send row (tool:send-a-post-to-<place>) per destination still to be sent, at the post's scheduled_for. That run sends only while the post is still set to go as it was then, so a post taken back, changed or set again sends nothing at the old time. It sends nothing itself, polls nothing and keeps nothing. Its rights are the ones the sends it sets need (the person's posts, their connections and their files), because each send reaches only what this wake was granted. Returns set (each post, destination, send row and time), left_out (each send not set, with why) and said.

values.title: Send prepared batches into my lists, resuming where I stopped (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put the batches of rows I prepared into my lists one at a time, wait and retry when the list is busy, split a batch that is too big, and remember what was already sent
values.description: Reads a config the person gives (the command that writes rows into a list, optionally a command to wake the list first, the errors that mean wait and retry, the errors that mean the batch is too big, the waits and the order). Sends each batch of an export in order, counts what the command kept, writes progress to a status file and skips what it already sent when run again. A batch counts only when every row was kept; a refusal stops the run and the status file names the batch and the reason.

values.title: Update my Live Activity
values.job: Start, update or end the one Live Activity board for running work
values.description: Pass a stable update_id, board_key and up to four items. Push-to-start uses each device’s registered attributes_type; missing or invalid registration refuses delivery without guessing a native type. Running items update existing activity tokens or push-to-start when none has returned yet; an empty running set ends active tokens. Apple acceptance does not prove the person saw it. Reusing update_id returns its durable result; unknown outcomes are never sent again. Definite failures may be retried with retry_failed=true.

values.title: Send a recorded notification to my devices
values.job: Send one already-recorded notice through my registered Apple devices
values.description: Pass notification_id and the audience reference that the recorded event names. The notice is first kept in told-the-person; APNs and browser push attempts are recorded before sending, accepted is never treated as read, and an unknown network result is not blindly retried. Set retry_failed only after a definite failure. Device-pull registrations get the notice queued for their next read; per-device route results identify which registered devices received or may read it.

values.title: Set a product's customer target
values.job: Set how many customers I want for a product, so progress toward that target can be tracked
values.description: Keeps the target in your own customer records (one per product; setting it again replaces it) and returns it; see-where-each-customer-is counts the product's customers against it.

values.title: Set a post to go at its time
values.job: Set an approved post to go out at its scheduled time, once it is ready for every place it is going; nothing is sent now
values.description: Give post_id of an approved post whose scheduled_for is still ahead. It is checked for every destination (as tool:check-a-post does); when ready, its status becomes scheduled and it waits for its time, and when not, it stays approved and said gives what each place is missing. Nothing is sent by this tool. tool:take-back-a-post makes a scheduled post a draft again. Returns post_id, status, post, ready and said.

values.title: Set up someone I pay in Stripe
values.job: Make a Stripe account for a person I pay, or check one, and get their Stripe onboarding page and what Stripe still needs from them
values.description: Give settings ({ country, controller, capabilities }), owner, payee_ref, refresh_url and return_url, or an existing account id. Returns the account, whether it can be paid and what is due, and the onboarding address. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Set up Stripe payment links
values.job: Make Stripe hold one lasting payment link for every priced option of my offers, with the buyer plan page and my percent-off codes
values.description: Give owner (a name that marks the Stripe objects as yours) and after_payment_url. Reads your offers and code adjustments from your records. Safe to run again: prices, links, codes and the plan page are found, not made twice; links for options you no longer sell stop taking payments. Webhook endpoints are not made here (Stripe shows a signing secret only once); add yours in the Stripe dashboard and keep its secret in your held values. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Settle a triage of one incoming item
values.job: Keep the decision made about one incoming item only if it holds up against the person's priorities and dispositions, and otherwise hold the item back
values.description: Give the same item, priorities, dispositions and least confidence you were briefed with, and answers: a list holding your one answer ({disposition_ref, confidence, rationale, target_ref, and objective with acceptance_criteria where the disposition needs them}). Returns and keeps one decision record per item and version. If there are no priorities, no answer or more than one, the confidence is not a number, is outside 0 to 1 or is under the least, the rationale or objective has more words than max_words allows, the disposition is not listed, or a needed objective is missing, the decision is the fallback disposition, blocked, with each reason in words. blocked is false only where the disposition's row says blocked_default is false. It does nothing else; whoever owns the disposition acts on the decision.

values.title: Settle shared resource cost
values.job: Allocate one verified supplier invoice among its attributed excess users under purchased limits, with separate platform expense, explicit funding gaps and exact subcent amounts; nothing is sent to a payment provider
values.description: Allocate one verified supplier invoice among its attributed excess users under purchased limits, with separate platform expense, explicit funding gaps and exact subcent amounts; nothing is sent to a payment provider

values.title: Make a decision safe to share
values.job: Make a decided decision safe to show strangers: the plain privacy pass with the person's own private terms, then a second model's re-identification check bound to the exact words
values.description: In three turns. With only decision_id: the decision's facts with every private term already redacted, and how to rewrite them in general terms. With rewrite: the plain privacy pass (tools/learn-from-everyones-results) runs on it with the person's own private terms (their never-publish list rows and the proper names in the decision) and must find nothing; then reidentification, the whole answer tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict gave for the rubric and content this tool names, must be accepted and bound to exactly this rewrite. Only then is the entry kept on the decision as shared and answered with the pool tool to send it to (tool:add-a-shared-situation). Nothing leaves the person's records here.

values.title: Show which offers a buyer may see
values.job: Work out which of my offers to show a buyer given what they already hold, with my upsell and already-owns rules
values.description: Give held_access_refs (what the buyer holds now). Offers and eligibility rules come from your records (or pass offers and rules); an offer with no rule is always shown, and a refund that shrinks what is held reverses every decision.

values.title: Sign someone up for an email course (sends through Amazon SES)
values.job: Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others
values.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional), provider (amazon-ses) and region (the SES region). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Records the consent with its words, version, time and source; queues each later lesson at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons-with-amazon-ses sends them); sends lesson 1; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.

values.title: Sign someone up for an email course (sends through Resend)
values.job: Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others
values.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional) and provider (resend). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Records the consent with its words, version, time and source; queues each later lesson at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons-with-resend sends them); sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.

values.title: Sort reservations by status
values.job: Group my reservations (tables, rooms, visits) by status, the ones that need me first
values.description: Groups reservations by status, with the statuses the person lists in attention_order first and in that order, then any other status in the order seen. Reads the rows given, or the person's own reservation records when none are given. Rows may use camelCase or snake_case; a row with no id is dropped. Also lists the reservations that name no policy.

values.title: Split a long document of many items into one document per item
values.job: Turn long markdown documents that hold many numbered items (rules, lessons, questions) into one document per item with its fields in frontmatter, so each item is a row of a folder list
values.description: Reads the documents a mapping names and finds the items by the mapping's heading and table-row patterns, merging pieces of one item from several documents. Each item becomes `<id>.md`: frontmatter (id, then the fields the mapping captures, groups and flags) and its parts under headings. Text that belongs to no item is kept in one leftover file per document. Every line read is placed (the report counts both), and pieces with the same words are written once. It refuses a folder that is not empty. It knows no item kind: everything comes from the mapping.

values.title: Choose files for the next commit
values.job: Add chosen files in a project on the person's computer to the next commit
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and paths (the files to add, relative to the folder). Returns the project's changes after it, as tool:see-changes-in-a-project does. The files themselves are not changed.

values.title: Start a decision with my method
values.job: Start a decision my AI will make with my method: what is being decided, the facts, and the options
values.description: Opens a decision in the person's own records from a source_id (the same source always opens the same decision; the same input again is that decision, different input is refused), its goal, its evidence ({ref, claim}, each ref unique) and at least two options ({id, label}), under the method named or the person's default (their Methods list). The decision keeps the exact method it was opened with. Returns case_id and the first question.

values.title: Start a run of a recipe: leave its steps as a job for my AI
values.job: When a recipe of mine is started, by a wake I switched on or by a call, put its steps and its input in my own records as one job waiting for my AI, once per firing
values.description: Every recipe row runs as this tool (the recipes' row source names it in invoke_with), with the recipe's id in input.row. It reads that recipe from the person's own list of workflows and the rows of its steps, or else from the public recipes folder (the person's own row wins when both hold the id), and writes one record of kind ai-job, id ai-job:<recipe id>:<request key>, holding status waiting, the recipe id and label, its steps, the input it was started with and the wake cause that started it. It does no step itself, schedules nothing and keeps nothing else. The AI that next connects to the person's records lists ai-job records with status waiting, does the oldest, and writes status done with its result. A firing or a call that comes again with the same request key finds its job and writes nothing.

values.title: Start a Stripe checkout
values.job: Make the Stripe hosted checkout page a buyer is sent to, for one of my offers, with my own Stripe account
values.description: Prices the sale as price-a-sale does, needs the buyer agreement in consent (billing and legal), and success_url and cancel_url for where the buyer lands afterwards (they only land the buyer; they never grant access). Returns the address to send the buyer to. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Start a Stripe checkout that pays someone else
values.job: Make a Stripe hosted checkout whose money goes to a person I pay, with my fee kept back
values.description: Give offer_id, price_option_id, payer_ref, payee_account (their Stripe account id), fee ({ percent }), success_url and cancel_url. The platform fee is worked out in whole cents and never above the amount. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Move a person through a guided tour, quiz or spotlight
values.job: Work out where a person is in a guided tour, walkthrough, spotlight or branching quiz after they start, go on, answer, go back, jump to a step or restart
values.description: Give the tour (an ordered list of steps with an entry step; a step may route by the person's answer with a branch_map of by_answer routes and a default_next) and one action: start or restart, advance (with the person's answer when the step asks one), back, or jump (with step_id). The cursor from the last answer goes back in with every action but start and restart. The answer is the new cursor (current_step_id, the history of steps visited, and status active or complete), the whole current step exactly as the tour author wrote it (what it shows and where it points are the author's and pass through untouched) and whether the tour has finished. Going on from the last step, or along a route to a step the tour does not have, finishes the tour and the cursor stays on the last step shown. Going back undoes exactly, even across a branch. Nothing is kept between calls; the caller keeps the cursor.

values.title: Link records into people and stage each
values.job: Link records that share a key into one person and give each person the highest stage their records reach
values.description: Takes records and a config. Records that share a value at any key path are one person (the same value at two different paths never links). Each person gets the highest-ranked stage any of their records reaches by the stage rules (exists, equals or greater-than tests on a field), the first source by time, the sum of a value field, and a confidence word: the identified word when any strong key is present, the anonymous word otherwise. Answers the people best stage first. Key paths, stage rules, the base stage and the confidence words are all in the config.

values.title: Stop sending an email course to someone who unsubscribed
values.job: End a person's email course subscription from the token in their unsubscribe link, so no further lesson is sent
values.description: Give token (the unsubscribe token in the link the person was sent). Marks the subscription unsubscribed with the time; an unknown or already used token answers unsubscribed too. Answers { status: unsubscribed }.

values.title: Put my finished cuts one after another into one reel to watch (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put all my finished cuts into one video to watch in a row, with a short card naming each one before it, and tell me where each starts
values.description: Strings the cuts the person lists, in their order, into one reel without re-encoding them, with a plain text card of the seconds and words the person gives between each two, made at the first cut's frame size and rate. Returns where each cut starts in the reel (and writes it as text when asked); a listed file that does not exist is named and left out.

values.title: Submit answers to a form
values.job: Check a person's answers against a saved form and, when they are all valid, record them with the score and segment they earn and any follow-up the form hands to its owner
values.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and answers (questionId to value), and optionally submission_id (for a form answered again and again, so each time is kept) and answered_at. The answers are checked against the saved form as check-form-answers does. If any is invalid nothing is written and the first to fix is returned. Otherwise one write keeps an answer fact for each answer the form asks about, one segment assignment (the score rows and segment rows that apply to this form pick the segment; the segment's follow-up sequence is returned), and one request record for each question whose afterSaved names an owner and action, with the answers filled into its input.

values.title: Tag a Stripe subscription
values.job: Add notes (metadata) to a buyer Stripe subscription without changing the ones already there
values.description: Give subscription_id and metadata (text values). Only keys you give are added or changed, and nothing is written when nothing changes. Uses your Stripe key from your held values.

values.title: Take a request
values.job: Keep one request that arrived, as decided, and ask the owner who should act on it
values.description: request is what arrived: request_id, source_ref, atom_ref, text, origin_ref, optionally message_ref, content_revision and at. Its origin_ref must be one the person accepts (an intake-origins record with id intake-origins:accepted). decision is the caller's: disposition and reason, and hand_to_owner true with owner_ref (an active intake-owner record) and acceptance_criteria when an owner should act; hand_off, required when hand_to_owner is true, names what the owner is asked to run (action_ref or action_refs, optional id, input and copy rows). existing_task_ref is refused (current_task_executor_not_verified): a task reference says nothing about who runs it now. max_text_chars (default 65536) bounds the kept text: a longer text is kept cut to it, or, when it is being handed to an owner, held back. Returns { status, request_id, problems, owner_request, said }. status is handed, recorded, deferred (nothing is kept because the owner is not on file or the text is too long; take it again once fixed), already-taken (the same request again changes nothing) or refused (no accepted origins on file, incomplete, origin not accepted, a decision that names an existing task, or the same id from another source, message, place or version).

values.title: Take back a post
values.job: Take back a post that is waiting for its time and that nothing was sent for, so it is a draft again and goes nowhere
values.description: Give post_id of a scheduled post nothing was sent for. It becomes a draft again, so its time sends nothing. A post already on its way cannot be taken back. Returns post and said.

values.title: Take me to the thing that needs me
values.job: Take a person to the thing that needs them: give the screen to open on one waiting card, the arrangement that puts it beside what the caller names, the walkthrough that points at the card's own control and the notice that links to both, or say in plain words that nothing is waiting there or it opens outside their places
values.description: Give thing (a card id from the answer of tool:what-is-waiting-on-me, or a batch section's key, batch: and the section id), waiting (that answer: { sections: [{ cards }] } or { cards }, a card { id, source?, title?, action?, address?, points_at? }), screens (the caller's rows, { path_prefix, tool_id, route_input_from_query?: [names] }, one for each address path that opens a screen) and own_origins (the origins whose links open inside the person's own places). Answers { taken: false, said } when the thing is not waiting now or its link leads outside those origins or to no screen; otherwise { taken: true, screen: { tool_id, route_input }, arrangement (one pane, or a split with beside, its id the thing's key), tour (when steps are given: each step points at the card's own control, points_at filled with the item id, else a fallback selector; started by name, finished when the card's ids are completed), notice (when say is given), open (the address that opens the arrangement and tour), said }. It saves no arrangement or tour and sends no notice: whoever keeps those does that with what this returns.

values.title: Tally a community's match picks
values.job: Show how a community picked the winner of each match (the split by choice), what the result was, and how one person's own picks turned out
values.description: Give the records of the matches (pick-match: matchId, label, startsAt, choices of { choiceId, label }), the picks (match-pick: matchId, pickerId, choiceId, createdAt) and the results (match-pick-result: matchId, winningChoiceId, summary, resolvedAt). Each match comes back by start time with every choice's count and whole percent (rounded, so the percents may not add to 100), the winning choice once there is a result (the latest result record counts) and, with picker_id, that picker's own choice. A picker who changed their pick counts once, for the latest pick. With picker_id the answer also lists that picker's picks newest first with the match and choice in words, the result summary, whether the pick was right once the match has a result, and whether a later pick replaced it. Free picks only: this tool reads records and moves no money. To keep wording out of a prompt or a result summary (for example talk of money), check the text with tool:check-pick-copy and the list the person gives.

values.title: Tell a judge it was wrong, so it is tested on that case from now on (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a verdict that was wrong into a known case in my rubrics file, so every model is tested against it from the next calibration on
values.description: Give rubrics_file, rubric_id, should_have_been (true, false, a number or one of the options), and either about (the text) or log_file (a verdict log written by tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict, the last verdict for that rubric is used), and optionally because. Adds one labelled case and stops: it does not change the question, the line or the model. The same text twice is not added twice (a different label corrects the earlier one). Adding cases makes a rubric harder to pass, which is the point: a model that cannot handle the new case stops being chosen for the question.

values.title: Follow one thing I point at through a video clip and outline it in every frame (runs on your computer)
values.job: Follow an object or a person I pointed at through a clip and get its outline in every frame
values.description: Takes a video, a stretch of up to 30 seconds, the second at which the person pointed, and one to 32 points on that frame, each marked as inside the object or outside it. It runs a point-prompted SAM 2 video model on the person's own computer and writes, in a new folder, a lossless grayscale mask video (mask.mkv), one mask picture and one transparent preview picture per frame, and result.json with how many pixels the object covers in each frame. A frame where the object is hidden has an empty mask: it is kept empty, not filled with a guess. If nothing is found at the pointed spot the run fails and says to choose another point. Frames never leave the computer, the model is read from the local cache and never downloaded, and the video is only read.

values.title: Transcribe a recording with a time for every word, and repair Whisper loops (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a recording into a transcript with a time for every word, and fix the places where the transcription got stuck repeating one sentence
values.description: Runs the audio-transcription package's own transcribe-audio.py on the person's own computer: the recording (audio, or video with sound) is decoded to 16 kHz mono and read by whisper.cpp, and the answer is the package's result: language, full text, segments, and words with a start, an end and a timing_source that says whether the time came from the engine's token times, from the segment's bounds or from an even split of the segment. The seam adds the recording's length. Whisper sometimes gets stuck and writes one sentence again and again over minutes of real speech or silence. find-loops finds those stretches (a sentence said four or more times that fills half a segment, or a segment that repeats the one before). repair merges the ones that are close, hears again only those windows with the earlier text not carried in (whisper.cpp -mc 0) and splices the new words in at their true seconds. A sentence that still loops is taken out and kept in removed_hallucinated, so nothing disappears silently. Nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

values.title: Turn a drawn stroke into a line, rectangle or polygon
values.job: Turn the points of a drawn stroke into the shape the chosen drawing tool makes: freehand ink, a straight line, a rectangle or a regular polygon or ellipse
values.description: Give the drawing tool's own row and the stroke's points in order. The tool's mapper picks the shape: passthrough keeps every point, segment keeps the first and last, polygon with corners gives the four corners of the rectangle between first and last point, polygon with sides N gives N points on the ellipse inscribed in that rectangle (3 to 18 reads as a regular polygon, many as an ellipse). A mapper of any other kind keeps the stroke as drawn. The answer also says whether the tool closes its figure and whether it is an eraser (an eraser appends a hide effect instead of ink). Points are [x, y] or { values: [x, y] }.

values.title: Turn frames into slides
values.job: Turn a board's presentation frames into slides in story order, one page each, as SVG, printable HTML, a PDF and a picture of every page
values.description: Give a request file: board (its items: a presentation frame is an item with extra.presentationFrame.order, and every item centred inside it is on that slide), title, look_values and look_css (from tool:resolve-a-look, so any colour or font written as a variable name such as --accent-primary is the look's own), assets (name to file or https address; an item with src asset:<name> draws it, a file carried as its bytes), frames (the frame memberIds to make, in order; absent: every frame) and words_from (a filled word template from tool:fill-a-word-template: its tokens name the item they belong to, and that item's words become the filled ones). Text may show a look value as {{--name}} (a swatch label), so the value is never copied. An item may carry its own type: extra.fontSize, fontWeight, fontFamily, lineHeight, textInset and charWidth, and extra.imageFit contain for a logo. Every frame is one page of the frame's size. Writes slides/NN.svg and deck.html (which keeps the slide words as inert records a word template can be made from); with --pdf the PDF, with --pictures pages/NN.png. A variable the look lacks, an unknown asset or a frame of another size stops the run and says which.

values.title: Take files out of the next commit
values.job: Take chosen files in a project on the person's computer out of the next commit, leaving the files as they are
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and paths (the files to take out, relative to the folder). Returns the project's changes after it. The files keep every edit they have; only their place in the next commit changes.

values.title: See a poker table as one player may see it
values.job: Show a poker table as one player may see it: the board, the pot, each seat, what that player may do now and only that player's own cards
values.description: Give a saved table (the room run-a-poker-table returned) and, optionally, the id of the player looking. Returns the phase and street, hand number, pot, current bet, minimum raise and blinds, the board as it is dealt so far, the label of the next street, every seat (chips, bet, dealer and blind marks, whose turn it is, folded, all in, out, connected), the four betting controls (fold, check or call with what a call costs, raise with its minimum, all in) switched on only for the player whose turn it is, that player's own two cards, every player's cards once the hand is over and never before, and the hand's result with the winners' names. With no player id it is the view of a spectator and holds no private cards. Refuses a room that is not a saved table and a player who is not at it.

values.title: Record a voice take of every line my plans have a voice read (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a voice recording of every line in my plans that a voice reads aloud, with the voice I choose, and keep each one so it is made only once
values.description: Finds every segment whose piece is a voiced line in the person's piece table, and for each line with no take yet runs the person's speaker commands (voice.say: any text-to-speech and finishing chain, each command filled with the line, a file of it, a folder of its own and the take to write). Each take is kept as <name>.wav beside <name>.txt holding its exact words, named by the BLAKE3 of the words, so a line is found by what it says. Comes with a Kokoro speaker (do-work/say_line_kokoro.py: mlx-audio on Apple Silicon, trimmed to the words, a soft end and a little room tone).

values.title: Walk a sales funnel
values.job: Read a sales funnel's offers and see the price a buyer is shown and where an outcome such as buying or declining takes them next
values.description: Reads the funnel records a person keeps: the funnel graph, its offer nodes (each with an offer, a price and the outcomes that move a buyer on), and the price experiments run on them. Gives back the whole flow in the order a buyer meets it, the price shown on the entry offer (the winning version of a settled price experiment when one applies, else the offer's own price, with which record decided it), the step a buyer is on, and where a named outcome takes them (an outcome that leads to no node ends the flow). It can also order a page's call-to-action links, main one first. Outcomes and offers are the person's own words; nothing is built in.

values.title: Walk through an app like its users
values.job: Check that people can still do what they come to my app for after a change: walk each journey in a real browser, keep pictures, a log and a video, and tell my coding agent exactly what to fix, then check the fix
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer (so it reaches local, VPN and Tailscale addresses the computer reaches) and walks each journey in a browser context of its own. A journey is DATA: { id, goal, expect_every_step?, steps: [{ id, intent, do?, expect? }] }. `do` is one action a person takes: goto { url }, click { target }, fill { target, value }, press { key }, upload { target, files } (files relative to fixtures_folder) or wait { ms }; a target names a control as a person sees it: { role, name } or { role, name_contains }, with nth when several match. `expect` lists what must then be true: text_visible, text_absent, url_contains, title_contains { text }; control_present, control_absent { target }; field_value { target, equals }; checked { target, equals }; no_console_errors; no_failed_requests. A step with no `do` (or a learned action whose control has gone) stops as needs_decision with the actions the page offers, as `do` objects to copy back; the AI chooses one and runs again with it in `learned` or in the journey. Answers the report: verdict, each step with its pictures (the touched control boxed and numbered), console errors and failed requests, `fixes` (for each failed step: what was expected, what was there, the steps that reproduce it and the evidence), `decisions_needed`, `learned` (the actions that passed, to replay next time) and, given previous_report, `compared_with_previous` (fixed, still_failing, newly_failing, still_passing, now_passing). Every run walks every step again; nothing passes because it passed before. Evidence is written under evidence_folder (or a new folder in the computer's temporary folder) and report_file names the saved report.

values.title: List what can do steps
values.job: List everything that can do a step for a person, with what each covers and what it costs, and the reasons a step may stay the person's
values.description: Give doers (the caller's own list) and optionally only_a_person. Answers each doer's id, label, the needs it covers, cost, and whether it spends money or reaches others, and the reasons. It is the list a caller chooses `needs` words from for tool:who-does-each-step.

values.title: Show everything waiting on me
values.job: Show everything waiting on this person that only they can do, gathered from every place it is kept: what their AIs asked them for, drafts to approve, work that is stuck, a sign-in, a decision
values.description: Give sources (the places that hold things up, the person's own list: { id, label, title, where?, detail?, opens?, at?, most? }) and found (the records of each source, { <source id>: [{ id, value }] }, read from the person's account by the caller). A record waits when every where test holds (equals, in, present or absent on a field). Answers one card per waiting record, newest first, with the title, detail and the address it opens read from the record by the source's templates, a count for each source, and a sentence. A source with no records handed in is told as unread, never as nothing waiting. The tool reads no records and names no source: a new place is a new row.

values.title: Who agreed to get which emails
values.job: Show who agreed to get which email list, in what words, when and from where, and whether they still do
values.description: Optional list (one list's id) and status (active, pending or unsubscribed). Reads every consent in my records: email courses and one-update interest lists. Returns people [{ email, list, kind: course or update, status, consented_at, consent_text, consent_version, source }], agreed (the addresses that can be sent to now, each once) and said. It changes nothing; hand agreed to a send tool as recipients.

values.title: Say who should do each step of a plan
values.job: For each step of my plan, protocol, checklist or workflow, say who should do it instead of me: a tool or my AIs, a tool after one tap, or only me for a reason only I can meet
values.description: Give steps (words, or { id, words, needs, only_a_person_because, given_in, past }) and doers (the caller's own list: { id, label, does: [words], tool_id?, cost?, spends?, reaches_others?, hand_off?, how? }), and optionally only_a_person (the reasons only the person can do a step), approved (doer ids the person already said yes to), past (outcomes { doer, result: met or failed }), words and ranking. For every step answers who (trillion, one-tap, you or nobody-yet), the doers that cover it with their cost and whether they need a tap, the needs nobody covers, and a sentence. A step is the person's only for a reason in only_a_person; a step nobody can do is nobody-yet, never a to-do; a reason the person gave once is not asked again when the step names the message that gave it; a reason with a first_try doer waits until that doer failed. Nothing is spent or sent. The doers and reasons are never built in.

values.title: Say who said each part of a recording
values.job: Name who said each stretch of a call or recording, from the voices of people who agreed to be known
values.description: Takes a recording and its transcript (the timed stretches tools/audio-transcription gives) and answers each turn with who said it: the person's name when one enrolled person is clearly the closest voice; every person it could be when two are too close to tell, so a guess is never made silently; otherwise an unknown voice with a number that stays the same for the whole listening, across every recording of it. Stretches of one voice are judged together, a stretch too short to measure takes its neighbour's voice, and turns of one voice a couple of seconds apart are joined. Thresholds, the wording of the labels and the gap that joins turns are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented clips. The voice-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: only the listening's listening-voices record is kept, with the numbers of the unknown voices heard, on this device. It names no one who has not enrolled.

values.title: Withdraw a referral code
values.job: Stop a referral code from earning, and give back the event to save
values.description: Gives back the event that, once saved, stops a referral code you made from earning. Only the account that made a code can withdraw it; a withdrawal from any other account is ignored when the events are read.

values.title: Take a person's results out of the pool
values.job: Remove every noisy result one person ever gave the pool when they stop sharing
values.description: Runs in the account that holds the pool. Removes every pooled results row whose id starts with the contributor's id, in writes of at most the engine's cap, and says how many were removed. The next answer is worked out from what is left, with new noise for the shards it changed.

values.title: Turn words into a picture vector
values.job: Turn words into the vector a picture model (CLIP ViT-B-32, OpenAI weights) gives pictures that show them, to compare with picture vectors kept for recordings
values.description: Encodes 1 to 64 short texts with the CLIP ViT-B-32 text model (OpenAI weights, ONNX export pinned by BLAKE3) and returns one unit-length 512-number vector per text, with the model named, so it is compared only with picture vectors made by the same model. Runs sealed, without the network.

values.title: Work one piece through a bank of questions, with evidence for every answer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a small set of the right questions about one thing I am making or reviewing, keep each answer with the files that show it, tell me when an answer's evidence has changed, and add what I learned to my library of findings
values.description: From a person's bank of questions and the run profile they name, picks a small routed set for one piece (a folder with a header listing its tags), writes the piece's investigation record, says which questions can be answered next, records each answer with the BLAKE3 identity of every evidence file (a missing file is refused, an unchanged file is not recorded twice), reports progress and which answers rest on evidence that has since changed or gone, and adds findings to the findings library. A recorded answer establishes structure and file identity, not that the answer is true. Everything about the bank, the profiles, the routes, the statuses and the finding kinds comes from the schema the person gives.

values.title: Work a session catalog
values.job: Offer my sessions in a catalog: publish an entry, read what is current, change it, withdraw it, replace it, or point it to a related offer
values.description: Works on catalog entries, each naming the groups that own it, the sessions it offers, a reference to the person's own visibility rule, a recommendation policy, related offers and where it is shown. An entry is current until it is superseded or retracted. Operations: publish (checks and tidies an entry), read (the current entries, optionally for given entry or session refs), update, retract (with a reason), supersede (an entry by a different one), cross_offer (point one entry at another, replacing an earlier pointer to the same target). Who may see an entry, and the order entries are recommended in, are the person's own rules and are not decided here. Nothing is saved.

values.title: Work out measures from my records
values.job: Work out measures from my records: counts, totals, ratios, ranks, quantiles, the latest value, groups, or a ranked and packed list
values.description: Takes facts (a list of records) and measure definitions, or a pipeline of stages where a later stage reads the rows an earlier stage emitted. Each definition names an op (count, sum, distinct, ratio, bin, band, rank, latest, quantile, angle, rollup, formula, reduce-graph, weighted-rank, derive-spans, constrained-span-pack, relevance-rank, mutual-overlap), the fact windows it reads (a match on fields and a field path) and the op's params. Answers each measure with its value, confidence, the ids of the facts it read and ok. An op that is not known, or that fails, gives ok false and confidence 0, never a made-up number. Nothing is named by the tool: the fields, bands, weights and words are in the definitions.

values.title: Work out referral codes
values.job: See which referral codes are live, which sales a code a buyer typed earns, what share it earns, and how many referrals an account has accepted
values.description: Reads the referral events a person saved (a code made, a code withdrawn, a signup that named a referrer) and works out the codes: who made each one, what it points at, and whether it is still live. The first account to make a code keeps it, in any order the events arrive; only the account that made a code can withdraw it. Give it the codes buyers typed and the sales, and it says for each pair which live code that is, whether the sale earns it (the sale attribute the code points at has the value the code names), and, when you give a share rule (the amount field and basis points), what the sale earns in whole cents. It reads and adds up only: it moves no money and sends nothing.

values.title: Work out unit economics
values.job: Work out a business's unit economics (ARPU, gross margin, CAC, LTV, LTV to CAC, payback) from one period's revenue, costs, ad spend and customer counts
values.description: Takes one period's numbers in whole cents and counts and returns revenue per customer, gross margin, cost to win a customer, lifetime value, lifetime value to acquisition cost and months (periods) to earn back that cost. A figure these numbers cannot give (no cost, no spend, no churn, a zero count) comes back as null, never as a made-up zero.

values.title: Work out where a learner stands on a track
values.job: See how far a learner is along a course, lesson plan or learning path, which step comes next, and what they last showed
values.description: Give the tracks, their ordered steps and the learner's progress states, evaluation receipts, evidence and label rows, and (to look at one person) the learner. Returns, per track, the steps in order, the percent finished counted from the steps (a stored percent or a "mastered" label never counts), the step to do next, the latest evaluation the learner's state names, the three newest pieces of evidence, the label for the latest decision and the path: each step complete, active or locked.

values.title: Turn a document into a message body (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a document I wrote (headings, paragraphs, images, a quoted reply) into the HTML and plain-text body of a message, ready to send
values.description: Takes a request file { document_nodes: [{ id, kind, props, children, visible }] or one root node, options? } and writes { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }. Text and heading kinds become paragraphs and headings with a plain-text line each; image and media blocks become inline_refs { cid, fetch_ref, mime } for the sender to attach; blocks marked as a quote become one blockquote with > lines; hidden subtrees are skipped; a block kind it does not know falls back to its text and is listed in degraded, never dropped silently. options.kind_renderers maps your own block kinds to paragraph, heading1 to heading3 or media. It names no mail provider.

values.title: Prepare the request for a profile of a creator or a topic
values.job: Turn what was gathered about a creator or a topic (video words, page text) into the instruction the person's AI writes a profile from
values.description: Give subject_ref (who or what is profiled), instruction (the person's own words on what to look for; they come before the material) and either material (one text) or evidence ([{ id, text }], for example one video's words each). Optional profile_ref (profile:<subject_ref> when left out) and output_kind (profile). Returns one request per piece of material: { kind, status requested, request_id (subject_ref:id), profile_ref, subject_ref, output_kind, instruction_text }, and in skipped the ids whose text was empty (a video with no captions). It asks no model and stores nothing; the AI that called it writes the profile from instruction_text and keeps it in the person's own records.

values.title: Write a web page from one record and a description of how to publish it (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn one record and a publication descriptor into a finished web page: its words, its address, its search and sharing tags, its structured data and a proof of what it was made from
values.description: Takes an envelope file: publication_descriptor, source_record, optional materialized_values and correlation_id. The descriptor says which record fields become the title, description, language and page sections (heading, paragraph, prose, list, quote, code, image, group; any other operation still shows its text), where the page will live (scheme, domain and path pieces, each a literal or a value read from the record), the colours and font (tokens), extra sharing tags, and a list of structured-data nodes whose values are read from the record, with empty values dropped. Words from the record are escaped; a prose section is written as given, so its owner must have made it safe. The new page is written to the output path. The answer gives the address, tags, byte count and a proof naming the descriptor, record and revision it came from.

values.title: Write legal documents
values.job: Write a business's terms of service, privacy policy, refund policy or waiver from its facts
values.description: Assembles each document you ask for from a library of forty clauses, choosing the clauses the business's facts call for (accounts, paid offers, subscriptions, AI, physical activity, minors) and filling in its name, address, contact and policies. Each document comes back with its text, its identity, the clauses used, the facts still missing or to be confirmed, and whether it is ready to publish; nothing is ready to publish until a lawyer has reviewed it. facts_it_reads lists every fact each document uses, so a first call with a few facts shows what to ask for next.
